Hola hola. Toda la gente creativa que da vida a esta comunidad un gusto volver a saludarlos. 

>Hello everyone! It's great to greet all the creative people who bring this community to life again. 

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/medicenbecky/23tRzahyKP49uw3XYpghH3qBV6Uoavd7ALNjJ51oXbucPxG5DdauaSJGTTqx2rCNf4AfY.png

Cómo saben me gusta estar inventando un poco jeje así que el día de hoy les mostrare como convertí la caja de una lavadora en un hermoso paral para la decoración de cumpleaños de mi hija., no queriamos hacer celebración debido a que nuestros familiares no están en este país, sola le íbamos a decorar su silla de comer colocar unos regalos y llevarla a un parque en la tarde. Pero a última hora decidimos hacerle un lindo compartir y que nos quedarán esas fotos de recuerdo de su primer y bendecido cumpleaños 

>As you know, I like to get creative a bit, hehe, so today I'll show you how I transformed a washing machine box into a beautiful stand for my daughter's birthday decorations. We didn't want to have a big celebration because our family isn't in this country; we were just going to decorate her high chair, put out some presents, and take her to a park in the afternoon. But at the last minute, we decided to have a nice get-together so we could have these photos to remember her first and blessed birthday.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/medicenbecky/23tRzahyKP49uw3XYpghH3qBV6Uoavd7ALNjJ51oXbucPxG5DdauaSJGTTqx2rCNf4AfY.png

No tome muchas fotos ya que estaba concentrada armando todo, el cumpleaños era un sábado y yo estaba un jueves como un pulpo, gracias a qué mi esposo me ayuda, lo primero que hice fue estirar el cartón y  cortar la parte de arriba con forma de semi circulo y colocar trozos del mismo en la parte donde estuviese doblado para estirarlo, cuando lo pare el cartón que le pegue no era suficiente se seguia doblando , así que decidió   pegar dos palos de cepillo y quedo súper firme 

>I didn't take many pictures because I was focused on putting everything together. The birthday was on a Saturday, and I was working like an octopus on a Thursday. Thankfully, my husband helps me. The first thing I did was stretch the cardboard and cut the top part into a semi-circle shape. I then placed pieces of cardboard on the folded part to stretch it out. When I stood it up, the cardboard I glued on wasn't enough; it kept folding. So, I decided to glue on two brush handles, and it became super sturdy.

![1000273482.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gene28/23tSayJsqNBL3rD2j2E6YQCSxQWaq42k6sL9UEeXLL1HT7YFMLrqMwxSt6PthnNezhHUb.jpg)

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/medicenbecky/23tRzahyKP49uw3XYpghH3qBV6Uoavd7ALNjJ51oXbucPxG5DdauaSJGTTqx2rCNf4AfY.png

Para las patas cortamos varias capas de cartón en forma de triangulo y lo pegamos una de otra , cuando estaba seca lo pegamos a nuestra base, lo paramos y quedó espectacular, ya me estaba gustando mucho 

>For the legs, we cut several layers of cardboard into triangles and glued them together. When it was dry, we glued it to our base, stood it up, and it looked spectacular. I was already really liking it.

![1000305220.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gene28/23yd8NN7MeXW3ESqHvU6gE4y1DEi4ZXqsUKy2eCxd4xSWmSzsrqkjaqCgRxZaDUf8Jkt2.jpg)

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/medicenbecky/23tRzahyKP49uw3XYpghH3qBV6Uoavd7ALNjJ51oXbucPxG5DdauaSJGTTqx2rCNf4AfY.png

Luego forramos todo con papel color fucsia la intención era dejar eso de fondo pero no nos gustó, nos pareció muy intenso el color   así que decidimos pegarle una cortina metalizada blanca y miren que bello se ve, todos me preguntaron si lo había alquilado 

>Then we covered everything with fuchsia-colored paper. The intention was to leave that as a background, but we didn't like it; the color seemed too intense. So we decided to glue on a white metallic curtain, and look at that!

![1000273985.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gene28/23yd8PRgj6RESnZfTG7WMtNqLoff9S4srDa46nLWkPbbWRaAwy8aaC8g6ud8CcJnw3Rw5.jpg)

![1000273987.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gene28/23tmUTEtiC7oZ9z3CehK7VuSqTRAyZSfCZJ5D25u1aWUPuH9YEmxQkbmcCP7zyj3LZy78.jpg)

![1000274257.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gene28/EoiWgaanViUqcVnSRCPig5CS5ftk26wuEmZiQ7hNAabh3M1aCpz5u5MmWtVVBR43KMa.jpg)

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/medicenbecky/23tRzahyKP49uw3XYpghH3qBV6Uoavd7ALNjJ51oXbucPxG5DdauaSJGTTqx2rCNf4AfY.png

El sábado en la mañana empecé a inflar los globos para hacer un semi arco y colocarlo de un lado del paral , también coloque el nombre de mi hija en el centro y otras decoraciones como una Minnie , un lazo de globo 

>On Saturday morning I started inflating the balloons to make a semi-arch and place it on one side of the pole. I also put my daughter's name in the center and other decorations like a Minnie Mouse and a balloon bow.

![1000274767.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gene28/23wX3hCQLg7QyeMFNgR3rVVAFefLMYGcLEmVr952VQZ4R9uRSTNHZjJNn3CYXYcpfjFg8.jpg)

Y este es el resultado final,  besos

body.title: The Yummiest Binignit I've Tasted : Children's Snacks for May Flores
body.body:
In our place, there's an event called *May Flores* where children are taught about God in local churches . After each sessions,snack are provided by the concern citizens, mostly members of the church. 

My mother suggested that my sister and I contribute to sponsoring the snacks the other day, so I bought the ingredients when I went back to the Mayor's Office. 

![IMG_20260523_193738.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emminemsss/23w347CSsdHeNomGfZ6Rrp2KpQVUA3TC3LAtsFXZdxdNMethggkhobqmkwvadSQTFHGsJ.jpg)
> This is the *malagkit rice* that I took to the milling place to have it ground into powder. 

I added water to the rice little by little until it reached the right consistency- make sure not to add too much water. My mother taught me first, and I followed what she did. She made small circles called *bilo-bilo*. She told me to put some of the malagkit rice powder in another container and coat the small circles so they wouldn't stick to each other. 


![IMG_20260523_204713.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emminemsss/23z7Wq88W5ooWkBj2f8oo53BBKb7NJD8j826SuTW2X8DWoh4a6PcCLBm75yFx5H9p68Cu.jpg)
I didn't buy bisol because there's a lot at home. *Binignit* will be so much better with lots of bisol. My sister planted a lot of it, so we can cook it whenever we want, for whatever dish. 

My mother told me to cut the bisol into smaller pieces so it will dissolve in the soup and become sticky. 

![IMG_20260523_205111.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emminemsss/23zkxoVHghza7QEgVC3rMUBKhhafdcxuSvxHH6DyRsBdovEQHS5APEhFcUmkLL2nw66x2.jpg)
> My favorite ingredients of all are the sweet potatoes. 

I then cut the sweet potatoes (camote) into cubes slightly bigger than the bisol. 

![IMG_20260523_205847.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emminemsss/23ynYkZLezxSSmdJb6zic8SDpngiALWzu9kfSsFPnoxtdc7fvb97BLW9VLQCeDxZdXesj.jpg)
> Bananas, kamoteng kahoy, and rice 

I cut the half of *kamoteng kahoy* to the same size as the sweet potatoes, and used the other half to make bilo-bilo. I also cut the bananas into smaller pieces, and prepared the rice as my mother instructed. 

![IMG_20260523_211158.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emminemsss/23y96ZCKoPgLxFonFVutUTnBQ115dcWic8jPzWcQiKwHbEBnTgFgo7vKpYcoUsNnPDPRH.jpg)
> Last were the sagu and coconut. 🥥 

I boiled the bigger sago the night before cooking *binignit* because it will took a long time to soften it. 

The hardest part, and the one that required the most of effort, was the coconut. I peeled off the *bunot*. I used four pieces of coconut and grated them . Luckily, my father helped me when only two were left. Making coconut milk is tiring, and my mother was rushing me because everything else was soft and only the coconut milk wasn't ready yet. 

![IMG_20260523_211525.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emminemsss/EpEKeaUqqXhqubB9jR5Quxf15VyDp2VBueGC81ffs5bcK4FEDNJQB1qKGV6gp9zXf2f.jpg)
> I almost forgot to mention that I added ube powder to make it look more colorful and delectable. 

*Pro tip: add a pinch of salt to balance the taste*. 

Finally, our binignit was ready to serve. My mother packed it in ice wrappers for easy delivery to the church. It was no hassle for my brother, who was carrying it, since he will be teaching the kids.  

---
**Ingredients for *binignit***:

- *powdered malagkit rice*
- *ordinary rice*
- *bisol*
- *sweet potatoes or camote*
- *bananas* 
- *kamoteng kahoy* 
- *coconut milk*
- *big and small size sago*
- *sugar*
- *ube powder* 

---
***Procedure:***

- **Prepare** all the ingredients, including *bilo-bilo* and cooked sago. 
- **Boil** water in a pot. 
- **Add** the *bilo-bilo* and small sago. 
- **Add** the rice and bisol, and cook until tender. 
- **Add** the sweet potatoes, *kamoteng kahoy*, and the cooked sago. 
- **Add** the bananas and sugar. 
- **Check** if everything is tender, then taste. 
- **Lastly, add** the coconut milk. Your *binignit* is now ready to serve. 

*Pro tip: Make sure to stir well, or it may stick to the pot*. 

---
This ends my blog. Thanks for reading! Love lots. 😘

--emmin◉⁠‿⁠◉msss

body.title: Andrés and Andrea's Journey Toward Confirmation [ENG-ESP]
body.body:
> Hello, dear mothers and fathers of Motherhood! It’s been a while since I’ve stopped by to share with you. My children are growing up every day; their days are filled with a pretty hectic routine between high school and baseball (by the way, a new championship is coming up very soon, but I’ll tell you more about that in an upcoming post). Today I want to open my heart to you about a very beautiful and spiritual phase we’re experiencing at home: my two children are currently taking the course to receive the sacrament of Confirmation. ![20230317_070722_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/23ydTXWXufPZ1Hu18eVGXcqx5oxZHgRkqLBy31mKdqTufgJvB6fPSM9kr1zRZdyHn4P9r.png) >¡Hola, queridas madres y padres de Motherhood! Tenía ya un tiempo sin pasar por aquí a compartir con ustedes. Mis hijos cada día están más grandes; sus días transcurren en una rutina bastante movida entre el liceo y el béisbol (por cierto, se viene un nuevo campeonato muy pronto, pero de eso les contaré en un próximo post). >Hoy quiero abrirles mi corazón sobre una etapa muy bonita y espiritual que estamos viviendo en casa: mis dos hijos se encuentran realizando el curso para recibir el sacramento de la Confirmación.
![1001596022.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/EpXJRZ1GcWPbyoci4rWv42tZMbM9rkPfvEnvREJxXWFt7wc9AQr6rZWtgHE74Gx5kU9.jpg)
We’re a Catholic family. Andrés, our oldest, made his First Communion when he was 9. With Andrea, however, things were different; time just slipped by, and when she turned 12, she didn’t want to sign up for catechism class. She felt much older than the other kids in the class, who were much younger than her, and she felt self-conscious. As a mom, I decided not to pressure her and to wait for a better time. And that time finally came. Andrés is now 16, and Andrea is almost a month away from turning 14. Interestingly, to receive Confirmation, the Church requires that you be at least 14 years old. Since Andrea hadn’t yet received her First Communion, I spoke with the parish catechist. I suggested that she prepare for both sacraments at the same time, explaining my strong desire for her to receive Confirmation alongside her older brother. The catechist agreed with great empathy, since the course lasts a full year and by the time of the ceremony, Andrea will have reached the required age. ![20230317_070722_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/23ydTXWXufPZ1Hu18eVGXcqx5oxZHgRkqLBy31mKdqTufgJvB6fPSM9kr1zRZdyHn4P9r.png) >En casa somos católicos. Andrés, el mayor, hizo su Primera Comunión cuando tenía 9 años. Sin embargo, con Andrea las cosas fueron diferentes; el tiempo se nos fue pasando y, cuando cumplió los 12 años, no quiso inscribirse en la catequesis. Se sentía muy grande en comparación con los niños del curso, que eran mucho más pequeños que ella, y le daba pena. Como mamá, decidí no presionarla y esperar un mejor momento. >Y ese momento, por fin, llegó. Actualmente Andrés ya tiene 16 años y Andrea está a casi un mes de cumplir los 14. Curiosamente, para poder recibir la Confirmación, la iglesia pide como requisito tener los 14 años cumplidos. >Como a Andrea le faltaba su Primera Comunión, conversé con la catequista de la parroquia. Le propuse que realizara la preparación para ambos sacramentos a la vez, explicándole mi gran deseo de que hiciera la Confirmación junto a su hermano mayor. La catequista aceptó con mucha empatía, ya que el curso dura un año entero y para el momento de la ceremonia Andrea ya tendrá la edad requerida. ![1001596077.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/23xyVGdCk3gvEatGdP8f2Dhp71y5uGk7q7YmyDYGRBCrV741hzMF5C84KECW6BgyVU8eW.jpg) A week ago, we attended a very meaningful Mass as part of Andrea’s journey toward her First Communion, known as the “Misa de paso.” This celebration symbolizes that the young people are moving on to the next stage in their preparation. During the Mass, they are given a white rosary, which they must carry with them from now on whenever they attend their catechism classes and Sunday Masses. On this occasion, Andrea had the opportunity to share the Mass with the youngest children in the community. Although at first I feared she might feel uncomfortable due to the age difference, fortunately she wasn’t alone: two other boys in her Confirmation group are also receiving their First Communion. So she was in good company and supported by young people her own age. ![20230317_070722_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/23ydTXWXufPZ1Hu18eVGXcqx5oxZHgRkqLBy31mKdqTufgJvB6fPSM9kr1zRZdyHn4P9r.png) >Hace una semana asistimos a una eucaristía muy significativa dentro del camino de Andrea hacia su comunión, llamada “Misa de paso”. Esta celebración simboliza que los jóvenes avanzan a un siguiente nivel en su preparación. Durante la misa, se les hace entrega de un rosario blanco, el cual deben llevar con ellos de ahora en adelante cada vez que asistan a sus clases de catecismo y a las eucaristías dominicales. >En esta ocasión, a Andrea le tocó compartir la misa con los niños más pequeños de la comunidad. Aunque al principio temía que se sintiera incómoda por la diferencia de edad, afortunadamente no estuvo sola: dos chicos más que están en su mismo grupo de Confirmación también deben hacer la Comunión primero. Así que estuvo muy bien acompañada y arropada por jóvenes de su edad.
![1001596237.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/EpLgsM7aTV8UqSjkkmpVF1zJWjkuJfk3UMiVK4buPz6ybqMqoyJ8mUgfabn3x8pdLyn.jpg)
Seeing my two children happy with their catechism classes is a blessing. They’ve made new friends, spend time with young people who share their values, and attend church with great enthusiasm. I am well aware that these days many people prefer to stay away from religion or the church. However, personally, I feel extremely at ease and at peace having returned to the church, and above all, it fills me with pride to see that my teenage children are happy to be part of such a wonderful community. ![20230317_070722_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/23ydTXWXufPZ1Hu18eVGXcqx5oxZHgRkqLBy31mKdqTufgJvB6fPSM9kr1zRZdyHn4P9r.png) >Ver a mis dos hijos contentos con sus catequesis es una bendición. Han hecho nuevos amigos, comparten con jóvenes que tienen sus mismos valores y asisten a la iglesia con muchísimo gusto. >Sé perfectamente que en la actualidad muchas personas prefieren mantenerse alejadas de las religiones o de la iglesia. Sin embargo, en lo personal, me siento sumamente a gusto y en paz por haber vuelto a la iglesia, y sobre todo, me llena de orgullo ver que mis hijos adolescentes se sienten felices de formar parte de una comunidad tan bonita.
![1001633437.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beysyd/23z7HdejFxgghq8ayXLbresE7nsJMBP7PuRzNBm6fripgJXscmhwzfYWVxaYhSwT56njK.jpg)

body.title: It was a good Monday!
body.body:
Just imagine, I said it was a good Monday!
It was an awesome day.
I stayed up at the trailer last night by myself, my friend that camps next door to us, stayed up also. 
It was just the two of us at the trailer park!
We had a nice fire in the fire pit, and had a nice chat.
Poor Cyril worked hard on Saturday and Sunday switching things from his old trailer to his new one. 
His wife Roxanne didn't get up this weekend, but I am sure she will be happy with all the hard work he done.
They will certainly enjoy their new trailer this weekend coming up!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cathyarrow/23wCEJ4ui7Yoyhzt2teMakFsVQ2rjLqprqZD8jt27iB7pSWQGPKtYaUmcUE8piLNQsJQi.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cathyarrow/23wqik5MFU5hTNs3vTLYKNghAPSjNDKYtzZUXotWD8VdasQ5okBZehbZ7DSbpkPAr3bwo.png)
Chase sure missed Alyssa!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cathyarrow/243fffMTpHqfAfh9fu2SQgHALbxnwCL3wEjaUU1xfLCu4RegKExro1wPk727cfgKMGJn6.png)
Their trailer getting put in its spot!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cathyarrow/242Y9htDzGJNp4w7NYCQHQpGyusf8ULAbhnQgiHdyqkZnqvXUYdQDECf9ZMJkcrqFRPb9.png)
My Aunt Greta in the green jacket and my best friend, Jackie in the pink hoodie, Chase loves Aunt Jackie!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cathyarrow/23vsJAGw98qKuUDqhdLyNVBSLKDjYbRQTdbx9SvLTh92Bhi3o1oAYtCmxFhb5M2hWTtK3.png)
Some cute puppy!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cathyarrow/23uQnVK48kzKkJ348YWqNPbQfZEFvtGChELdbaXGabdwVaz1MFXmKhvyaS2UQ5LMtr3yh.png)
Last nights fire!

I sure did miss @bradleyarrow and Chase last night, having them there fills my heart with joy!
We will surely have plenty of camping time together, making memories that money can't buy.

Having someone in your life that enjoys the same things you do is amazing.
I never thought Bradley would enjoy camping and not in a million years did I ever expect to be blogging. 
I didn't have a clue what Bradley was talking about when he explained to me what he was doing.
Hive, BBH foundation, PeakD, crypto, you get the drift, I said to myself, \

I have learned some things, I am eager to learn more.
I love blogging and reading others blogs.
I want to read everyone's blogs that follow me but, that will take some time, I am so busy.
But it will come with time.

I really missed blogging when I was up at the trailer. 
I had my computer with me, but every time I turned around someone was popping in for a visit!
I didn't have time to think.
I love that I get to see my family more and catch up with my childhood friends!

Remember to support the BBH Foundation!
We want to help others, but we can not do it without your donations!

Good night, God Bless🙏
Life is good!❤️

body.title: MSS communication strategy
body.body:
![0BE6A0E3-B64E-42EC-8CD7-690495A0A8B8.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dwayne16/23wgFYyFVZefaxcXUoVhLUCQ5verFjp6KGwkTpMNWT51A7fDzJhJ5bU7eNryHYpFSsDFg.jpeg)
***
# Communication Strategy Used by the Disciplinary Committee, MSS

## 1. Highlight the Current Communication Strategy Used

The disciplinary committee, MSS uses the One-way Asymmetrical communication strategy. This communication strategy is used because:

### • Authority is prioritized:

As much as the students can defend themselves, we found out that authority is a huge factor of the committee. There is a need to maintain respect from the students to the MSS.

### • Rules are imposed:

The students do not have a choice whether to obey the rules or not. They are obligated to act according to the rules set by the MSS which is vested in the handbook to create order in the Covenant University environment.

### • Student input is minimal:

Though students can provide feedback during hearings, we found out that the input of student is not as much as it would be in a two- way communication system. The students have to follow the rules duly and go through the disciplinary process before they can give their take on issues or matters of the university.

## Communication Channels Used

### • Formal:

Most of the channels listed above are formal, and are well structured and we found out that this is due to the need for documentation.

### • Authority Driven:

These channels used are ones used to bring about a level of authority.

### • Structure:

The use of mostly formal channels has brought about structure to the communication strategy used by the committee.

The strategy focuses on enforcing rules and maintaining discipline rater than promoting two-way dialogue or participatory communication.

---

# 2. Name the Communication Strategy

The communication strategy used is the One-way Asymmetrical Model developed from the Two-way Symmetrical Model developed by James Grunig and Todd Hunt.

The strategy is characterized by:

### • Communication flowing from the authority (MSS) to the audience which in this case is the Covenant University students.

### • The main goal is persuasion and control.

### • There is limited or controlled feedback from the audience.

In this context or scenario, the disciplinary committee, MSS uses this strategy to enforce rules and policies rather than mutual understanding in the initial stage. Mutual understanding is only thought of or enforced when the rules are broken or during disciplinary hearing.

---

# 3. Measure the Effectiveness of the Communication Strategy

To measure the effectiveness of the communication strategy in this context, the following were considered:

## 1. Compliance role:

A staff of MSS let us know that there has been 70% of students comply to the rules and codes of conduct of the university. Only a few percentages of students don’t comply by the rules and actually put in their ‘A’ game.

## 2. Speed of behavioral compliance:

When students have been given a warning letter or they have been given some form of punishment, we found out that the students do not repeat the same act of misconduct.

## 3. Student Perception:

We also found out that students believe the MSS is a ‘scary’ institution and most students do not want to associate with them. They believe the committee is not welcoming and this has been due to the laws that have been imposed and how they have been communicated. The communication strategy being used has brought about a disassociation with the university with the committee, MSS. According to the survey, the students believe the MSS communication strategy is effective to some extent.

## 4. Institutional Stability:

The communication strategy used by the university has brought about a level of stability. Due to the fear they have for the MSS, the students comply by the rules and do accordingly what they are expected to do.

---

# Overall Evaluation

# <center><u>**💚🌟PEACE BE UPON YOU ALL💚🌟**</u></center>

<center><u>**Welcome Back to @alive.chat Monday Challenge. Let’s share our goals, track our progress, and support each other.**</u></center>

<center>

<center>

You already know the purpose of this activity is simple: to share our goals, share our progress, and try to support each other in achieving them.

Everyone has goals, and the journey is not always easy. Here, we can motivate one another, learn from each other, and grow together. There is no pressure, just honest sharing, encouragement, and positive energy.

Feel free to share your goals, update your progress, and engage with others because when we support one another, success becomes more achievable for all.

<center>**<u>We are alive, we are growing, and we are moving forward together. 💪✨</u>**</center>

<center>![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SiJNYXS5WrkQGHwUTqc8ovYW5dnPFQJstbWui91WWNjsSipwyPyZ5ZEqXFc6gRK.jpg)</center>

# <center><u>**Challenge Task and Rules.**</u></center> 

<center>**<u>Kindly read the rules before participating in the challenge activity. You must follow all the rules mentioned below to be eligible for the Prizes.</u>**</center>

1. To be eligible, each participant must **<u>share their weekly, monthly, or yearly goals (whether posted or not) in the comments section, along with their progress during the week.</u>**

2. **<u>Sharing your weekly progress is an important part of this activity.</u>**
Please remember to include your progress along with your goals; without it, your entry won’t be eligible for the challenge.   
This requirement does not apply to first-time participants only.

3. <u>**Increased the time duration:**</u> This challenge will remain open for **<u>more than 48 hours, until Wednesday at 11:59 PM UTC</u>**.

body.title: #MyHiveGoals week #19: Checking my progress on my Hive/HP and HBD goals while organizing my desk in the Lab! [Eng/Esp]
body.body:
> Greetings, community, and happy start to the week! Hoping you're starting your day full of energy and in the best mood, I'm here to share my usual #MyHiveGoals report! In it, I summarize our activity and output from last week, and I was pleasantly surprised to see how productive it was. I've been finishing the last corrections my advisor sent me on my paper, and I've spent the last two weeks fine-tuning the details. I think I'll have it ready this week. Ironically, even though it seems like I have more time, I have to organize my desk in the lab. It's full of scientific articles, manuals, and lab protocols that I spent hours reading to finish my thesis discussion. Now I have to tidy up my desk to dedicate myself to the next phase of my professional career: applying for my first research project. ---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQoMtNS7e6G34e2omNb3XA4QAiAUCUoNzku7ioQbxwq2y/image.png) Link: [livecoinwatch](https://www.livecoinwatch.com/price/Hive-HIVE)

> The first big news I saw while brewing my coffee was that the price of Hive had recovered! $0.065 was the price I used to exchange all the liquid Hive from all my weekly rewards (remember that due to the low price of Hive, we aren't receiving HBD). It was depressing last week to see the price of Hive at $0.058 after almost reaching $0.09, although with the current circumstances, it only takes one geopolitical event for everything to collapse. Let's hope that this week we can overcome this fragile state in the crypto market.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/Eo4Ab6YHDAqaRVh7pHakA5AGvkNLYU7VLBS8c1rk9qDwzndFTYaNHBV8B4vRG9gDDam.png)
# Hive/HP

> We haven't funded our wallet on Hive yet; I think that will be towards the end of this month. However, that hasn't stopped us from continuing to do the daily power-ups. We're on track to complete the 5th Hive Power Up Month, which, added to this week's rewards, has generated a total of 125 HP, which we add to our influence within the network. This is what surprised me, because I thought I would generate less since I was busy with my academic and teaching activities, and this week will be the same, tomorrow I will start giving practical classes in the laboratory so I don't know if I will get out early enough to get online. ---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdXX6umzY8TrcxZFGbS3bma8NKHbGeBdnKfHRzG9D7DZz/image.png)

> But overall, we're on the right track. We'll probably reach 10,000 HP sometime this week, and in June we'll formally begin working towards our annual goal of 12,000 HP. It would take six months of network activity to reach that amount, so I think it's perfectly achievable. ---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUW2z8ja4yh4ami7nVZBQdSfiYp2o7mkoEAhyfL877uHg/image.png)|![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNpNwB22C14t7CrdEXWpKQ3MYuHQ672qXy4x1qofag429/image.png) --|-- Link: [hivestats](https://hivestats.io/)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tbkj8mbMn9CYGJL7qVH3Zzq9mBSpZMLFAwUuy9ggaZ1KBkyRJwKGLVu3gb6pfH3bZUd.png)
# HBD Savings

> The next metric we'll review is our HBD savings. In our previous post, we celebrated reaching 2,000 HBD after two years of deciding to explore the potential of this savings tool within the blockchain, through the HBD stablecoin (Hive-backed dollar). My thoughts at this point, considering not only our progress but also the challenging state of the crypto market in general, are that the HBD savings tool remains an excellent way to save and generate returns. I say this because even with the APR at 12%, it's still worth investing in HBD. ---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQgkXjTw7PqwJKe7srF7mpG3RsYsJrmt2Q83jPrKAwCX7/image.png)

> This week we managed to generate 7,286 HBD. This was because I converted my liquid Hives to HBD right during this price recovery. A week ago, this would have been equivalent to 6 HBD, bringing our total to 2,008,236 HBD.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSGWf6Jt2WhA3qLASySnTdDq7RNt8cLeQSSpaCzPMGixY/image.png) --- ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPxyWm6MDkf5pUCfbdrEuSDdkHi4Uj97f6jRXA5yRWRWn/image.png)

> Compared to last week, when we started with 2,000 HBD, we've now taken our first step of 2,008.236 HBD toward our annual goal of 2,300 HBD. It's a challenging task considering Hive's low price and 12% APR, but I believe it's all about consistency and exploring other opportunities to connect with new Hive communities and reach more users. As long as we remain active and consistent on the platform, the rewards will follow.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tGyXZoWHqdFmZ3okUbJHeoVbbUXGqH9Q7Eq9XGt2nrFidVxjieoh8GH2HD5583firb5.png)

> Well, friends, that's all for my weekly report on my Hive goals. I just wanted to mention that HBD I've earned in my wallet. In my previous post, I mentioned my interest in investing some of my HBD in second-layer and NFT projects, but recently Hive Engine was apparently compromised, and one of the consequences was that Rising Star, one of my favorite NFT games, will have to rethink its future. This led me to decide not to spend my HBD and to hold onto it until things are back to normal with Hive Engine. Until then, I just want to wish you a productive week and good health. See you soon, friends! ---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYGMg3RHm63sYKwXtb64GCkKjkXEuKMxNwcJUNyRZEcGx/front_mhgw19.jpg)

> ¡Saludos, comunidad, y feliz inicio de semana! Espero que comiencen el día con energía y de buen humor. ¡Aquí les comparto mi informe habitual de #MyHiveGoals! En él, resumo nuestra actividad y producción de la semana pasada, y me sorprendió gratamente lo productiva que fue. He estado terminando las últimas correcciones que mi asesor me envió para mi trabajo y he dedicado las últimas dos semanas a perfeccionar los detalles. Creo que lo tendré listo esta semana. Irónicamente, aunque parece que tengo más tiempo, tengo que organizar mi escritorio en el laboratorio. Está lleno de artículos científicos, manuales y protocolos de laboratorio que leí durante horas para terminar la defensa de mi tesis. Ahora tengo que ordenar mi escritorio para dedicarme a la siguiente etapa de mi carrera profesional: solicitar mi primer proyecto de investigación. ---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQoMtNS7e6G34e2omNb3XA4QAiAUCUoNzku7ioQbxwq2y/image.png) Link: [livecoinwatch](https://www.livecoinwatch.com/price/Hive-HIVE)

> La primera gran noticia que vi mientras preparaba mi café fue que el precio de Hive se había recuperado. ¡Usé $0.065 para intercambiar todo el Hive líquido de mis recompensas semanales (recuerden que, debido al bajo precio de Hive, no estamos recibiendo HBD)! Fue desalentador la semana pasada ver el precio de Hive en $0.058 después de casi alcanzar los $0.09, aunque con las circunstancias actuales, basta un solo evento geopolítico para que todo se derrumbe. Esperemos que esta semana podamos superar esta frágil situación en el mercado de criptomonedas.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/Eo4Ab6YHDAqaRVh7pHakA5AGvkNLYU7VLBS8c1rk9qDwzndFTYaNHBV8B4vRG9gDDam.png)
# Hive/HP

> Aún no hemos recargado nuestra billetera en Hive; creo que lo haremos hacia finales de este mes. Sin embargo, eso no nos ha impedido continuar con las recargas diarias. Estamos en camino de completar el 5.º Mes de Recargas de Hive, que, sumado a las recompensas de esta semana, ha generado un total de 125 HP, que añadimos a nuestra influencia dentro de la red. Esto me sorprendió, porque pensé que generaría menos, ya que estaba ocupado con mis actividades académicas y docentes, y esta semana será igual: mañana empiezo a dar clases prácticas en el laboratorio, así que no sé si podré salir lo suficientemente temprano para conectarme. ---

body.body: Lasca**, un músico de oficio cuya huella en el bajo, la composición y la producción ha sido vital para el sonido del pop-rock venezolano.

Lasca**, a craftsman musician whose mark on bass, songwriting, and production has been vital to the sound of Venezuelan pop-rock. ---  
[English version below!](#contenido-english)
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/musicavenezuela/AJeayd7puGynPwGiQH5DfFG9tqCKAi21u45JovVgQ99Djgf6ktKWj6eoqu5sGRR.png) # Lasca: El oficio musical entre el bajo y la producción

>\n\nLa carrera de **David Lasca**, conocido en el medio artístico simplemente como **Lasca** o bajo su eterno apodo de **Chapis**, es un ejemplo de constancia y oficio dentro de la escena musical en **Venezuela**. Aunque nació en **México**, su vida y su obra se desarrollaron en territorio venezolano. El sobrenombre de **Chapis** es una herencia directa de su país de nacimiento, siendo un diminutivo de \

por ser el menor de sus hermanos; una expresión muy mexicana que se le quedó grabada al mudarse y que se convirtió en su identidad personal en la movida de **Caracas**.

Su formación es profunda, habiendo estudiado con maestros fundamentales como **Gerry Weil**, **Gustavo Carucí** y **Albin Zapata**. Antes de los grandes escenarios, **Chapis** pasó varios años curtiéndose en la movida nocturna caraqueña, tocando en fiestas y restaurantes de la ciudad. Este bagaje en los locales nocturnos fue fundamental para desarrollar su versatilidad y dominio del instrumento en vivo. En 1996, se integró como bajista a **Los Cañoneros**, agrupación fundamental para mantener vivo el sonido festivo, rítmico y urbano de la **Caracas** de principios del siglo XX. Ya para esa época, su inquietud creativa lo llevó a grabar un EP con canciones propias; aunque ese proyecto no consiguió en su momento el apoyo de una compañía discográfica, dejó constancia de su temprano interés por desarrollar una propuesta personal más allá de las bandas comerciales.

Sin embargo, su nombre se hizo familiar para el gran público a partir de 1998, cuando cofundó la banda **Malanga**. En este grupo, **Chapis** no solo ejecutó el bajo, sino que fue pieza esencial como coautor de los temas que posicionaron a la banda en la radio nacional e internacional. Paralelo a esto, su curiosidad por el estudio lo llevó al campo de la producción, destacando su labor en el primer disco de **La Vida Bohème**, una producción que alcanzó nominaciones al **Grammy** y refrescó el sonido de la escena alternativa.

Como solista, su propuesta bajo el nombre de **Lasca** ofrece un matiz más personal. En 2010 presentó su primer álbum, **\
**, trabajo que puso a disposición de sus seguidores en la red. Años más tarde, en 2017, lanzó su segunda placa titulada **\

** (**Cero**), reafirmando una búsqueda sonora propia y alejada de las fórmulas convencionales. Un elemento distintivo de esta etapa es la cuidada estética de sus videos, realizados por su hermano, el cineasta **Vadim Lasca**, logrando una sinergia familiar que ha dado como resultado piezas audiovisuales de alto nivel artístico.

### Lasca: Musical Craftsmanship Between Bass and Production

The career of **David Lasca**, known in the artistic world simply as **Lasca** or by his eternal nickname **Chapis**, is an example of perseverance and craftsmanship within the musical scene in **Venezuela**. Although he was born in **Mexico**, his life and work developed in Venezuelan territory. The nickname **Chapis** is a direct heritage from his birth country, being a diminutive of \

(short) for being the youngest of his brothers; a very Mexican expression that stuck with him when he moved and became his personal identity in the **Caracas** scene.

His training is deep, having studied with fundamental teachers such as **Gerry Weil**, **Gustavo Carucí**, and **Albin Zapata**. Before the big stages, **Chapis** spent several years honing his skills in the Caracas nightlife, playing at parties and restaurants in the city. This background in night venues was fundamental to developing his versatility and mastery of the instrument live. In 1996, he joined **Los Cañoneros** as a bassist, a key group for keeping alive the festive, rhythmic, and urban sound of early 20th-century **Caracas**. By that time, his creative restlessness led him to record an EP with his own songs; although that project did not get the support of a record company at the time, it left evidence of his early interest in developing a personal proposal beyond commercial bands.

However, his name became familiar to the general public starting in 1998, when he co-founded the band **Malanga**. In this group, **Chapis** not only played the bass but was also an essential piece as a co-author of the songs that positioned the band on national and international radio. Parallel to this, his curiosity for the studio led him to the field of production, highlighting his work on the first album by **La Vida Bohème**, a production that reached **Grammy** nominations and refreshed the sound of the alternative scene.

As a soloist, his proposal under the name **Lasca** offers a more personal nuance. In 2010 he presented his first album, **\
**, a work he made available to his followers online. Years later, in 2017, he released his second record titled **\

** (**Zero**), reaffirming a sound search of his own, away from conventional formulas. A distinctive element of this stage is the careful aesthetics of his videos, mostly made by his brother, the filmmaker **Vadim Lasca**, achieving a family synergy that has resulted in high-level artistic audiovisual pieces. #

body.title: TO ANYONE WHO FEELS BEHIND IN LIFE RIGHT NOW
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme5faP8Cyu5Sd5FYjWQCm32HSmu2mXuZvBJ5cJp5R5BUf/1779746528914.png)


I need to say this to someone today: 

You are not behind. You are not late. You are not failing.

Life isn’t a race with a single finish line. Some people build careers in their 20s. Some find peace in their 40s. Some lose everything and start over at 50 and end up happier than ever. There’s no universal timeline, only your timeline.

I know it’s easy to look around and feel like everyone else has it figured out. The curated posts, the “announcing my new job” updates, the couples, the houses, the milestones. It makes your own quiet progress feel invisible.

But here’s the truth: growth happens in the unseen moments.
- The days you choose not to quit even when you feel tired.
- The nights you remind yourself to keep going when no one is clapping.
- The small choices to be kind, to learn, to try again after failing.

That’s real progress. That’s the kind that actually lasts.



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQZfHqDAx1GwBCSCJbkToMeVzsyt7KHi8wcj2HPNu9Si1/1779746596193.jpg)



If you’re in a season where things feel slow, messy, or uncertain — that’s okay. Seasons change. The road you’re walking right now is building resilience, wisdom, and strength you’ll need later. One day you’ll look back and understand why it had to be this way.

So take a breath. You’re doing better than you think.

If this found you at the right time, what’s one thing you’re proud of yourself for lately, even if it feels small? Drop it below. Let’s remind each other that progress counts, no matter how quiet it is.

body.title: Character Over Cleverness: The True Foundation of Leadership
body.body:
<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcYUVgoiFKZ2egnx2uFGpjM5WzF3rwWQFtXvu1MAbdNQU/17797467161122687857331579322760.jpg 
[Source](https://www.facebook.com/groups/427696355197727/posts/1170034957630526/)</center>

Leadership is a potent combination of strategy and character, so if you must be one, you mustn't be without a strategy. When you look at it at first, this statement might look sometimes counterintuitive. In this part of the world that is obsessed with optimization, metrics and tactical precision, we celebrate those who can forecast trends and predict the future over those who can put strategies in place.

We have come to see those who outmaneuver competitors and execute flawless plans as being the lord of our all. Strategy is visible, it is measurable and immediate results are produced by it. Character on the other hand is a little bit quiet and it reveals itself over time and is consistent too.

In decision making under pressure, in how power is being used and how people are being treated when there is nothing to gain, it does not always produce quick wins but it shapes lasting impact. The truth is, strategy without character is dangerous. When people have a lot of strategy but there is no good character that brings people across board, that's a very dangerous thing.

A leader with a sharp strategy but weak character can still achieve success but at a cost. Ethical corners might be salvaged because of this and sacrifices of people for the outcome might be done. System might be manipulated because of personal gain and in short time, all this might look a little bit effective but in the long term, trust is eroding away, culture is being damaged, fragile system is the only thing that is left on the table and these two can collapse without control.

History and business alike are filled with people of leadership characters who are strategically brilliantly and more compromised. Though these people's rise were fast, their influence was wide, the likes of Barack Obama, Nelson Mandela and the likes of Martin Luther King Jr. and many more. They are often tarnished, sometimes by destructive.

When you look at it at the other spectrum, through a leader with a strong character but imperfect strategy operates differently. They may not always make the smartest tactical move, they misjudge timing and look at things differently, but they build trust, that is one thing you can't take away from them. They create environments where people feel valued, heard and well respected.

They foster the resilience and make sure that things are done right and things are done well. We've already learned that strategy can be learned and it can be passed across from one person to the other. Character takes time and is a little bit hard, it can also break in a day and takes years to build up, that is a crazy aspect of character that many people don't even know.

A leader who is grounded in integrity, humility and accountability will develop a strategy that many people are going to fall in love with as time goes on and they will surely listen to this kind of leader, they will adapt and improve on what he has said. People will support this kind of leader, not because they are perfect, nobody is looking for perfection, but because they see trustworthiness, trustworthiness is like a magnet that when you have it, people want to associate with you because they know that they can trust their life, their money, their business with you on it. In practical terms, this has challenged that character over time brings more and better reward than having a lot of people underneath you who cannot even trust you with their life.



Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@timscreative/character-over-cleverness-the-true-foundation-of-leadership-7sz)

body.title: Sell the experience not the subscription
body.body:
![278451.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23tRxo5vFHH3Pb2btiWg2voP5UZRkLevzxo6LtvDKqH2Gh4EFSWgsKw3uJ7FwK8xkkD9o.jpg)



<hr>

Some days back I got a canva pro offer by entering a coupon. I got this pro for 3 months and I was ecstatic, I think a lot of people value canva, but don't think it's valuable enough for anyone to pay for a yearly or monthly subscription, I'm one of those people. 


Although I like it. I've been using it for years now, and I enjoy it, but it doesn't really major a lot as a main tool for content creation. After getting that 3 months free trial coupon, I was elated, used the AI agents for a few days and it was amazing and I designed cool stuffs but after like 5 days the pro trial was removed and I wondered why.

 This could have been a great experience and a reminder for users to actually renew their subs, the experience could get many people using canva again, but I guess the didn't happen. I'm not denying that the use experience has been great, I just wonder why they'd go back on their words of letting people use a free coupon for 3 months by enjoying the pro version of the app. 


It just reminds you of the fact that nothing is free anymore, every tool, app, interface or system is monetized, but a lot of app fail to understand that you need to still offer free, or a sort of free trial to people to enable them to use and decide if your app is worth paying for. 


The likes of **chatGPT** and **Claude** are currently doing this. Even capcut one of the best modern video editing tool that is also a huge \

experience is also doing it, and funny enough, capcut pro is even cheaper than canva. 

This is why I think canva has a very terrible marketing team. Their app (canva) is not a bulk or major editing tool app, and should have been cheaper too. 

Despite the fact that capcut is a main editing tool, it offers better value for money and because of that, most people has no choice but to subscribe to that for the bulk of their video editing. 

Perhaps canva is trying to charge more to make up for the lower number of people using them to other freer available option, but then, this itself is a very terrible idea. 


Claude for example is arguably the best AI models, it murders chatGPT and Gemini at almost everything and they still let's you have 5 to 6 free prompts daily.

 Infact the main flagship AI too is not divided into PRO and PRO+, you pay 25$ or thereabout *(can't remember)* and you can continue using the experience. Infact it's the only AI tool I can confidently pay for...

> why? 

I have seen the experience, it's breathtaking and worth every money. Infact it would get so better that it puts the like of chatGPT out of business, but this is another discussion for another day. 


### Conclusion 

The point is that people have to be comfortable with parting with their money and they have to be happy that they're actually doing it, they need to be eager, they have to dream of the experience and not the price they're paying. 


They need to wish they have the money to pay, and they need to place the experience above any price they need to pay, and this is exactly what the likes of Claude and caput have done: make the experience even far more memorable than the price. 


A lot of apps are like canva; placing the subscription fee over the the experience they're supposed to give their customers. This is a bad business models, especially since people would prefer to have an choose a cheaper alternative.

 If you're not the best in the business, then you have to business charging fees that makes people think of instant alternatives.

body.title: My Secret Life as a Garden Gnome (a flash fiction story)
body.body:
Sometimes, an idea is more than an idea. A story is more than a story. Today, I’m sharing a flash fiction story I wrote a while back (as in a few years). I’ve read it publicly. I haven’t published it. But today, that changes.

Introducing …

## **My Secret Life as a Garden Gnome**

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!b1Qf!,w_1456,c_limit,f_webp,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb66191aa-6dca-40fb-975b-94732b3f0f82_1536x1024.png) 

It started as an ailment to curiosity.

I was walking home from school one spring day when I saw a statue of a little bearded man standing happily in Mrs. Crenshaw’s garden. He stood there in an unmoving, unflinching happy pose. Wondering how it would feel, I slid gracefully into the garden and stood beside him, doing my best to mimic his contentedness with a version of my own.

It was a five-minute jaunt. No more. Harmless.

When I stepped out of the garden I felt a rush unlike any feeling I’d ever felt. I looked around to see if anyone had noticed me. No one had.

Taking my path again, I made my way home, quickening my pace so as not to arouse any suspicions from Mother regarding my tardiness. When nothing came of my indiscretion, I felt relieved. A full week passed before I tried it again.

The rain felt as good as the sunshine. Mrs. Crenshaw was not one of those 1950s women who stayed home and kept house. She was more like those women who drove themselves daily to some downtown office to prove themselves as capable of joyful employment as any man. With no one home, I took advantage of the opportunity.

I stepped into Mrs. Crenshaw’s garden the second time and felt the soft ground sink beneath my overly shod feet. It had rained for most of the day. The drizzle at that moment made the adventure all the more exciting. The little man seemed as happy in the rain as he had been in the sun.

At first apprehensive about the weather, I assumed the most trance-like pose I could imagine and realized that I was living the best ten minutes of my life. The rain blasted my face and I felt like a new boy.

I soon found myself in Mrs. Crenshaw’s garden every day. Sometimes for a quick two-minute fix. Other times, I lingered for a full half hour. But I always managed to make it home in time for dinner. If my dalliances aroused Mother’s suspicions she never voiced any concerns.

It wasn’t long before my short daily stints as Mrs. Crenshaw’s garden gnome weren’t enough. I had to have more. I snuck out of the house one night impelled by an urge I could not control.

I waited until my parents went to bed. Then I quietly pulled myself from my comfort, traded pajamas for day clothes, and crept to Mrs. Crenshaw’s house in the dark. It was the most mood-enhancing three hours of my existence.

It then became my nightly compulsion to be the best garden gnome in the city. Mrs. Crenshaw’s wasn’t enough. I found myself taking different paths home from school every day to scout the locations of other gardens. At night, after my parents retired to sleep, I would make my way to a different address and personify myself as the resident garden gnome. I eventually did so without divesting myself of my pajamas.

At Old Man Johnson’s house, I got jealous. The permanent garden gnome didn’t like me being there. I set him on the front porch with his back toward me. It was the greatest pleasure I’d ever known. A whole garden all to myself for five straight hours.

I liked full moon nights best. The rays of hope upon my face made me the happiest garden gnome in any garden on any night. But I always enjoyed the scene under any unchangeable conditions.

It mattered not what plants, what fruit, what vegetables, what flora may have occupied a garden, or whose house, church, school, business, or government building hosted it. My life as a garden gnome was the most fulfilling it could have been. I was happiest when standing without movement under the moon and stars. But soon, that, too, became a monotonous chore. I searched for ways to make it more interesting, to bring back that waning exhilaration that once made my life complete.

I removed my pajamas, standing naked in whatever natural or unnatural light, if any, might be present.

I posed with cigarettes in my mouth. I stood with one leg raised. I sampled various poses—the sailor pose, the schoolboy pose, the hard worker pose, and poses which had no name. My life as a garden gnome brought me a whole new level of satisfaction. Even then, I would eventually grow weary and seek new challenges.

My grades began to slide. Sharply. I fell asleep in class. Miss Pataki once threw a book at me to stop me from snoring. My parents had a conference with the school principal. They grounded me. I was suspended from school for one week due to a lunchtime lack of judgment that found me in the school’s Japanese garden behind the automotive shop. Another student caught me sneaking in, taking off my clothes, and inserting one of Mr. Brondshell’s cigars into my mouth before taking up a pose as a merchant marine. My secret was out.

Eventually, I turned to a life of crime. No one understood the pleasure I derived from standing in gardens. I couldn’t get anyone’s permission to be their unpaid garden gnome. Home owners couldn’t comprehend what beauty I found standing motionless and without purpose in their well-kept gardens. I found myself slinking into gardens when no one could detect me. I had become a hapless cur. This never-ending passion soon had me standing in gardens every minute of the day.

Even at the local police precinct.

The chief wasn’t happy. He cuffed me. He booked me, placed me behind bars.

Thus was the beginning of my career as a criminal garden gnome. Today, I am in prison, captive to an addiction of my own making. Still, I am grateful for the staff letting me stand in the warden’s oft-neglected garden unabated by guilt or their attempts to rehabilitate me.

_Allen Taylor is the author of many fictions, flash and otherwise. Stay tuned for more to come._

Image by ChatGPT

[First published at Substack](https://thetaylorkarass.substack.com/p/my-secret-life-as-a-garden-gnome).

body.title: Qurator's: Hive Top Chef! | Tomatoes | Stuffed tomato rings and a very nutritious mini burger
body.body: >Greetings dear friends, welcome to my blog. Today I am once again joining the weekly contest [Qurator's: Hive Top Chef! | Tomatoes]( https://hive.blog/qurator/@qurator/qurators-hive-top-chef-or-tomatoes-tfd0om). After being away for several days due to work and a broken phone, I’m glad to be back. I missed out on a few recipes, but I’m back now to share my recipe featuring tomatoes, this week’s ingredient. The truth is, I don’t eat this vegetable very often. A couple of months ago, I stopped eating it because my uric acid levels had gone up, so I also cut out red meat. I use tomatoes in salads and Bolognese sauce, and I love pairing them with onions when I eat tuna._

>This time, even though I’m using tuna, I made something different. I usually mix diced tomatoes and onions with the flaked tuna, but this time I made tomato rings stuffed with tuna. I also had a little of this mixture left over, so I used it to make mini burgers.<div>


<hr>


<center>


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmce83zEL2nNmwSZvbufBprzsWUnt5RdtvCzETB6hEnfwS/image.png)



</center>


<hr>

<div class=\

>I made a mixture with eggs, tuna, and spices, which served as the filling for the tomato rings that I pan-fried with a little olive oil. I wanted to eat burgers too, so I made some omelets with the egg-tuna mixture to use as the buns. I added lettuce and tomato—what a nutritious and tasty burger! Here’s the step-by-step guide; I hope you like it.<div>


<hr>



## Ingredients


<hr>


<div class=\
>- 5 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil\n

>1.- Wash the lettuce, tear it into pieces with your hands, and soak it in water with a teaspoon of white vinegar for about 15 minutes. After that time, rinse it with water to remove the vinegar. Set aside.
![1779728384825.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNVAtQ2xrHzDEjKEGc96dtwAt9EiRWFAoz7efgCsWrXdD/1779728384825.jpg)
![1779728384978.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX82NyKufbrj7AiVFv6Uw3T1Yx9uqMVfJh35RHpvSeQnx/1779728384978.jpg)

>2.- Peel the onion, wash it, and dice it into small pieces.
![1779728384835.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZgrKGid4sTevTjN6ksTCUPmyHrFfjZ69gBh6N8kpZ4gf/1779728384835.jpg)
![1779728384966.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVLthVtN2abNvKNZRqwB5R2TyEWxkGyCduHiocWKAEwsp/1779728384966.jpg)

>3.- Add a tablespoon of olive oil to a skillet and sauté the onions with salt to taste.
![1779728384853.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV5S3z9VHUpVv44Z9jaQmEygaF1ptGGW4ChVWAsuQR4Tk/1779728384853.jpg)

>4.-. Add the sautéed onion to the tuna, then add the eggs, spices (paprika and oregano), and salt to taste. Mix well.
![1779728384860.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY3ExBhv7uvV8fHvq18BX9EG6zqDcmso6Db9vAMSfTG5b/1779728384860.jpg)

>5.-. Wash the tomato, slice it, and carefully remove the core to form rings. Set aside the slices that aren’t perfectly round for the mini burger, but remove the seeds from them. Heat the olive oil in a skillet and add the tomato rings.
![1779728384844.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTFVDGKuxchmnzJcdxYF6WVqsyqLFTdGsGQeDC5hH2fSZ/1779728384844.jpg)

>6.-. Using a teaspoon, carefully spoon the mixture of tuna, eggs, and onion into the center of each tomato ring. It’s okay if some of the egg mixture spills out the sides; just gently wipe it away. Flip them over to brown the other side, then place them on paper towels. Repeat the process until all the tomato rings are done.
![1779728384870.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXazL14BjGgvp6B5KGcVX9f1WWaC4gYLNN3ehakpAPSbz/1779728384870.jpg)
![1779746244573.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdQHZLP94wRLPLW55XnRuVGZNH7aBLc3deGGEW1eaTHL9/1779746244573.jpg)

>7.-. Using the remaining mixture of tuna, eggs, and onion, make a couple of tortillas, shaping them as round as possible. To do this, pour a tablespoon of olive oil (one per tortilla) into the pan to cook each one. Once they’re ready, place the lettuce and tomato slices between the tortillas, and your mini burger is ready.
![1779728384878.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbZALEhpXqTEoP7YY6zavTF5AsDLDKFLu8U65TH5fvaJY/1779728384878.jpg)

> This dish with tomatoes turned out delicious—a nice change of pace for breakfast or dinner. I served it with tartar sauce.
![1779728384902.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQRa3fxBB1bJAWsnYKRHdPWVBs6tGMJY4aDXCT3gjdwE6/1779728384902.jpg)
![1779728384914.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNVnj2QbCKsN8DpZ3j7pWTeFSrJ9vmhUydxnTRy8gXHxu/1779728384914.jpg)
![1779728384954.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQsxRUXAgHzVpaRGf2CEZ652atcGai5iytR6HTdAUvtHM/1779728384954.jpg)
I hope you liked it, this has been my participation in Hive Top Chef competition. See you another time.
All photos are original, taken with my Xiaomi Redmi 9 cell phone. The editions were made with the application [GridArt](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=photoeditor.layout.collagemaker&hl=en_ZA&gl=US).

body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQWZia4btc3dnzPSJJCzfyp6aKkzrvEfaAdq3m9w5i9aZ/1779694038094.png)
<Center>_Portada_</center>
<center>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eve66/23tGwQ9PTdcLGhdgdVToYFZeRnY1T3ux5FhspwX5hhXgM2TeSzAz4RQzmDPSHuziMPTmv.png</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVgTW75oBAQ8nyU75DdzpiYYZA1ENekALBQgaXsGKk4mS/1779694209152.png)

___

**_‎5 de marzo de 2013_**

‎
‎–_¡Vecina! ¡Vecina, asómese rápido!_– gritaba una voz por el fondo, a través del patio de la casa. 
‎
‎Gemía con dolor, angustia y lamento. 
‎
‎–_¡Vecinaaa!_ –volvió a gritar pero esta vez con un marcado tono que transmitía agonía. 
‎
<div class=\

>Era Carolina, la dueña del local donde funcionaba un Comedor Popular financiado por el gobierno -que daba patio con patio con nuestra casa- donde trabajaba mi mamá como cocinera desde que el comedor se estableció allí. Y era a mi mamá a quien llamaba. ‎ ‎Ella no estaba, pero esos gritos me hicieron erizar la piel porque era el tipo de grito que suele oírse cuando ha sucedido una tragedia, así que salí corriendo a asomarme esperando cualquier cosa. Apenas me vio a lo lejos, rompió a llorar y con voz ahogada por la angustia, me gritó: ‎ ‎–_¡Dile a tu mamá que Chávez se murió!_– ‎ ‎Al cabo de unos momentos repetían una y otra vez en todos los canales de televisión, emisoras de radio y redes sociales: ‎ >‎***_... a las cuatro y veinticinco de la tarde, ha fallecido... Hugo Chávez_***

___ ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX1DVYHmwg6R2xmMfzrg7qif7pBGsC4sQc81YBnvVJ7hu/1779694906551.jpg) _Para muchas personas en los sectores populares, el anuncio oficial de la muerte de Hugo Chávez supuso un golpe dífícil de aguantar_

_Fotografía de [Fábio Ribeiro](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/mujer-retrato-pelo-canoso-cabello-corto-18048520/) en Pexels_
___ ‎ ‎Ese fue, palabra por palabra, el anuncio que había hecho minutos antes el entonces vicepresidente de la República: Nicolás Maduro Moros. ‎ ‎Todo se paralizó. La conmoción se generalizó en el ambiente. El hombre que se había atornillado al poder por más de una década, oficialmente estaba muerto. A partir de ese día, nada... absolutamente nada sería igual. Ni mejor. ‎ ‎
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eve66/23tGwQ9PTdcLGhdgdVToYFZeRnY1T3ux5FhspwX5hhXgM2TeSzAz4RQzmDPSHuziMPTmv.png
‎ ‎ ‎Desde que salimos de La Guaira –mi papá, mi mamá embarazada de mi hermano Abraham y yo– en condición de damnificados en el año 1999 a causa de la tragedia de Vargas, jamás me acostumbré a vivir en otro lugar. Incluso al día de hoy me considero una criatura errante y sin hogar, lejos del lugar donde nací. ‎ ‎No sé qué sello emocional o de sangre lleva un guaireño desde que nace que difícilmente se adapta a vivir en otro lado que no sea su terruño; y si lo hace, es resignación. Pero yo jamás pude ni he podido resignarme a vivir en otro lado que no sea mi Guaira. ‎ ‎La playa, la montaña, el aire cargado de salitre, el bullicio de su día a día entre autobuses abarrotados hasta más no poder, camiones-gandolas trasladando contenedores desde las aduanas del puerto, el ruido de los aviones al aterrizar y despegar del aeropuerto, el calor humano tan auténtico de su gente, sus tambores, su cercanía con Caracas, las oportunidades... en fin; lo vibrante de su espíritu cotidiano. Todo eso y mucho más que faltaría por mencionar hace de La Guaira para mí, un lugar único y especial. ___ ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRqLKmcCBR19zmsijqNKYWwXQJxFsxY73PKwDkBZHd4uP/1779701383809.jpg)
_Una playa_
_Fotografía de [yonaldi malin basa](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/mar-playa-costa-orilla-del-mar-8566028/) en Pexels_
___ ‎ ‎Allí vivía toda mi familia paterna, con quienes tenía una particular cercanía emocional; razón por la cual anualmente la temporada de vacaciones era sobremanera especial para mí porque era la oportunidad de visitarlos y pasar alrededor de un mes en el litoral central. ‎‎En el año 2009, cuando me gradué de bachiller, mi horizonte fue –y ha sido– regresarme a la Guaira definitivamente. Mi infancia la viví allí, mis mejores recuerdos están allí y mis ilusiones se resumen en retornar al lugar donde fui feliz. ‎ ‎Pero volviendo a los días que siguieron al anuncio del deceso de Chávez, el gobierno agilizó un enorme aparato de movilización en todo el país. Harían un enorme esfuerzo logístico para llevar a los fieles revolucionarios a ver a su comandante en capilla ardiente durante la semana que estuvo en la academia militar. Por esa razón, en Cantaura se organizó una caravana con varios autobuses que salían desde la plaza de la ciudad en un viaje ida y vuelta para quienes desearan embarcarse en aquella aventura. ___ ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVxL7sS3ActX5ik5iAeu9eNzxD9vAgwPZLh5d4JLfRk3R/1779701520996.jpg)
_Autobuses_
_Fotografia de [HONG SON](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/vista-de-autobuses-en-una-calle-de-la-ciudad-20528591/) en Pexels_
___ ‎ ‎Contemplando en esa marea una oportunidad irrepetible, me puse una camisa roja, empaqué suficiente ropa y al grito de _\

_ no necesité pensarlo dos veces para irme de polizón. La expresión en la cara de mis padres fue todo un poema cuando, viéndome hacer maletas, les dije escuetamente: 
‎
‎–_Me voy para La Guaira_–
‎
‎Pero a ellos no les hizo ninguna gracia. 
‎
‎–_¿Te vas para La Guaira?_– me preguntó mi papá como creyendo que yo le jugaba una broma. 
‎
‎–_Sí_– le respondí sin más. 
‎
‎–_¿Y con qué dinero vas tú a pagar pasaje si no tienes ni medio, muchacho?_–
‎
‎–_Yo no necesito pasaje_– afirmé –_Me voy en los autobuses que salen de la plaza llevando gente a Caracas a ver el cadáver de Chávez... solo que yo no voy a ver el cadáver de Chávez_– hice una pausa mientras mi papá me veía conteniendo la respiración– _No más consiga bajar del autobús en Caracas, me voy a la parada donde salen las busetas que van para La Guaira, me monto y me voy a la casa de mi abuela._
‎
‎La determinación que ambos percibieron en mi voz los convenció de que no estaba jugando y se limitaron a guardar silencio. No podían detenerme, me conocían bien y sabían que cuando me decidía por algo, era contra cielo y tierra que me enfrentaba por lograrlo. Y tampoco podían salirme con el disco rayado aquel de: _\

_. Pues oficialmente, ya no quería vivir bajo ese techo. Es simple. 


___


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf1LSDkumHwHrQEsZD83gGaWismRoHuHEa6cv8S8fk7qt/1779702300488.jpg)
<center>_Preparé mi maleta y me fui_</center>
<center>_Fotografía de [Mathias Reding](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/persona-viaje-viajar-bolso-11213249/) en Pexels_</center>
___

‎
‎Estaba harto de vivir en Cantaura. Hasta aquellos 21 años de mi vida, ese pueblo había representado el peor lugar para vivir. No concebía un futuro estable y en mi opinión, aquel sitio solo se resumía en eso: _la nada_. Sin oportunidades de empleo, sin lugares de esparcimiento ni áreas de recreación, ni un cine, un zoológico, una pista de patinaje, un simple parque ¡Dios mío...! Nada.
‎
‎
‎Explicar por qué Cantaura representaba la nada para mí... pues, pensándolo bien; es complejo. Pero lo resumiré de la manera más precisa posible. 
‎
‎En mayor medida se debía a la ausencia absoluta de propósito que yo sentía en ese lugar, tanto en ese momento como en perspectiva para el futuro. Tradicionalmente, Cantaura es una ciudad dormitorio y su economía es de subsistencia. No hay fuentes sólidas ni estables de empleo, la economía informal es la norma, y el campo laboral convencional se limita a las vacantes políticas que habilite la municipalidad o los comercios minoristas de asiáticos. 
‎
‎Además, es un lugar caluroso, muy caluroso. Y mi composición biológica, con un metabolismo muy acelerado y fuertes golpes de ansiedad me obligan a sudar hasta por el simple acto de pensar. Puede sonar cómico, pero es la verdad. Y para una persona así, como yo, Cantaura es un horno insoportable. 

___

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQnmLXBDGgUXUwyzr8snQT3wwAuST8EbkdR7nu4oKuh9M/1779702581149.jpg)
<center>_Calor sofocante_</center>
<center>_Fotografía de [Mathias Reding](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/persona-viaje-viajar-bolso-11213249/) en Pexels_</center>
___

‎
‎A eso debo añadirle que no veía factible ese escenario para formar una familia. De paso, el único núcleo universitario que existe planteaba en ese entonces carreras que no encajaban en la realidad de la zona, y que de estudiar alguna, necesariamente obligaba a considerar hacer maletas para ejercerla en otro sitio más desarrollado.
‎
‎De este modo, Cantaura se sentía para mí como una especie de cárcel a cielo abierto, un campo de concentración en condiciones forzadas para habitarlo, dónde cada día era una lucha contra la adversidad y el deseo de avanzar, de crecer, de volar. 
‎
‎Se me dificultaba muchísimo entender por qué razón después de once años pasando tanta necesidad allí juntos, mis padres nunca se propusieron mudarse de ese hueco. ‎Y yo no me iba a quedar acompañándolos. Si ellos no consideraban otra opción aparte de secarse en vida allí, pues yo sí. 
‎
___
‎
‎El nueve de marzo, a las seis de la mañana, después de toda una noche de viaje por tierra en el convoy de autobuses, ya en la plaza Diego Ibarra de Caracas, bajaba el escalón de la puerta del bus y daba mis primeros pasos a una vida, en teoría, independiente.
‎
‎Ese día el ambiente en Caracas era febril. Se respiraba la tristeza y la frustración en cada esquina por haber perdido un ídolo que creían inmortal. Sin embargo, aún lo asumían como tal. Bajo el grito de la consigna: _\

_ comenzaba una nueva era donde la persona se convertía en una leyenda.
‎

‎
‎Con el dinero suficiente para desplazarme desde Caracas hasta La Guaira y llegar a la casa de mi familia paterna con comodidad, me separé de la oleada que empujaba a la marea en la efervescencia política y me fuí en dirección a Gato Negro, una famosa estación del Metro en el oeste de Caracas, desde donde salían (y todavía salen) unidades de transporte con dirección al litoral. 
‎
‎Más tarde, mi abuelo –que por ese entonces aún vivía– y mis tíos recibieron la visita con sorpresa, la misma sorpresa que, muy a pesar de mi ingenuidad, cambiaría a una sensación sin nombre que no capté ni entendí en los pequeños gestos, signos y señales que gritaban en silencio _\

_, cuando les dije:
‎
‎–_Me vine para quedarme._
‎
‎Hoy entiendo y reconozco que mi gran error (de muchos otros más) comenzó por no avisarles de mis planes, sino creer que todos allí pensaban como María Martina, mi abuela. 
‎
‎Para el año 2013, ella tendría cinco años de fallecida, pero en mi interior aún conservaba esa sensación intensa, profunda y genuina de buena fe, seguridad, confianza y cobijo que su memoria y su casa –junto con esa familia– representaban para mí. Convencido de que todos sus hijos –y mi abuelo– pensaban igual que ella, demasiado tarde me di cuenta con amargura de que, como dice un dicho popular: \

. 
‎
‎Con mi abuela en la tumba y sin ninguna experiencia conviviendo por tiempo prolongado con mi familia paterna, tuve que experimentar en carne propia a partir de ese momento, que por muy bueno y sólido que haya sido el caminar de una persona noble en esta vida –y al mando de un hogar al cual gobernó con vara de hierro–, no hay garantía alguna de que necesariamente todos los que quedaron tras su muerte sigan su ejemplo.
‎
‎
‎En retrospectiva, no me arrepiento de haberme ido para La Guaira en aquel tiempo y enfrentarme a la vida por mi cuenta, pero sí me arrepiento profundamente de haber confiado en mi familia como parte de esta etapa. Entendería de maneras desagradables que una cosa era ir de visita y pasar unos cuantos días, y otra muy distinta era convivir con ellos... y descubrir que durante años albergaron turbios resentimientos y sucios celos a causa del cariño sincero de María Martina por mí papá y por todos sus hijos, pero especialmente por mí. 
‎
‎
‎Y por atravesar la circunstancia equivocada en el lugar equivocado, tuve que pagar un altísimo precio.
‎

‎
‎María Martina era todo lo que se podía desear de una madre y una abuela. Lógicamente era un ser humano, cargado de errores, mañas y manías, pero las compensaba con su determinación a ser una persona diferente. 
‎
‎Levantó a todos sus hijos con el mismo ejemplo y la misma actitud. Pero de todos ellos, uno sobresalía por acoplarse voluntariamente al sano modelo que le fue enseñado: mi papá. No que los demás no lo hicieran, pero no de aquel modo tan devoto y agradecido como él. 
‎
‎Para ella, ese fue el motor de una conexión afectiva muy especial que perduraría hasta convertirla, más que una madre, en su mejor amiga. Después de crecer, independizarse y formar su hogar, mi papá y ella se acercaron mucho más en torno a un genuino e inquebrantable amor de familia que terminó haciendo que mi abuela se enamorara de los nietos que mi papá le dio. 

‎De ese modo la historia y las circunstancias me involucran. Mi abuela vio en mi una especie de prototipo de lo que fue mi papá de niño. Revivió la experiencia de identificarse de esa forma tan especial con alguien y evidentemente yo correspondí a ese cariño. Fue así como María Martina se convirtió en mi otra madre.

‎Anualmente, en las vacaciones, se daban dos posibilidades invariables pero aleatorias: o íbamos a visitarla, o ella nos visitaba. Terminó siendo una peregrinación casi religiosa a pesar de la distancia de siete horas de asfalto entre el calor de Cantaura y el salitre de La Guaira; pero aún así, esa cercanía emocional nunca se rompió. 
‎
‎Seis meses antes de mi graduación como bachiller, ella acordó con mi papá llevarme en las vacaciones de verano para estar con ella durante un mes. Recuerdo ese corto periodo de tiempo como un episodio de mucha conexión emocional. Mientras estuve con ella, hablábamos como adultos de cualquier cosa; íbamos juntos de compras, a la iglesia, a la plaza, a Caracas, a la feria, ¡a todas partes! Y en casa siempre estuve a su servicio para ayudarle en lo que fuese necesario. 
‎
‎Casi todas las noches nos sentábamos juntos en la platabanda de la casa, y se nos iban las horas mientras ella me contaba sus experiencias de vida, algunas alegres, otras angustiosas, tragos amargos, lágrimas, decepciones, logros y anécdotas que ella buscaba fuesen para mí lecciones de las que en mi intuición, sustrajera enseñanzas y consejos valiosos. 

‎
‎Maria Martina padecía mucho con sus rodillas. Un desgaste óseo severo hizo que con el tiempo, le costara cada vez más el sencillo hecho elemental de caminar. Los dolores eran muy frecuentes y su médico de cabecera le recomendó un implante de prótesis. Una vez, sentados al atardecer en el techo de concreto de su casa, mientras soplaba la brisa, tomé una decisión. 
‎
‎–_Voy a estudiar Ingeniería Civil._
‎
‎Ella me miró sorprendida. 
‎
‎–_¿Y eso?_– me preguntó. 
‎
‎–_Voy a graduarme con honores y empezaré a trabajar en contratos de construcción para hacer el dinero y pagarte la prótesis_ –le dije mirándola fijamente con una determinación inquebrantable. 
‎
‎Sus ojos se llenaron de lágrimas. Mi abuela era extraordinariamente sensible. Le sonreí enternecido. 
‎
‎–_Quiero que tus días de vejez puedas pasarlos lo más cómoda posible_ –agregué– _y si tengo que romperme el lomo para que así sea, no me importa. Te lo mereces._
‎
‎Mi abuela rompió a llorar. Entre sollozos que me desgarraban por dentro me dijo:
‎
‎–_Tú aquí en mi casa siempre tendrás un hogar; y sea que estudies eso o no, yo siempre te voy a apoyar y siempre voy a hacer el sacrificio que haga falta para que tú seas un profesional y tengas con qué mantenerte y poder formar una familia. Aquí estoy yo, tienes a tus tíos, a tu abuelo... y esta casa siempre será tu casa._

‎Sus palabras me dieron un golpe de oxígeno brutal. Por fin una oportunidad de regresar a La Guaira, el lugar donde era feliz. A partir de ese día, mi decisión de ser Ingeniero en Construcciones Civiles fue tan legítima y necesaria como mi cédula de identidad. 
‎
‎Ella me prometió que estaría en mi graduación de bachiller al precio que fuese. Faltaban solo ocho meses para eso y la expectativa era fantástica. Solo pensar que ella estuviese presente me mantenía en una sensación de alegría constante. Pasado el mes de las vacaciones, regresé a Cantaura con nuevas expectativas y una perspectiva distinta. 
‎
‎Alrededor de un mes después, la mañana del día de mi cumpleaños, sin avisar, mi abuela nos sorprendió con su visita. Yo no podía contener la emoción por la sorpresa: justo el día de mi cumpleaños. Fue el mejor regalo que recibí en esa ocasión.
‎
‎Su visita en aquella oportunidad duró siete días. A su partida de retorno a La Guaira, la acompañé al terminal de pasajeros y justo cuando se anunció la salida de su bus, ella rompió a llorar. Entendí que le dolía de formas indecibles separarse de nosotros, no soportaba estar lejos de su hijo y sus nietos. La tomé de las manos, miré sus ojos y le dije: 
‎
‎–_No es la última vez que nos vamos a ver. Tenemos un encuentro pendiente en mi graduación._
‎
‎Ella solo lloró con más intensidad. Me costó mantenerme sereno y no quebrarme porque sabía que eso iba a crear una conmoción más intensa en sus frágiles emociones.
‎
‎Subió al autobús y coincidió con los últimos asientos, desde donde ella podía voltear y por el vidrio trasero, verme durante la partida. Me dio una sensación desagradable en el pecho ver sus ojos a lo lejos bañados en lágrimas mientras se despedía con su mirada. 
‎
‎
‎A la mañana siguiente, alrededor de las seis de la mañana nos despertamos en casa por el sonido del timbre del teléfono. Era el celular de mi papá que tras varios pitidos, cesó. Luego sonó el mío que lo tenía debajo de la almohada. Dada la hora, era extraordinariamente inusual recibir una llamada en casa. Al ver el código de área del que marcaban, comprobé la procedencia de la llamada: desde Caracas. 
‎
‎
‎–_¿Aló?_– respondí con la mente aún adormecida. 
‎
‎–_¿Por qué tu papá no contesta el teléfono?_ –identifiqué la voz de mi tío del otro lado del celular, pero extrañamente alterado, como molesto... ¿o asustado?
‎
‎– _Es que la llamada se cayó antes de que pudiera contestar_ – me excusé todavía soñoliento– _estábamos durmiendo._
‎
‎– _Dile que se venga_– me dijo sin más; jadeando como si estuviese caminando un maratón– _a mi mamá le dió un infarto._ 
‎

‎
‎It was a cry of pain, anguish and despair. 
‎

Ever since we left La Guaira – my dad, my mum, who was pregnant with my brother Abraham, and me – as victims of the Vargas tragedy in 1999, I have never got used to living anywhere else. Even today, I still see myself as a wandering, homeless soul, far from the place where I was born. ‎ ‎I don’t know what emotional or blood-related mark a native of La Guaira bears from birth that makes it so difficult for them to adapt to living anywhere other than their homeland; and if they do, it is out of resignation. But I have never been able to resign myself to living anywhere other than my La Guaira. ‎ ‎The beach, the mountains, the air thick with saltpetre, the hustle and bustle of daily life amidst buses crammed to bursting point, lorries hauling containers from the port’s customs, the noise of planes landing and taking off from the airport, the genuine warmth of its people, their drums, its proximity to Caracas, the opportunities... in short; the vibrancy of its everyday spirit. I spent my childhood there, my fondest memories are there, and my hopes boil down to returning to the place where I was happy. ‎ ‎But returning to the days following the announcement of Chávez’s death, the government set in motion a massive mobilisation effort across the country. ___ ‎ ‎Seeing in that tide a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, I put on a red shirt, packed enough clothes and, shouting _\

_, I didn’t need to think twice about leaving as a stowaway. The look on my parents’ faces was priceless when, seeing me packing my bags, I told them bluntly: 
‎
‎–_I’m off to La Guaira_–
‎
‎But they didn’t find it funny at all. 
‎
‎–_You’re off to La Guaira?_– my dad asked me, as if he thought I was playing a joke on him. 
‎
‎–_Yes_– I replied, without further ado. 
‎
‎–_And how on earth are you going to pay for a ticket when you’re penniless, lad?_–
‎
‎–_I don’t need a ticket_– I stated –_I’m going on the buses leaving the square, taking people to Caracas to see Chávez’s body... only I’m not going to see Chávez’s body_– I paused whilst my dad watched me, holding his breath – _As soon as I get off the bus in Caracas, I’ll go to the stop where the minibuses leave for La Guaira, hop on one and head to my grandmother’s house._
‎
‎The determination they both sensed in my voice convinced them I wasn’t joking, and they simply fell silent. They couldn’t stop me; they knew me well and knew that when I set my mind on something, I’d move heaven and earth to achieve it. Nor could they pull that old line on me: “As long as you live under this roof, you won’t get your own way.” Well, officially, I no longer wanted to live under that roof. It’s simple.
