A little bit of leaves and flowers to quench the thirst for freedom, a little air without smoke, the lungs; the most grateful. My tired eyes, seeing cars and poles, ask for green, the lens rejoices and I, well, filled with little plants that prick and cling to clothes.

Un poco de hojas y flores para calmar la sed de libertad, un poco de aire sin humo, los pulmones; los más agradecidos. Mis ojos cansados se ver carros y postes piden verde, la lente feliz y yo, bueno, llena de maticas qué pinchan y se pegan a la ropa.

body.title: Strength Has a Support System
body.body:
>

Trying to carry the whole weight of your success, both personal and professional, on your own shoulders almost always ends the same way, with stress piling up and your motivation quietly fading.

>Intentar cargar todo el peso de tu éxito, tanto personal como profesional, sobre tus propios hombros casi siempre termina igual, con el estrés acumulándose y tu motivación apagándose poco a poco.

When the demands of work and family stack on top of each other, willpower alone won't hold the line, and sooner or later you end up drained, watching that clear vision of where you're headed start to blur.

>Cuando las exigencias del trabajo y la familia se van amontonando una sobre otra, la pura fuerza de voluntad no alcanza para sostenerlo todo, y tarde o temprano terminas agotado, viendo cómo esa visión clara de hacia dónde vas se empieza a esfumar.

The truth is you were never meant to do it all alone, and the real shift comes from actively building a support system around you.

>La verdad es que nunca estuviste hecho para hacerlo todo solo, y el verdadero cambio llega cuando construyes de forma activa una red de apoyo a tu alrededor.

Without the right people around you the journey turns heavy, discouraging, and lonely.

>Sin las personas correctas a tu lado el camino se vuelve pesado, desalentador y solitario.

My question for you today is, how is the weight of trying to manage everything yourself showing up in your stress levels right now.

>Así que aquí va una pregunta para ti, ¿cómo se manifiesta en tus niveles de estrés, justo ahora, el peso de intentar manejarlo todo tú solo?

body.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 25 2026
body.body:
Hello Actifit community and fitness enthusiasts! This picture is created with AI ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/bb03f179-ca99-4e5d-a1f0-d9d832d02330.jpg) ​What a way to kickstart the week! Today is Monday, May 25, 2026, and it has been an absolute scorcher here in London. The thermometer hit a staggering 36°C (96.8°F), which is incredibly hot for this time of the year. While a lot of people might prefer staying indoors with the AC on full blast on a day like this, I decided to take advantage of the bright weather and get moving. It wasn't easy, but keeping up with my fitness goals is non-negotiable! ​I am incredibly proud to report that I officially smashed my daily goal today, wrapping up the afternoon with a total of 11,191 steps! ​Keeping the Streak Alive ​Consistency is everything when it comes to long-term fitness. Looking at my Actifit dashboard, hitting today's goal means I have officially extended my consistency streak to 17 days in a row! There is something so satisfying about seeing those green checkmarks light up for every single day of the week. ​Hats off to Actifit’s latest updates as well—the app interface feels smoother than ever, and tracking my progress during this Spring Refresh season has been a breeze. ​Fun, Heat, and Scooters ​Most of my steps today came from spending some high-energy time outdoors with the family. The kids brought out their scooters to the open paved area near the park, and watching them zip around meant I had to keep up! One of the boys was rocking his helmet and leading the pack, while the others were pushing hard and cheering each other on. ​As you can tell from the photos, it was a sweaty affair. I had my trusty bottle of water with me at all times to stay hydrated, and a towel to wipe off the sweat. Working out or simply staying active in 36°C heat requires a lot of extra effort and discipline. Your heart pumps faster, you sweat instantly, and every step feels a bit heavier. But honestly, the feeling of accomplishment afterward makes it all worth it. ​Hydration is Key! ​If you are exercising or walking in hot weather, please remember to take care of your body: ​Drink water before, during, and after your session. ​Take short breaks in the shade if you feel overheated. ​Listen to your body and don't overdo it. ​After a long, active afternoon, the sun finally started to dip below the horizon, bringing a much-needed cool breeze. The peaceful evening sky was the perfect reward after a demanding, high-step day. ​How was your Monday? Did you manage to hit your step goals today? Let me know in the comments below, and let's keep pushing each other to stay active, healthy, and consistent! ​
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@lovlygirl/actifit-lovlygirl-20260525t213653823z)_

body.body:
I saw a snippet of the movie on tiktok and I knew I had to watch it. This movie was way too heavy, it's the kind that you still feel even hours after watching it, I swear I still haven't recovered.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ4fBCAKePGXAkHUSQbgjdnhBXZUR7byoLM7er7EBT1kW/1779462849848.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVNvAuhb1a88i1KonDLydXfsMKyj5AomQU66Bio7Kog2Z/1779462849986.png)

My Sister’s Keeper is  based on the novel by Jodi Picoult and it follows Anna Fitzgerald, played by Abigail Breslin as she fights for medical emancipation from her parents. She was conceived for a specific purpose, she had to be a genetic match for her older sister Kate, who has leukemia. From childhood, Anna undergoes countless medical procedures to help keep Kate alive. But at age eleven, she sues her parents for medical emancipation, essentially demanding the right to control her own body.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT8jtZgGnr5fod19zJmzJShGyLKMAbSVmXNndfNSULxS4/1779462905066.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU1VMDsjShjxNXwwTzggVLzvMrg5tWPQUo9JU9HPc883o/1779462905224.png)


The plot alone already tug your heartstrings as you try to wrap your head around what it feels like to be an organ bank for someone else. This movie contemplates \

And “Would you save one child at the expense of another?”. What makes the movie works so well emotionally is because nobody feels completely wrong. You can put yourself in the shoes of opposing characters and still understand where they are coming from, most movies can't pull that, there's usually a clear line, but My Sister’s Keeper refuses that. Sara Fitzgerald (the mother), played by Cameron Diaz, is simultaneously loving and terrifying. She dedicates her entire life to saving Kate. She sacrifices her career, her marriage, her sanity, and nearly every aspect of normal life. And yet, in doing so, she slowly stops seeing Anna as a separate person. That’s what makes the movie so emotionally complicated because she is not malicious. She is just desperate. Her parental love parental love mixed with fear of losing kate, can become controlling without the her even noticing. I was torn between sympathy and frustration because understand where she's coming from. But I resent her, then I feel guilty for resenting her.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXHqqH5NdvbaRoxiymd5ZmXyZsNv5Xw72XLyHM9nDyhzc/1779462971212.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVsdcassdviUnH7443PA3k1dW6syCx4R98KgVcgXZdzBR/1779462971359.png)

I feel Anna's fight was more than just about controlling her body. It was more about identity. Imagine growing up knowing your existence had a medical purpose attached to it from birth, knowing that if her sister wasn't sick she might have not even exist. Every surgery, every needle, every hospital visit reinforces the idea that your body belongs partly to someone else. Her taking control and resisting to give her sister one of her kidneys doesn't mean she's wants her sister to die, or that she's just rebellious because she clearly loves her but this was her trying to see if she can exist outside being a organ donor for her sister. Anna carries a heavy responsibility throughout the film, something she shouldn't. She is emotionally older than she should be, like someone forced to mature too quickly because illness consumed her family’s entire emotional ecosystem. And it's not just her but everyone in the family becomes emotionally shaped around Kate’s illness. Even Jesse, the older brother, becomes almost invisible.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeUZ6QKz9sWrPVK3YLHgQyZKFLji1mojHvsn2Pk1d1Pvf/1779463011620.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZSshZUFXeESRzHHZYQ5kAR1Qhrz41zBBuCoQ6LbXKHhN/1779463011855.png)

Jesse Fitzgerald , played by Evan Ellingson, is the saddest character. Jesse is drowning emotionally, yet nobody fully notices because of  Kate’s illness. This is one of the realistic aspects the movie portray. Families dealing with chronic illness, the other children pay emotionally They’re expected to “understand,” stay quiet, mature faster, and avoid adding problems to an already overwhelmed family. Jesse acts out through rebellion and destructive behavior, but underneath that anger is neglect. This leads you to ask, What happens to the children who aren’t dying, but are still suffering?

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRdh6N3tqPfp8FPLwnJgphiwE3W3yEyNrJzc1uA9xWwc5/1779463192725.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXfev7pBf91a3Xy1hZWU9Ytm8unm2dWcjuCNSBs52WdgC/1779463168567.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZjryJvF59j4j6P6DjtwdK1NwSiSDNf1n3YZQAmorVHDJ/1779463168720.png)

Funny enough Kate, played by Sofia Vassilieva, the sick child everyone is trying to save has the least control over her own life. She is exhausted by years of treatment, pain, hospitals, and false hope. She wants to go but her mother is holding on strong, which essential forces her to tell her sister to reject helping her so she can pass on. Suddenly, Anna’s lawsuit becomes less about rebellion and more about love. A painful kind of love. The emotionally intelligence in the movie shines through as I understand that fighting endlessly to stay alive is not the same thing as living. I'll critic the fact that the movie moved far from realism in most aspects, especially the legal scene. They were more emotional than real. I also found out that the movie changed the ending of the novel, and fans argued that the original ending was harsher but more thematically powerful. The film’s ending feels more emotionally comforting than the novel’s deeply tragic irony. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmewX7cVdcNJcz1BpxdNxzAQ1hzSz2Equ6R6eAAXdqmmAj/1779463125078.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNMMvWCqY9MCvbQQzd3cF55BcFtcrqUPE3w1msk5cjoxi/1779463125228.png)

My Sister’s Keeper is not just about cancer. It’s about the psychological weight of loving someone you cannot save.
It's about trying to fight through impossible choices. What make it sad is that  nobody’s pain cancels out anybody else’s. Everyone pain is justified. My Sister’s Keeper is emotionally overwhelming, occasionally manipulative, imperfectly written, and carries a powerful message. Nobody exists purely to be right or wrong. They are simply people trying, and often failing, to navigate grief before grief has even fully arrived. Underneath the melodramatic, emotional, and sentimental scenes are genuine ethical questions:
Can love for one child unintentionally become injustice toward another? How do families survive when love itself becomes painful?

It's Still Abeegail,
Thank you for Reading 🥹 
__________________________________________________________________________


The images are scenshots from the movie,
Thank you for stopping by.

body.title: 🌹 Red roses and daydreams
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeqezNBWFg1EKWpsJcAXEW19baqiJU2MyHavMCgyPpieq/IMG_3948.jpg 

There’s something about red roses that always feels special.

Maybe it’s because they remind me of the stories I love reading. In so many manga and comics, a single flower can mean a thousand different things—friendship, courage, love, or simply a beautiful memory.

Today I wasn’t thinking about anything complicated. I was just enjoying the moment, appreciating the little details around me. The flowers hanging above, the bright colors, and that feeling of slowing down for a while.

Life doesn’t always have to be exciting to be meaningful.

Sometimes happiness is just taking a picture, smiling at yourself afterward, and realizing that this ordinary day was actually pretty nice.

I spend a lot of time imagining adventures through the pages of my favorite stories, but moments like these remind me that real life can be beautiful too.

Maybe not as dramatic as a manga chapter... but beautiful in its own way 🌹✨

Just Lynda, collecting simple memories one day at a time.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@lyndax/-red-roses-and-daydreams-4g3)

body.title: Jokari Venshiro: Death Splinter's Backline Damage Dealer
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRemZS7sv11aBerJ3qXr86WA2VnHB437RB2BZ87DPyMsg/image.png)

Hello Splinterlands summoners and welcome back to my blog!

The Conclave Arcana reward cards introduced new units that shake up the meta and take advantage of rulesets. Jokari Venshiro is one such card with stats and abilities that will be a welcome addition in our battles. In today's post, we'll go over Jokari's lore, stats & abilities as well as show my own battle where I used him effectively.

***

# Lore

Joraki Venshiro is a fierce and rebellious dragudo warrior sent by the Empire to investigate the disappearance of Tasoshi Drakamoto in the Wild Northeast. Jokari was known for his combat skill and defiant attitude toward authority. He wields a powerful dragonbone bow capable of devastating attacks. Though he openly mocks his companions and ignores orders, he remains committed to the mission and understands the importance of stopping the Conclave Arcana. He shows arrogance but he has a deep sense of duty to the Dragonsguard, the Empire and the truth behind Tasoshi’s disappearance.

***

# Stats and Abilities

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSfwZakM46DcdwbQZfcAvZeJSAm4CZgdgzio18G1AujgG/image.png)

Jokari Venshiro is an eight mana, epic Death splinter card. At maxed level, he deals five range damage, has eight health and three speed. He has four abilities with various effects. Painforge enables him to increase his power when he gets poisoned, burned or hit by an ally. He can blind enemies, increasing their chance to miss physical attacks. He has Piercing to complement his high attack stats and finally, he has Affliction to prevent healing to afflicted units.

My Jokari Venshiro is level two and already useful at that level in Silver and Gold Leagues. I plan to raise him at level three where he increases his attack to four and gains the Piercing ability.

***

# Featured Battle

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXJYsThyTApgVaNcoRQv1uoLVBiKw3eqbVKMEQiWc3YjQ/image.png)

The battle included the Equalizer and Collateral Damage rulesets. When I see this rulesets, two key cards come to mind. One with Painforge ability and the other with Corrupted Healing ability. Having this in mind, I picked the dragon splinter led by Kavor Skarn and chose Death units. I had Doomshield Warden as tank followed by Nightreaper as a second tank. In third, I had a taunt unit Syrenth to draw attacks. In fourth I had a high damage dealer Magnificent Mollusk. In fifth position I had Jokari Venshiro. His Painforge ability will add power to him as he gets damaged by Reckless. In last, I had the Arachne Weaver who heals the whole team as they get damaged by Reckless.

The enemy chose Death who also had the twin units Jokari Venshiro and Arachne Weaver in the team. The difference that gave me the advantage was the higher level Jokari who had the Blind ability. I also had more attacker units in team that added to my advantage.

[Replay the Battle](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_e678182fb40a865da9f267be44d438a6?ref=logen9f)

***

# Come Play Splinterlands!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfAX3xcPAwc8omveh7imyKtqbHntKgVLqLckGTCHSjPyw/image.png)

Start your Splinterlands adventure today with my [referral](https://splinterlands.com/register?ref=logen9f). You can play the game for free in the Frontier Mode or take your game to the next level by purchasing a spellbook. Buying a spellbook allows you to earn SPS tokens and use the  market to sell in game assets. Also, we will both get 500 Credits which can be used top purchase cards once you buy a spellbook.

body.title: Paseo en bicicleta por el parque [ESP/ENG]
body.body:
> ## Español Hola a todos! el fin de semana pasado la pasamos genial, primero porque hizo buen clima pero también porque disfrutamos juntos y en familia, y es que el sábado decidimos ir al Park im. Jacka Kuronia aquí en Sosnowiec y es un lugar que nos encanta ya que hay muchas cosas para hacer allí y lo más importante para Olivia es que hay parque infantil y mucho espacio para andar su bicicleta, así que eso fue lo primero que ella hizo. Nosotros caminando y Olivia andando bicicleta nos dimos cuenta que en el parque había un evento que la verdad no sabíamos de que era pero se veía con mucho ambiente y tenía que ver con el Alcalde de Sosnowiec ya que él estaba ahí, más tarde fuímos a ver los animales ya que como ya les he dicho hay un pequeño zoológico en el parque, y por supuesto la parada para ver los patos comiendo en el estanque no podía faltar. Esta vez estuvimos caminando más por el bosque (algo que no habíamos hecho antes) y nos encantó ya que vimos algunas cosas nuevas y se sentía muy fresco allí, y es que como pueden ver en las fotos este parque está rodeado de mucha naturaleza y nosotros amamos estar rodeados de la misma. Después de un gran paseo en bicicleta, tuvimos que hacer la respectiva parada en el parque infantil donde Olivia se divirtió mucho más, de hecho ella fue la que más se divirtió allí y nosotros estabamos felices de que ella estuviese disfrutando, aunque terminamos un poco cansados ya que a veces Olivia manejaba rápido y teníamos que estar pendiente corriendo detrás de ella, pero debo decir que todos amamos este parque pues es un parque muy completo para disfrutar toda la familia bien sea caminando, andando bicicleta, patinando o relajandose a tomar o comer algo ya que hay algunos sitios para hacerlo y nos encantan los lugares así por lo que lo visitaremos más seguido este verano, y ustedes que planes disfrutan en familia? ## English Hi everyone! We had a great time last weekend—first because the weather was nice, but also because we got to spend time together as a family. On Saturday, we decided to go to Jack Kuron Park here in Sosnowiec, a place we love because there’s so much to do there. And the most important thing for Olivia is that there’s a playground and plenty of space to ride her bike, so that’s the first thing she did. As we were walking and Olivia was riding her bike, we noticed there was an event going on in the park. We didn’t really know what it was about, but it had a great atmosphere and seemed to involve the Mayor of Sosnowiec since he was there. Later, we went to see the animals—as I’ve mentioned before, there’s a small zoo in the park—and of course, we couldn’t miss the chance to watch the ducks eating at the pond. This time we spent more time walking through the woods (something we hadn’t done before), and we loved it because we saw some new things and it felt really refreshing out there. As you can see in the photos, this park is surrounded by lots of nature, and we love being surrounded by it. After a great bike ride, we had to make the usual stop at the playground where Olivia had a blast—in fact, she was the one who had the most fun there, and we were happy she was enjoying herself, even though we ended up a little tired since Olivia sometimes rode really fast and we had to keep an eye on her, running after her, but I have to say that we all love this park because it’s a very well-rounded place for the whole family to enjoy—whether walking, biking, skating, or relaxing with a drink or a snack—since there are spots to do all of that, and we love places like this, so we’ll be visiting more often this summer. What kind of family outings do you enjoy?

body.title: Necesito más de un millón de dólares.
body.body:
Muchas veces tenemos tantas ideas en mente que quisiéramos ejecutar que, cuando hacemos el análisis de costos, nos damos cuenta de qué tan cerca o lejos estamos de lograrlo. Y, a medida que pasa el tiempo, surgen nuevas ideas que se van acumulando a la gran lista de tareas por ejecutar.

Muchas de las cosas que hemos logrado ejecutar han sido gracias a patrocinadores, quienes responden a las convocatorias de patrocinio de acuerdo con sus intereses, presupuestos anuales y beneficios, pero no precisamente porque crean en una visión concreta de transformación o ejecución.

Durante años hemos logrado avances en el desarrollo de proyectos; no obstante, a medida que vamos creciendo, los proyectos se vuelven más demandantes, más costosos, más visionarios y, a veces, poco comprendidos.

## Estudios de mercado
Desde hace aproximadamente ocho años he tenido una tarea pendiente: medir a la población extranjera en Panamá sobre el uso de criptomonedas. ¿Por qué?

Porque en Panamá no solemos usar criptomonedas con recurrencia como medio de pago, en comparación con otros países de Latinoamérica, sino más bien como un medio de ahorro a largo plazo o capital de inversión. No obstante, algo que se ha identificado es que no tenemos data dura ni estadística local que fortalezca el conocimiento sobre dónde estamos parados y hacia dónde realmente queremos construir.

Claramente, mi perfil comercial de consumo masivo me obliga a pensar en medir y evaluar para decidir sobre la ruta y estrategia a implementar, pero para ello también se necesita capital.

Existe plena certeza de que muchos extranjeros que vienen a Panamá poseen criptomonedas porque prefieren evitarse comisiones de cambio y comisiones por transacciones en el exterior que cobran las tarjetas. Sin embargo, la pregunta es: ¿cuál es el porcentaje real de esos extranjeros que llegan al país?

Sobre esto ya he conversado con consultoras de investigación de mercado, quienes me han planteado iniciar con estudios más introductorios; medir primero a la comunidad local antes de dar el siguiente paso. Lo cual tiene lógica, pero financieramente aumenta los costos.

## Documental
Quizás esta es una de las ideas más recientes, pero también una de las más interesantes.

Panamá tiene una historia particular sobre la evolución del ecosistema Bitcoin, Cripto, Blockchain y Web3. Personajes reconocidos, que no imaginamos, formaron parte de los inicios del desarrollo de las primeras comunidades locales, las cuales marcaron un antes y un después.

El conocimiento y desarrollo de la tecnología han tenido un enfoque más académico, desde la arquitectura de Bitcoin, fortaleciendo una perspectiva científica al hablar de la tecnología y no tanto desde un enfoque de inversión, que suele ser la narrativa tradicional.

El desarrollo de proyectos y negocios juega un papel preponderante, pero siempre con predominio en la necesidad de conocimiento. Por ello, documentar estas experiencias se convierte en una acción clave, ya que descubriríamos historias impresionantes. Por lo tanto, un documental valdría la pena.

## Conferencias y reuniones
Es interesante ver cómo ha crecido el sector MICE (Reuniones, Incentivos, Congresos y Exposiciones) en materia de Bitcoin, Blockchain, Web3 y Cripto. Antes solo existían dos o tres encuentros reconocidos, pero ahora cada país tiene su propia versión, valorando las características propias de ese país en función de la comunidad que lo lidera.

Porque no es lo mismo hablar de una conferencia dedicada únicamente a Bitcoin que hablar de Blockchain o Web3 dentro del mismo país y enfocado en sus propias características. Esto es asombroso, ya que permite descubrir potenciales únicos más allá de temas transversales.

Hoy parece que el sector MICE dentro de nuestra industria no ofrece un valor diferenciador, ya que existe la percepción de que los temas son los mismos en cada conferencia, por ejemplo, debido a que se invita todos los años a los mismos oradores.

También se ha identificado que muchos temas han dejado de ser técnicos para convertirse en un espectáculo político y de marketing, algo completamente alejado de los primeros eventos.

No obstante, cuando te dedicas a estudiar y analizar profundamente, descubres áreas que aún no han sido abordadas. Y es allí donde el ecosistema panameño juega un papel crucial.

Aunado a ello, algo que se debe considerar es que las experiencias deben ser anualizadas y no únicamente puntuales durante las fechas del evento. Por lo tanto, los fondos ya no solo aplican para el evento en sí, sino para cada acción que ocurra a lo largo del año.

Esto permitiría que los patrocinios no solo cubran el evento principal, sino también las actividades adicionales que se planifiquen durante el año.

## Experiencia anualizada
Trabajar sobre una experiencia anualizada implica que, semana tras semana o mes tras mes, las acciones que se realicen incluyan meetups, entrenamientos sociales y corporativos, grabaciones de episodios de podcast, coberturas audiovisuales y programas especiales, así como provisión para atención legal.

Esto último es quizás lo más crucial, ya que se han identificado casos donde miembros del ecosistema se han visto envueltos en situaciones de naturaleza penal y no cuentan con fondos para cubrir honorarios profesionales de abogados defensores ni trámites administrativos que les permitan afrontar mejor dichas situaciones cuando han actuado de buena fe.

Son muchas las situaciones a las que día tras día nos enfrentamos y que, más allá del marketing y la publicidad, atendemos para mantener un ecosistema dinámico, íntegro e integral. Y es por eso que necesito un millón de dólares para poder hacerle frente a esos proyectos.

Claramente, cada una de las acciones implica cubrir los honorarios de los profesionales que trabajan en cada aspecto de las actividades mencionadas, y es allí donde se asume la responsabilidad financiera del desarrollo de cada proyecto.

A veces, la solicitud de patrocinios se realiza de manera transaccional, pero lo cierto es que, cuando se trabaja de esa forma, el desgaste y el consumo de tiempo son mayores que cuando se atiende desde una perspectiva global.


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRTuidAWX7pQrsq1bSK4LiYWeawhntihLjbwvekoN7V7T/image.png)

body.title: Supposed Hidden Messages In Denver Airport Artwork, According To Conspiracy Theories
body.body:
# Supposed Hidden Messages In Denver Airport Artwork, According To Conspiracy Theories

**Source:** https://www.ranker.com/list/denver-airport-hidden-symbols/jacob-shelton

Conspiracy theories about the Denver International Airport (DIA) often involve the admittedly creepy art that exists throughout the terminals. Due to a few unexplainable structures within the airport, the DIA has been the subject of conspiracy theories and speculation since its construction in the early 1990s. Most of the theories have to do with a series of murals, but every piece of art that decorates or has decorated the DIA is believed to be a deep well of symbolism. Many theorists believe that the artwork at the airport references a nefarious plan for a New World Order takeover, while some of the other pieces seem to hint at a dark history. 

![Image 1](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762511/original/the-freemason-capstone-was-funded-by-_the-new-world-airport-commission_-photo-u2?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

Whether or not travelers or Denver locals subscribe to the theories that abound about the airport, there is no denying the inherent darkness apparently surrounding each piece of suspicious artwork. Every mural, statue, and floor inlay is considerably creepier than your run-of-the-mill airport art. At the very least, you may have to wonder: What does the art in the Denver International Airport mean?Photo: The Denver International Airport is rife with Freemasonry symbols. The Masonic capstone in the Jeppesen Terminal is shrouded in conspiracy. First of all, it is engraved with the famous square and compass symbol of Freemasonry and mentions two of the main lodges in Colorado. Also, when the date of the dedication is added together (1+9+1+9+9+4 ) it equals 33, a particularly significant number to Freemasons.

![Image 2](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762520/original/the-blue-mustang-photo-u2?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

The stone is also dedicated to the \
which theorists suggest is a reference to the Nazi group that called themselves the \
is actually the name of a group of businesses who wanted to create a \
airport. Even skeptics note, however, that there is no other evidence a group called \

ever existed. \nPhoto: The Blue Mustang statue looming outside the Denver International Airport attracts plenty of attention - and not all of it is good. During its construction, a piece of the statue's head fell on its creator, Luis Jimémenez, and ended him. This bad omen has led many conspiracy theorists to believe that the mustang is cursed, also landing it the unfortunate nickname \

![Image 3](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762522/original/the-statue-of-anubis-photo-u1?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

Conspiracy theorist William Tapley believes that the statue also holds deep phallic symbolism, and that the mustang, in general, is \

Both that imagery and its ominous connections have led some people to speculate that Blucifer will eventually bring about the apocalypse by transporting one of the four horsemen to Earth. 
Photo: The last thing anyone wants to see upon entering an airport is a statue of the Egyptian god of death, Anubis. But when the King Tut exhibit passed through the Denver Art Museum in 2010, so did a statue of a man with the head of a jackal.

![Image 4](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762540/original/the-suitcase-gargoyle-might-be-a-fallen-angel-or-demon-photo-u3?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

Residents noted the symbolism of Anubis and they weren't happy. Millie Lieberman spoke to the Denver Post, saying: \

While the symbolism Lieberman is alluding to is partially correct, the skin of Anubis also represents the fertile soil of Nile.
Photo: In one section of the airport there's a statue of a gargoyle coming out of a suitcase. It's a cheeky nod to the tradition of gargoyles being used to scare away evil spirits, but some theorists believe there's something evil in the symbolism. Blogger L.A. Marzulli believes the statue is actually a demon or a fallen angel that's glaring over travelers near the baggage carousel: 

![Image 5](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762526/original/_in-peace-and-harmony-with-nature_-references-the-end-of-the-world-photo-u4?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

It is an open suitcase but the contents are not clothes! It is a winged creature with horns and a tail! Is it a depiction of a fallen angel? Has it been hiding in some unfortunate man or woman's suitcase? A bigger question for me is what is this \

doing at the Denver airport?

![Image 6](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762525/original/_children-of-the-world-dream-of-peace_-symbolizes-one-world-prevailing-over-war-photo-u3?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

Photo: One of the airport's murals, In Peace and Harmony with Nature, contains a dense collection of symbolism that reflects anything but peace and harmony. The first part of the mural shows a group of children around a group of extinct plants and animals as a fire rages behind them, engulfing a forest and a city. The city on fire has been retouched multiple times over the years, and its strange color recalls a chemical strike. If you look closely, one of the children is holding a Mayan tablet, a possible reference to the end of the world.

![Image 7](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762542/original/_children-of-the-world-dream-of-peace_-also-depicts-a-malicious-soldier_-photo-u2?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

The mural's artist, Leo Tanguma, says his piece represents the destruction of the environment and later the unification of humanity. 
Photo: Children of the World Dream of Peace is a two-part mural depicting the children \

The mural features children from across the world dressed in traditional folk costumes wrapping weapons in flags.

![Image 8](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762826/original/the-black-sun-in-the-great-hall-resembles-art-symbolizing-the-new-world-order-photo-u3?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

According to conspiracy theorists, this part of the mural represents people giving up their national identities in an attempt to create peace and liberation. In fact, some of the faces in the painting are actual children from Denver who perished due to gang conflict while the mural was being commissioned. 
Photo: While the first half of Children of the World Dream of Peace depicts a group of children from across the world joining together, the second half reveals a militaristic display of a figure dressed in a uniform that recalls the SS, using a massive scimitar to stab a dove. The soldier is surrounded by a group of parents crying for their deceased children and the rubble of a toppled building.

![Image 9](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762530/original/a-dedication-to-colorado_s-gold-mining-past-hints-at-a-sinister-parallel-photo-u2?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

The Vigilant Citizen points out that the scimitar is an official symbol of the Freemasons.
Photo: A lesser known piece of symbolism in the DIA is an inlay in the Great Hall, an open space on level five. The floor features a series of concentric circles, each with a large black dot in the center. It's believed they represent the \

![Image 10](https://imgix.ranker.com/user_node_img/50089/1001762553/original/the-runway-resembles-a-swastika-photo-u2?auto=format&q=60&fit=crop&fm=pjpg&dpr=2&w=500)

No one knows exactly where this symbol comes from, but many in the Third Reich used it as a personal rune to represent triumph and the unity of their New World Order. 
Photo: One floor inlay at the Denver Airport shows the periodic symbols for gold and silver, Au and Ag, in a mining cart. On the surface, this appears to be a nod to Colorado's rich gold rush history. However, many conspiracy theorists believe this piece of art is far more nefarious.

The Au-Ag symbols can also stand for the Austrian Antigen, a strain of the hepatitis B virus supposedly discovered by one of the airport's sponsors, although the connection between the researcher and the airport has not been proven. Theorists believe it is possible the symbol is meant to warn members of the New World Order that a dangerous strain of the virus will be released to reduce Earth's population. 
Photo: It has not gone unnoticed that the DIA's runways are shaped like a swastika. The symbol has a long history that predates its most infamous connections to one of the darkest periods in the world's history. Conspiracy theorists still believe, however, that the swastika in the runways is intended to symbolize the coming of the New World Order.

It might be important to note that aviation experts suggest the DIA's runway design is actually one of the most efficient for multi-runway airports.
Did you read that article that linked so-and-so to that guy from the thing? Or see the video about how this is the same as that? Come on, let's weave some tangled webs!

body.title: Cultural activity at the Zoo.
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfUkNwtT8bgBLPEM1KcU6DwqHGjFGrVoaBuYoZMz5Cehe/1779742828914.jpg)


Greetings to all my writer friends, photographers, and people who travel the world to bring their best images to the @worldmappin community. Today, like many of you, I bring you a story to tell, especially with my images.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSQP3UAWykBXrRa4AJQPcJMDuGb7Cr24C14JxhgRK7kRH/1779742893966.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbD6WgGrGe4BHfz5PmfjY8dNzTKmyuzJRrukiV82cMuyz/1779742894111.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmazZvxB1uJQBj9AZwvtH9xJ8ppVgZx9j6T2qvYfAa8C9V/1779742894234.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmakYse25bPMi2XBuXERfUSA1j9JDkJiAcZHpeERkYFfbD/1779742894376.jpg)


A few weeks ago, at the zoo in my city of Ciego de Ávila, located in the center of the island of Cuba, a large cultural activity was held for the enjoyment of children. As usual, the day chosen to gladden souls and fill people's faces with smiles is Saturday. I work at this place, and my role is to take many photographs to promote the work that is done there, which is not only with children but also with the animals and with other institutions that use it, such as schools and nursing homes.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb9VQhr4hqKL4LwauNNmurcNssRyvuDCb2S8Sgy2gdSHT/1779742958275.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRJx3jHAKgEnnfToicRft2Cvdrxrd3UGPsTQqHvBrxkyk/1779742958433.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmciY8k1Av4hDKJ2TFhc2BfLvsva6Sb6hDa3amgkACG7kV/1779742958555.jpg)


On this day I'm telling you about, a group of children of different ages who belong to the Polichinela theater group visited the zoo. This is a company with a lot of prestige within the performing arts in the province, who visit schools and other institutions every day bringing joy to those who enjoy their performances.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWN23Vn1vYnEpvW9N5qrRa1WS3cCFsn3HWw3UDY1BHeVw/1779743024668.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbt4bCzB9vA2VNJdUBF2hBPTqzX3MDbDXYNaep7J1N77K/1779743024810.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaibmqhMhDtxbCz8GnVFFCQqcNmvECA23NbqL9x4x2R96/1779743024934.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdSMFWkiXSp7QPKY9tLXupZhsz1MBxhE2VxLnGhayUJ5v/1779743025092.jpg)

The activity began with the youngest children who wore colorful costumes and danced to the rhythm of a rich Cuban son, typical of our culture. This was followed by a unique performance by the group's director, who demonstrated her skill in handling a puppet. This moment was very fun for the youngest children present.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma6CoyB189LUrTqWfb86F6642NjTqvsmkG95nqQtjv7qS/1779743075336.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeJmbAMvmS7obHrAjn3c8oTXVvtB2QTH9kitNnZerxNz8/1779743075454.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTAsuVudemU6kzsXRwgXkxc52Bps82eSHKQMu9J8zdnZw/1779743075572.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWkUhhiR2R2esZRgpdt8AYLte1GdKXPEsMHDopbh8s1h7/1779743075694.jpg)


While the puppet moved around the stage, the children took the opportunity to change their clothes, and a few minutes later they formed a magnificent choir where the voices of those talented children sang several songs together.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRU4EP6NwcnNFdwTe39Mf3J5cZg34Jxnc1R8rph2iggoX/1779743182793.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmULN8uWEbNGmY71yVojcHmSBrG4PhMsgXBtkeMT3cQn3c/1779743182927.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfVQg9Woha9HwE55vs6xUCSLquzFhhCN56iyd8TJ3zDNK/1779743183034.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme3o5vQrimoyVVeg4xuBs9YS1cisumQ92zqbiFSfwbuwT/1779743183157.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWQEG1N7hW2JSucjPwAxYrAveTany6N8HShcMVKVTuNsM/1779743183275.jpg)



And to end the cultural day, the older children arrived and danced under the shadows of the columns that were projected above them, providing a special opportunity to take some photographs.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQzzsdRiBN43tbCGrmF4WAWBPA2EmjjgNt2hGzmSJvZoW/1779743257228.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQk9yvoXdngQ9gcP366i3RhXhMtP9uGyrt2YunXokPCfR/1779743257375.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZtWdbHzNWQRXPsAG1tCMEKk3DBFABQqsE1MNdDAd74xb/1779743257482.jpg)

The activity ended at noon just as the sun was shining brightly. We all went to the ice cream shop where we enjoyed ourselves and quenched our thirst after that unforgettable moment. Thanks to everyone for reading, greetings and until the next post.

body.title: Remember the fallen….
body.body: Afternoon everyone…. Happy Memorial Day everyone, especially those that have served us! As I write this post the rain is just about getting ready to end. But the damage is done…. They have cancelled the yearly parade in town, due to the amount of standing water everywhere from three straight days of rain. Plus it was still raining at the time the parade was supposed to start. I am writing this post prior to leaving for a barbecue at my girlfriend’s house. I’m responsible for making the antipasta and dressing. So I’ll be doing that right after this. I’m surprising them with a caprese salad as well. I bought a rather large ball of handmade fresh mozzarella yesterday from the Italian market and it seems like a waste not to use it all. My antipasta is a traditional style like my uncle always did for any holiday. A base is of romaine cut up, with a little mescaline greens, vine ripe tomatoes, shaved red onion, green and black olives, roasted red peppers (which I did yesterday), salami, ham and fresh mozzarella. The dressing is both red and balsamic vinegar, fresh basil finely chopped, three cloves of garlic, half a shallot, salt and peeper and a teaspoon of raw honey. Hope everyone has a great day. Remember those that have served us. My entire family up until my brother and I has served. Several saw and engaged in war. Luckily they all made it home alive. Many didn’t. Remember them…

***The young woman's eyes peek out from behind an autumn leaf. Her inquisitive gaze questions us, as if she believes we're hiding something. What she doesn't know is that we're just as intrigued as she is.*** Los ojos de la joven asoman detrás de una hoja de otoño. Su mirada inquisitiva nos interroga, como si creyera que guardamos algún secreto. Lo que ella no sabe es que nosotros estamos tan intrigados como ella.

body.title: Film Review: Elite Squad (Tropa de Elite, 2007)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/tGb044NgQYQJr58fta5O3OB6SpQ.jpg)


The opening decades of the 21st Century have proven to be a golden age for Brazilian cinema, a period during which the nation’s film industry shed its reliance on the telenovela format and began to vie for serious attention on the world stage. This resurgence was not merely a matter of statistical increase, though the number of films receiving international acclaim and securing prestigious awards did rise significantly. More importantly, Brazil began producing works that penetrated global popular culture, spawning sequels, launching transnational careers, and achieving a level of commercial success that few national cinemas can match. Among the list of films that successfully bridged the gap between arthouse prestige and commercial viability, *Elite Squad* stands out as a formidable anomaly, a cinematic achievement that few Brazilian films have been able to replicate. 

Somewhat unsurprisingly, the enduring success of *Elite Squad* stems from its refusal to play the game of the \

directors who populate the international festival circuit. It is not a self-indulgent, politically charged drama that relies on snobbish critics to validate its worth through obscure themes. Instead, the film is a pure genre piece, a crime action thriller that delivers visceral excitement with a relentless kinetic energy. It understands the mechanics of storytelling and the audience's desire for tension and spectacle, eschewing pretension in favour of raw, unfiltered narrative propulsion. Yet, this genre classification does not diminish its sophistication; rather, it enhances it, grounding its high-octane action in a narrative structure that is both gripping and deeply rooted in reality.

The film's foundation is built upon a true story, one that lends it a documentary-like authenticity. It is based on the 2006 eponymous book co-written by André Batista and Rodrigo Pimentel, two veterans of BOPE – the Special Operations Battalion of the State of Rio de Janeiro – and the prominent sociologist Luiz Eduardo Soares. This collaboration between active-duty law enforcement and a sociologist provides the script with a dual perspective: the gritty, tactical reality of the streets and the broader sociological analysis of the favelas. The result is a film that feels less like a Hollywood fabrication and more like a captured slice of history, albeit one polished for dramatic effect.

The plot unfolds in Rio de Janeiro in 1997, shortly before the visit of Pope John Paul II. The visit requires a level of security that the city's regular police force cannot provide, leading to orders for a security sweep of the notorious favelas to deal with heavily armed drug dealing gangs with extreme prejudice. At the centre of this operation is Captain Nascimento (Wagner Moura). Nascimento is a man of action, hardened by years of violence, but he is also a man with a personal crisis: he has learned that his wife is pregnant and wants a transfer to a desk job. However, before he can leave the front lines, he must find a worthy successor within the force who can take over his responsibilities.

The opportunity for this succession arises when BOPE is called to intervene in an extremely violent and bloody confrontation. It occurs during a meeting between local drug dealers and a group of military policemen led by Captain Fábio Barbosa (Milhelm Cortaz). This conflict is deeply entrenched in personal and political rivalry; Barbosa has stolen money from Oliveira (Marcello Valle), his rival and superior, and the meeting is likely a trap. To protect himself, Barbosa brings two fresh recruits—Neto Gouveia (Caio Junquiera) and André Matias (André Ramiro)—armed with a sniper rifle. BOPE, utilising their superior firepower, training, and tactical doctrine, ends the fight decisively. Nascimento, observing the competence of the recruits in the heat of battle, offers them the chance to apply for the BOPE. After months of gruelling jungle training where many candidates fail, Neto and Matias succeed and are officially inducted into the elite unit.

For Matias, the situation is noticeably more complicated. Unlike Neto, who is a simple soldier, Matias balances his life as a BOPE operator with his studies at university, where he is pursuing a law degree. It is here that he meets Maria, a student from a middle-class background. A romance blossoms, but it is a romance built on a delicate foundation of secrecy and social friction. Matias is very careful not to mention his day job to Maria because his colleagues—along with Maria and their friends—tend to be liberals from the middle and upper classes who despise the police. They use marijuana, belong to NGOs that help children from the favelas, and view the police with a mixture of pity and suspicion. This class dynamic creates a tension that permeates Matias's life, forcing him to hide his profession from the person he loves.

This social friction explodes when the gang led by the ruthless Baiano (Fábio Lago) becomes involved. Baiano confronts the students about Matias being a policeman and, driven by the need for revenge after people from his community were killed in a previous incident, he organises an ambush. The ambuscade is successful, and Neto is killed. The tragedy weighs heavily on the BOPE unit. When Baiano learns that Neto had a BOPE tattoo, he goes into hiding, fearing Nascimento’s retribution. Nascimento tracks Baiano down, engages him in a brutal confrontation, and wounds him. In the film's final, symbolic scene, Matias takes a fatal shot, effectively taking Nascimento’s place and ending his own duality, choosing his brotherhood and his mission over his civilian life.

The director, José Padilha, had already become famous in Brazil thanks to his award-winning documentary *Bus 174*, which dedicated itself to the infamous 2000 bus hijacking in Rio de Janeiro. While researching the film, Padilha was introduced to the various characters in the favelas, but crucially, he was also introduced to the policemen and the BOPE. This exposure heavily influenced *Elite Squad*, his live-action debut. Padilha brings the same observational eye he used in the documentary to this fictionalised account, grounding the hyper-kinetic action in a lived-in reality that feels terrifyingly plausible.

*Elite Squad* is interesting not only because of its credentials as an action film but because of its unique and uncompromising approach towards the issue of crime and violence in the favelas. This approach is completely opposite to that espoused by many of the world's film critics, who tend to be composed of \

who view the favelas solely through the lens of victimhood and systemic oppression. Instead of using the perspective of the criminal or the impoverished people, *Elite Squad* adopts the perspective of the policemen. Padilha does not evade the issue of widespread corruption within the police ranks; indeed, it is a central theme. However, BOPE is portrayed not as a force for good in a romantic sense, but as a brutal and efficient crime-fighting tool.

Nascimento's methods of dealing with the favelas look more like penal expeditions than attempts to actually enforce the law. The film does not view Nascimento's heavy-handed methods—which include torture and extrajudicial killings—as problematic or morally ambiguous. Instead, at worst, these human rights abuses are portrayed as a necessary evil in the fight against something far worse: the chaos and violence of the drug gangs. It is a grim, transactional view of law and order that prioritises the preservation of the state's authority over the niceties of human rights.

Padilha didn't win many friends in the world's liberal and progressive circles by showing that those who are supposed to care about human rights—the middle and upper-class activists and intellectuals—are often hypocrites. They use the favelas as a backdrop for their own moral posturing, their NGO work often serving their own career advancement rather than effecting real change. This ideological clash might explain why the film was greeted with a colder reception by critics in the West, despite its massive popularity among general audiences. In Brazil, the film became a massive hit, breaking box office records despite a mass internet leak shortly before its premiere. It was eventually crowned with the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival in 2008, a prestigious accolade that recognized its artistic merit, even if it baffled some Western critics who were uncomfortable with its unapologetic stance.

Part of the film's brilliance lies in Padilha's clever direction, which handles a complicated plot with a great sense of rhythm. The editing is quick and comprehensive, transitioning seamlessly between scenes of action. The acting is brilliant across the board, but especially by Wagner Moura, whose portrayal of Nascimento is a masterclass in gritty character acting. Moura imbues the Captain with a weary authority that makes his brutality feel earned rather than gratuitous. André Ramiro also delivers a strong performance as Matias, capturing the internal conflict of a man torn between two worlds. The film also benefits from an ironic voiceover narration that helps with exposition without feeling clunky. Furthermore, the music plays a crucial role; the upbeat, catchy tune \

became an anthem for the film, merging the rhythm of hip-hop with the sound of gunfire, perfectly encapsulating the film's unique aesthetic.\n\nThe film became immensely popular not only in Brazil but across the rest of the world. This global resonance speaks to the universality of the themes it tackles. Many countries around the world face the same problems as those depicted in the film—urban decay, gang warfare, and the failure of state institutions to protect their citizens. In these contexts, the BOPE represents a simple but brutal solution that people can understand and, perhaps, envy. The concept of the \

has become a popular synonym for swift, uncompromising justice in the face of chaos.

In 2010, Padilha directed the sequel, *Elite Squad II: Enemy Within*, which continued to explore the political and social landscape of Rio with equal intensity. The success of the first film paved the way for significant career opportunities for both Padilha and Moura. Later, the two reunited on the set of *Narcos*, one of the most popular TV series of its time. This reunion was not accidental; it was the direct result of the credibility and international recognition that *Elite Squad* provided. It proved that Brazilian cinema could not only tell its own stories but could also tell them in a way that resonated globally, challenging the established norms of Hollywood and international film criticism alike.


RATING: 8/10 (+++)

body.title: Big Catch on Little Critters Day - My Actifit Report Card: May 25th, 2026
body.body:
<center>

### Welcome to  
## ***Liquid Eye’s*** Actifit Blog

# Monday ☀️ 16523

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/F527D1B2-65AF-4D80-96E7-EEB7FA2B47931779743511.107469) 

It was nice and warm again this morning, over 10 degrees, but windier, so a bit more refreshing. Hopped on my bike and headed to Plötzensee. The tendons in my foot are a bit annoying, but they don’t really hurt. Once at the lake, I started interval walking and listened to the concert of our feathered friends. As I was parking my bike, a stowaway fell off my shoulder, and it was clear: today is “Little Critters Day.” And sure enough, there were plenty of critters to be found, including a certain species I’d been on the lookout for a long time but had never managed to get in front of my lens: the caterpillars of the actually quite dangerous oak processionary moth, whose fine stinging hairs can cause skin irritation and even breathing problems. They’re the stars of the show today, of course. Spoiler alert: there are no photos of spiders.

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/F527D1B2-65AF-4D80-96E7-EEB7FA2B47931779743523.475154) 

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/F527D1B2-65AF-4D80-96E7-EEB7FA2B47931779743525.634558) 

Wieder gut warm heute Morgen bei über 10 Grad, aber mehr Wind, also etwas erfrischender. Ab aufs Rad und los zum Plötzensee. Die Sehnen im Fuß nerven etwas, aber schmerzen nicht richtig. An der Plötze dann los mit Intervall-Walking und dem Konzert der Gefiederten Freunde gelauscht. Beim Parken des Rads fiel mir ein blinder Passagier von der Schulter, und damit war klar, heute ist „Little Critters Day“. Dementsprechend bot sich tatsächlich auch so einiges an Critters an, inklusive einer bestimmten Spezies, nach der ich schon lange Ausschau hielt, aber noch nie vor die Linse bekam, die Raupen des sogar recht gefährlichen Eichenprozessionsspinner dessen feine Brandhaare Hautreizungen und auch Atemprobleme auslösen können. Die sind heute natürlich die Stars. Spoileralarm, es sind keine Fotos von Spinnen dabei.

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/F527D1B2-65AF-4D80-96E7-EEB7FA2B47931779743527.781142)

The Technical Picture Is Recovering

body.title: Hope: that “ally” that can also betray us 🤔 [Eng+Spa] La esperanza: ese “aliado” que también puede traicionarnos 🤔
body.body:
* * *

* * *

(Versión en español más abajo).
-------------------------------

* * *

* * *

Recently, reading and talking with my friend @emiliorios, I kept thinking about an idea that seems simple... but it is not so simple: **hope can save us... or condemn us**.

And yes, it sounds dramatic 😅, but come with me for a moment.

Pandora didn't let everything out. 🏺
-------------------------------------

We all remember (more or less) the Greek myth of Pandora's box. That story where all the evils of the world are released: diseases, pain, suffering... everything unpleasant that we know today.

But there is a curious detail that is sometimes overlooked: **hope did not escape with the others**.

Some versions say that she was trapped. Others suggest something more disturbing: that it was there, in the background, as a kind of “last letter” or \
\n\nImagine this like a movie scene: all the demons now free, chaos unleashed... and in the background, a figure who promises to help, who says he can _\
_ Her name: **Hope**. It sounds nice… but also suspicious. 😏

>Image source. (Pandora and her box)

Without hope we don't live... but with too much, neither. --------------------------------------------------------- This is where the paradox appears. * **Without hope**, everything weighs more. Life becomes an impossible slope. Every problem seems final. Depression lurks. Without that little “maybe tomorrow,” we simply stop moving forward. * **But with too much misplaced hope**, we enter another type of hell. A quieter one... more personal... crueler. It's like those stories we see in series or movies —think _Breaking Bad_, _BoJack Horseman_, or even _Black Mirror_— where the characters cling to an illusion that clearly isn't going to turn out well... and yet they continue. Because _“it has to improve”_, right? Spoiler: it doesn't always get better. 😐 When hope turns into blindness ------------------------------ I remember a real case, one of those that seem taken from a police chronicle. A relationship marked by violence. Promises of change. Moments of regret. And then… the same thing again. The victim was still there, sustained by an almost 'heroic hope': _“it's going to change… everything is going to get better…”_ But it wasn't hope... it was a trap. The outcome was fatal. The kind that ends up in the Events section, with headlines that one would prefer to never read. That's where hope stops being a virtue... and becomes **dangerous blindness**. Hope with your feet on the ground. 🌱 ------------------------------------- So what do we do? Do we stop expecting good things? No. That's not it either. The key is something much more difficult (and much more human): **_Have a hope that does not ignore reality_**. A hope that: * It drives us to act, not to stay still. * Help us build, not justify the unjustifiable. * It allows us to change course when something is not working. Because yes... sometimes you have to accept something uncomfortable: 👉 **Not everything can be saved.** 👉 **Not every goal is possible.** 👉 **Not every story has a happy ending.** And that is not defeat. It is lucidity.

>Image source. (Classic poster about the opening of Pandora's Box)

Know when to let go 🕊️ ----------------------- Perhaps one of the most difficult—and most necessary—acts is this: **_Give up a useless hope_**. Not because of weakness. But for survival. As in many classic stories—from Greek myths to modern cinema—true character growth occurs when you stop chasing a mirage and start seeing things as they are. Sometimes, the best decision is not to insist... It is letting go. And look for a different path. * * * In the end… ----------- #Hope is necessary. Without it, we sink. But you also need limits. Because when it overflows, it can drag us down with it. Maybe Pandora didn't let out hope by accident... Perhaps she knew that, in complete freedom, she would be as dangerous as any other demon. And we, meanwhile, continue learning to use it without it using us. 😊 * * * * * *

> (English version above). ------------------------ * * * * * * La esperanza: ese “aliado” que también puede traicionarnos 🤔 ============================================================= Hace poco, leyendo y comentando con el amigo @emiliorios, me quedé dándole vueltas a una idea que parece simple… pero no lo es tanto: **la esperanza puede salvarnos… o condenarnos**. Y sí, suena dramático 😅, pero acompáñame un momento para explicar la idea. Pandora no dejó salir todo 🏺 ----------------------------- Todos recordamos (más o menos) el mito griego de la caja de Pandora. Esa historia donde se liberan todos los males del mundo: enfermedades, dolor, sufrimiento… todo lo desagradable que hoy conocemos. Pero hay un detalle curioso que a veces se pasa por alto: **la esperanza no escapó con los demás**. Algunas versiones dicen que quedó atrapada. Otras sugieren algo más inquietante: que estaba allí, al fondo, como una especie de “última carta”. Imagina esto como una escena de película: todos los demonios ya libres, el caos desatado… y en el fondo, una figura que promete ayudar, que dice que puede “arreglarlo todo”. Su nombre: **Esperanza**. Suena bonito… pero también sospechoso. 😏

>Fuente de la imagen. Pandora y su caja.

Sin esperanza no vivimos… pero con demasiada, tampoco. ------------------------------------------------------ Aquí es donde aparece la paradoja. * **Sin esperanza**, todo pesa más. La vida se vuelve una cuesta imposible. Cada problema parece definitivo. La depresión acecha. Sin ese pequeño “quizás mañana”, simplemente dejamos de avanzar. * **Pero con demasiada esperanza mal puesta**, entramos en otro tipo de infierno. Uno más silencioso… más personal… más cruel. Es como esas historias que vemos en series o películas —piensa en _Breaking Bad_, _BoJack Horseman_ o incluso _Black Mirror_— donde los personajes se aferran a una ilusión que claramente no va a salir bien… y aun así siguen. Porque _“tiene que mejorar”_, ¿no? Spoiler: no siempre mejora. 😐 Cuando la esperanza se vuelve ceguera ------------------------------------- Recuerdo un caso real, de esos que parecen sacados de una crónica policial. Una relación marcada por la violencia. Promesas de cambio. Momentos de arrepentimiento. Y luego… lo mismo otra vez. La víctima seguía allí, sostenida por una esperanza casi heroica: _“_Va _a cambiar… todo va a mejorar…”_ Pero no era esperanza… era una trampa. El desenlace fue fatal. De esos que terminan en la sección de Sucesos, con titulares que uno preferiría no leer nunca. Ahí es donde la esperanza deja de ser virtud… y se convierte en **ceguera peligrosa**. Esperanza con los pies en la tierra 🌱 -------------------------------------- Entonces, ¿qué hacemos? ¿Dejamos de esperar cosas buenas? No. Tampoco es eso. La clave está en algo mucho más difícil (y mucho más humano): **_Tener una esperanza que no ignore la realidad_**. Una esperanza que: * Nos impulsa a actuar, no a quedarnos quietos. * Nos ayude a construir, no a justificar lo injustificable. * Nos permite cambiar de rumbo cuando algo no funciona. Porque sí… a veces hay que aceptar algo incómodo: 👉 **No todo se puede salvar.** 👉 **No toda meta es posible.** 👉 **No toda historia tiene final feliz.** Y eso no es derrota. Es lucidez.

>Fuente de la imagen. (Lámina clásica sobre la apertura de la 'Caja de Pandora')

Saber cuándo soltar 🕊️ ----------------------- Quizás uno de los actos más difíciles —y más necesarios— es este: **_Renunciar a una esperanza inútil_**. No por debilidad. Sino por supervivencia. Como en muchas historias clásicas —desde los mitos griegos hasta el cine moderno—, el verdadero crecimiento del personaje ocurre cuando deja de perseguir un espejismo y empieza a ver las cosas como son. A veces, la mejor decisión no es insistir… Es soltar. Y buscar un camino distinto. * * * Al final… --------- La esperanza es necesaria. Sin ella, nos hundimos. Pero también necesita límites. Porque cuando se desborda, puede arrastrarnos con ella. Tal vez Pandora no dejó salir la #esperanza por accidente… Tal vez sabía que, en libertad total, sería tan peligrosa como cualquier otro demonio. Y nosotros, mientras tanto, seguimos aprendiendo a usarla sin que nos use a nosotros. 😊 * * * * * * #tribe #community #lifestyle #thoughts #pandorabox #pandora #cajadepandora #pensamientos #reflexiones * * *

body.title: The discipline of my choice
body.body:
Greetings!

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVDW8iEQihqtTpt6TzjEx3hKp9y6d5Ws947fyGAFT4vit/1779743154126.jpg)

If discipline is lacking in the life of a human, then indiscipline will be the other day.  It is the indiscipline in the life of the individuals today that has brought our society to this state and stage we have found ourselves in the country. 

Having talked about discipline and its effect  on society extensively, I would like to delve into the topic of the prompt which is all about, “Physical Discipline.”

To start with, I would say that physical discipline is good and also the other discipline which is not physical is not bad either.  However, one thing I want us to know is that physical discipline has really helped a lot, especially in the past where children or wards are being disciplined or punished physically through beating and all forms of other punishment.

Then our society was in order as natural discipline in the form of fear was being instilled in the heart of the younger ones in the society. Most of us if not for the mode of punishment used for us back then wouldn't have been useful as we have been now to our society. 

Although, the creation of fear through the use of corporal punishment and beating to me back then wasn't good enough as this unnecessary creation of fear had resulted in destroying the physical body of  many of us.

The scars of the beating we received back then can still be seen in our body. Not only that, the scars of corporal punishment can still be felt as it was boldly inscribed on the heart of some of us and that's why some people still find it difficult to forgive and forget what their parents or guardians did to them when they were younger.

However, the physical discipline as the topic implies is still the best to me as it always helps to check the indiscipline of the majority of the children. Although, this punishment really had this kind of a negative effect on some children who would later turn out to be thugs and rogues on the street after they had fled home as a result of the corporal punishment being meted out on them by their parents.

Now coming down to the type of punishment being used today as a form or way of discipline a child, I would say it's another good way of instilling discipline in them, I mean the kids or the younger ones in the society and this is because, it's being done out of love and nothing else and the good news here is that, there's no physical assault or scar left in the physical body of a child nor in their heart and even at that, children are being corrected of their wrong doings which is an applause to this generation.

In conclusion, one thing I want us to know is that both forms of punishment are good, but the one with scar in the body or the heart is not as good as the one that comes with love.

This is my entry to week 219, episode 01 of the weekly featured contest in the Hive Learners community.

Thanks for reading.

body.title: After the Strong Rain and Flood, Our Backyard Garden Continues Growing Beautifully, Bringing Fresh Vegetables Daily
body.body:
![1000205265.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/48SqCJZ3rGYeK6nC5jL68W27PAiUANHrEVKSP3Mrxvh26FvEqYaWVMAcdkUKNJAAs4.jpg)


Hello my fellow gardeners! 

After many busy days in church, online work, and my responsibilities as a mom, I realized that I had not given enough time to my garden. For almost one week, I was not able to walk around and check my simple backyard garden. I missed it so much because I was used to visiting it every morning while drinking my coffee.


![1000205122.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23tvXmXdFLTKV6wAwmsRvWrAnFktQqzRCGjBtghoMzX7m1uiy7scKGxHVxUsjir72rtED.jpg)

The strong rains lately were almost like a storm. Since there is a small creek behind our house, the area became flooded because of the continuous rain. Honestly, I felt worried about my plants, thinking they might not survive. But when I finally had time to visit my garden again, I felt so happy and thankful because they were still alive and growing.

![1000205139.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23vsBnco5LPQwEEGkNVLN6Tn9sfKyVV8ayX21CxHkYGUABRrFamZrMbme18qx3oSPirjN.jpg)

Even though my backyard garden is simple, it helps me a lot. After our fiesta celebration, we already got tired of eating too much meat, so I decided to harvest some sweet potatoes and cucumber from the garden. It feels different and fulfilling when the food comes from your own backyard.

![1000205134.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23tvXrKhXA7MAjBDmwnMEWJvnrC48GozdFXpZzvSancbtPqTvHWHsZZ5eipBSJXz9CqNB.jpg)

![1000205132.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23u5vEFWvMaAJvsgpGXXkb31pTZJ3KWMH6aNBqCDZ2MopPQQbmHoNc8fPaGF59h5rWRfV.jpg)

![1000205143.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23tGyCoBh6Fp86o3KZreMRWatxikiyx68vYs95wHZxchtGxosHLPYhL7q9ZKacEQKBc7S.jpg)

I was also surprised to see that the beans seeds I had kept and set aside already started growing and are now ready to be planted. I had been looking for these seeds in our local agri supplies, but I could not find any. I even planned to order online, but it never happened because now I already have my own seedlings ready to grow.


![1000205144.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23vhwRKKZE7txp17aKkiJiypqiihjLXKAvQ8xQmBDdj12mdCMCPVmjUmXYZhcLoUDSKPm.jpg)

![1000205125.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wWpftq6Q4Q92scsKPi9frtHrMKWjaeseuacLa2riUBxeZfRy8D7kcNanG2yGJkza3MJ.jpg)


Another thing that made me smile was seeing my squash becoming healthier and stronger because of the rain. The plants are finally coming back to life. Little by little, I feel hopeful that someday I will harvest even more vegetables from this small space.


![1000205148.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uQNo9cwV8wHViNKzJ4cPCsNG71QanRp2CVr36KiTTme4JVVvAYNvYjqoZG4QarqPaSL.jpg)

Our calamansi tree is also starting to bear fruits again, and now we can already use them for our favorite dipping sauces. Simple things like this truly bring joy to my heart.


![1000205150.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23vhoDTrK2sr5WeS3JcY31WeJiWKYofKnxMV1F27QzvciREzj3tMtdfxVSfSupe3FNVr8.jpg)


Despite the heavy rain and my busy schedule, my garden remained alive. It reminded me that growth continues even during difficult and busy seasons of life.

Thank you for reading my story. These are my own pictures and my real experiences from my simple backyard garden. Have a nice day and keep growing wherever you are planted.

body.title: The Truth Behind Artificial Intelligence Is Finally Revealed
body.body: ![Geralt is the creator of this image/Source:  Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2021/11/04/06/24/ai-6767497_1280.jpg)\n\nAs I was surfing around on YouTube, I stumbled across a video that contained valuable information about artificial intelligence (\
).  Pam is an influencer who has a YouTube channel named \

and she did a video about how AI is being misused to post videos that misrepresent elderly people falling into conflicts with their own adult children. Here is her video below. Pam Warns That AI-Generated Videos Are Giving Elderly People Harmful Advice Meant To Alienate Them From Their Adult Children https://youtu.be/237CfL9gS04?si=bV_FsmDthUsrlVxT I find a large amount of wisdom to Pam's warnings about these AI-generated videos. I have noticed a whole slew of such videos that show AI-generated elderly people encouraging real elderly people to disinherit their adult children, even if their children are struggling financially due to no fault of their own. These AI-generated videos get me so angry that I have published articles urging every American to contact their elected officials to ask them to pass forced-heirship laws in their respective state jurisdictions here in the United States so that nobody will be able to cut their own children out of the will. There has been way too much child abuse and incest going on in our nation for decades, and abusive parents simply shouldn't have the right to disinherit their own kids if they are the ones who sabotaged their kids' lives in the first place and crippled them from being able to be financially prosperous. I've noticed this problem particularly with adult children from Generation X. Below is a video of a man from that generation who suffered violence at the hands of his parents. YouTuber The Semi-Retired Samurai Decided Not To Father Children To Break The Cycle Of Abuse In His Family https://youtu.be/Rsr-sZ_DEC4?si=dtqXIgt4XwbH04Ef The irony of this trend among Gen Xers is that many of them end up having to take care of their aging parents once their parents' health starts to break down regardless of whether or not they are estranged from them. What is so outrageous is that this same scenario could just as easily materialize if the parents were actually the ones to go no-contact with their adult children. Below is another video in which YouTuber The Semi-Retired Samurai talks about these same concerns. YouTuber The Semi-Retired Samurai Explains How No-Contact Adult Children Can End Up Caring For Their Aging Parents Anyway https://youtu.be/_bDIT2PvTuk?si=o1puNw2HFEEepvjE YouTuber The Semi-Retired Samurai's parents were baby boomers. Many people from his generation have parents from the Silent Generation, and they can be equally as disgraceful parents as baby boomers, if not worse. No generation appears to be immune from this situation. People from Generation Z and the Millennial Generation are confronting these same problems, although not in as large numbers at the current time in that many of them still have parents that are not yet elderly. The elephant in the room here is that if a parent beats or rapes their own child and then pushes that child away after that child reaches adulthood insofar as they become estranged, then that parent has unrealistic expectations in turning to that son or daughter to take care of them in old age. If that son or daughter caves in and does take care of them in old age, it should be completely illegal for that parent to cut that adult child out of their will. Also, you may have noticed that abusive parents always seem to live well into the mid-to-late nineties, if not into their hundreds. On the other hand, the kind, generous, loving parents always seem to die in their sixties. It's as though there is some kind of evil force hovering over all of us. Our nation has enough problems with poverty and homelessness. Someone who suffered any form of abuse at the hands of their parents is more likely than not to struggle financially throughout their adult life. Once their estranged parents want them to take care of them, perhaps their parents will have enough money so that their adult children don't have to worry about finances when they get saddled with that same responsibility. Nonetheless, taking care of an elderly parent is a great amount of responsibility in any event. It is particularly stressful if you are a man and you suck at cooking, because you can really begin to feel as though you're being absorbed into a never-ending prison sentence if you have to spend seven nights a week in the kitchen, dealing with all the aggravations and dangers of the stove and the oven. ![Geralt is the creator of this image/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2015/03/08/09/30/head-663997_1280.jpg) I don't know who is posting these AI-generated videos on YouTube advising elderly people to disinherit their children, but it needs to stop. Child abuse and incest are serious problems in our nation, and nobody needs to be encouraging abusive parents to disinherit the same people they victimized as children once those kids of theirs are adults and the parents are elderly. Then again, perhaps these AI-generated videos on YouTube are a wake-up call for all of us to contact our elected officials and get them to enact laws that would make it illegal for any parent to disinherit their children under any circumstances. I have an aunt who married into my family. She has stolen assets from other members of my family whenever the issue of inheritance has surfaced upon the death of any elderly family member. I don't claim this woman as my aunt. She is now in an assisted-living facility, and her mind is going on her. She isn't really old enough to have dementia or Alzheimer's diseases, but I guess that karma can be a real bummer. She certainly deserves whatever bad things come her way. Her mother disinherited her. I would never wish anything like that on my worst enemy. However, she was cruel to her sister. If she had treated her sister with greater respect, her sister probably would have split all the assets in half with her that she inherited from their mother. In any event, I still strongly believe that our nation needs forced heirship laws in every state jurisdiction. If you don't live in the United States as I do, then perhaps you live in a nation that has forced heirship laws; and if that is the case, then don't ever take those same laws for granted. In our nation, people have a way of finding out that their parents have disinherited them when those same people are in the worst of financial circumstances. **This article is copyright-protected.**
