title.title: COMENSANDO LA SEMANA CON UNA BUENA PIZZA-----STARTING THE WEEK WITH A GOOD PIZZA
title.body:
Buenos dias a todos hoy vamos a degustar una sabrosas piza cacera, asi que manos a la obra y para elaborar la masa  utilizamos harina, agua, levadura, sal, huevo, entonces colocamos en un volts, la harina, la abrimos un poco y le agregamos huevo, agua tibia , despues agregamos un poco de levadura y mesclamos todo muy bien, le vamos vertiendo de a poco el agua antes mencionada , previo le agregamos un poco de sal y comenzamos a mesclar todo, hasta que vaya tomando consistencia la misma, cuando esta dicha masa, la tapamos y dejamos que descanse un poco, para despues comenzar a armar lo que seria la piza.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/prm4031/23tvkbJiTxk527H4rAAsLcUyBsR6Wkb9GezF6VVuRNJ2pC2fc48MMCeDFZeJSozvErcMT.png)

La preparacion de la salsa como toda prepiza, morron bien picado, aceite de oliva, cebolla, condimentos varios, la verdad un manjar, la que luego va arriba de la piza, por eso la cebolla tiene que ser rehogada y morron en tiras, con bastante condimentos, utilizamos vastante cebolla, luego en el medio con tomate cortado en julianas y el otro costado con jamon cocido cortado en hebras, siempre todo arriba de la cebolla y para que quede mas exquisita le agregamos un poco de aceite de oliva.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR LEERME Y SEGUIRME.

TRADUCIDO AL INGLES

Good morning everyone, today we are going to taste a delicious homemade pizza, so let's get to work. To make the dough, we use flour, water, yeast, salt, and egg. First, we place the flour in a bowl, make a little well in the center, and add the egg and warm water. Then, we add a bit of yeast and mix everything very well. We gradually pour in the previously mentioned water, add a bit of salt, and start mixing everything until it reaches a consistent texture. Once the dough is ready, we cover it and let it rest for a bit before starting to shape the pizza.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/prm4031/23tvkbJiTxk527H4rAAsLcUyBsR6Wkb9GezF6VVuRNJ2pC2fc48MMCeDFZeJSoz

The preparation of the sauce, like any pizza prep, involves finely chopped bell pepper, olive oil, onion, various seasonings, truly a delicacy, which then goes on top of the pizza. That's why the onion needs to be sautéed and the bell pepper cut into strips, with plenty of seasonings. We use a lot of onion, then in the middle, sliced tomatoes, and on the other side, shredded cooked ham, always everything on top of the onion. To make it even more exquisite, we add a bit of olive oil.

Thank you very much for reading and following me.

title.title: I Keep Choosing \
Over the Life I Actually Want
title.body:
<div  class=text-justify>

If I am to compare the time I used in figuring out the prompts that connects more to my life right now, understanding the prompt I decided on, finding the right images that will relates to my response to the time I'm going to think through my life and give the response, it's way shorter.

While I was trying to understand the prompt and find images, my mind kept saying I should give up the prompt I've decided on... It all came from my second thought after the first thought had concluded on the best prompt to write on because it is what my life right now relates to.

![93b36320-0c94-4a02-88d2-576d9b706b48_20260525_082615_0000.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/23vsJF7gyLhBK3prNwtmFTist7fJqEzZCRWu8xgy6SaWcXFCqnQG2s8Ttzw8E7gYBQphp.jpg)

I'm starting this way to say, I love how thought-provoking these prompts are and that *\

*. So yeah, I decided to share a part of my life right now with the option about loops heh. For a while now, I've been learning and studying about my life, career path to choose and changing my mindset to relate better with myself and people around me. It's a journey that will not end until the end of my life, I believe so. But it's a journey with lots of loops that I'm holding on to. And from what I understand thought loops to be, they are the repetitive thoughts that keeps holding me back. Those things I keep thinking about again after I've decided on something, I've been able to find patterns with it and I've understood what will change when I let them go. ![6e5a750e-5a78-4784-89e1-e0dfa1e4bf01_20260525_082211_0000.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/23tva4zLHVgTnvQvHcvTVeYFqKaFmacLidwj65GCjZeg3FMfgcGaD34ZSuU45jrmDnNgG.jpg) The life I want is where I have this fire burning inside me, unfading excitement about something I am passionate about. A life where I speak what's in my mind clearly and considerably to the listener, a life where I manage my fears like a pro, a life where I am confident of the things I know. I want a life where I don't have to think too much about a decision to the extent of not taking action about it anymore. I want a life where I'll see myself as someone who can serve and make impact on people positively and to the delight of my creator and the universe. I want to attract good people, wealth and growth in all aspects. I've pictured my life in the future, I love it but one thing my mind knows very well and yet to apply right now is, I can live that life of my future now. Because I have only my present, not my future, the future it is yet to come. Embracing the moment and taking action right now is the goal. But then... ***The loops I am yet to release to think more clearly.*** ![74b5e6c8-63ca-42bd-bb92-a927d6ccbaa3_20260525_082512_0000.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/23uQp2ZxS2c4CFRiSYF4cEfY2jsFagkK4uweGSYFm1jEPGg31rcBUiVwiJ2Q7TqJWD4MZ.jpg) The loops that are holding me back from living the life that I want now are simple but weighing thoughts that I want to release, even though I keep holding on to them when a new day of opportunities comes. *“I’m not ready yet”, “I need to figure everything out first”, “What if I fail?”* Simply, I'm overthinking instead of taking action even when my first thoughts has given me lots of idea to work with until I have better ideas. It's a scary phase of my life because I know what's stopping me but no courage to overcome them or release them to think clearly to the live I want. A lot of thoughts are slowing down my growth but knowing them is a step I appreciate because I know I'll eventually get over them and grow into the life that will not just serve but impact others. **Images were taken and edited by me.** Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@merit.ahama/i-keep-choosing-not-yet-over-the-life-i-actually-want-eag)

title.body:
The 3% credit card interchange fee is a valid pain point, but the Bitcoin Lightning POS adoption faces a different friction: volatility. Even with Lightning's instant settlement, merchants need to convert BTC to fiat immediately to cover costs — and that adds a conversion step that the credit card system doesn't require.

The real competitor isn't credit cards. It's stablecoin payments on L2s. USDC on Lightning-compatible solutions or on Ethereum L2s gives merchants the same instant settlement with zero volatility risk. The question is which infrastructure reaches the terminal first.

Have you looked at how Strike's model handles the BTC-to-fiat conversion at point of sale? They've been running this playbook in El Salvador and the conversion latency is the key metric.

title.body:
The Taiwan chip dependency is one of those risks that everyone in the industry acknowledges but the financial system hasn't priced in. TSMC produces 90%+ of the world's advanced chips (sub-7nm). If the Strait becomes contested, the global economy faces a supply shock that makes COVID-era semiconductor shortages look minor.

What's interesting is the geography of the backup options. Intel's foundry push in Arizona, Samsung in Korea, and TSMC's own fabs in Japan and Arizona — but even combined, they cover maybe 15-20% of advanced node capacity by 2028. The diversification timeline doesn't match the risk timeline.

The question I keep coming back to: does the market eventually start pricing this risk into semi stocks, or is it one of those Black Swan events that stays theoretical until it isn't?

title.title: 📷 Sunset and Blue Hour in Panama City [EN/DE]
title.body:
![_DSC0352.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/travelshots/23xyV45cyrL6AMz6ZzswZsiQdXngB2FbfNA9aSUuSiph5wv55dBtn4BuZv9AQ5HWcM4nb.jpg)

Last month, I visited Central America for the first time in my life – Panama City, to be precise. The city’s impressive skyline, with its many unique skyscrapers, fascinated me just as much as the beautiful natural surroundings. The rainforest extends right into the heart of the metropolis. Unsurprisingly, the climate is correspondingly hot and tropical. It’s only towards evening that it becomes truly pleasant to be outside. And it was precisely this time of day that I used to take a few long exposures during the golden and blue hours. The two photos I’m showing you here were the ones I liked best in the end.

*Letzten Monat war ich zum ersten Mal in meinem Leben in Zentralamerika – genauer gesagt, in Panama City. Die beeindruckende Skyline der Stadt mit ihren vielen einzigartigen Wolkenkratzern faszinierte mich genauso wie die wunderschöne Natur. Der Regenwald ragt bis in das Zentrum der Metropole hinein. Entsprechend heiß und tropisch ist natürlich auch das Klima. Erst gegen Abend wird es wirklich angenehm, sich draußen aufzuhalten. Und genau diese Zeit nutzte ich, für ein paar Langzeitbelichtungen zur Goldenen und Blauen Stunde. Die beiden Bilder, die ich euch hier zeige, haben mir am Ende am besten gefallen.*

title.title: Reminiscing About a Time That Didn't Exist
title.body:
Sometimes I just let YouTube shuffle through an automatically generated playlist, presumably based on my typical listening habits and playlists.

Following on from yesterday's post, some music is just *evocative* and sinks me into the world of memories... something I believe happens to us more and more, as we age.

![0014-SunsetSilhouette.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/denmarkguy/23wMggN2AMvbGE4B81PuB1Gg3ABFjw5kMkbh8exwMQSZWLZQ6PbefSeXn2fyC36sUNtfa.jpg)

Anyways, a song came into rotation and it reminded me of my University days in the early 1980s. I remembered... oddly enough, what I *\

* was a slice of life I *didn't actually get to live,* like I was an outsider, looking in.

There's actually a name for it: *Anemoia.*

> *The longing for a time that didn't actually happen.*

We have an expression in Danish — *strøtanker* — which loosely translates as *\

* although that definition misses the vast majority of the deeper nuance, which often includes shades of sadness and ennui. 

*I arrived late for my own adulthood...*

![1140-Pacific.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/denmarkguy/245wFSQqRvWuEgzMLsuTb4yq2MUbcTonNUZkRWmpFuLQn6L29LNUymsgUzRkLqAzsaszR.jpg)

It's not something easily explained, but it is often experienced by kids who were forced to become adults early and missed part of the allegedly *\
* parts of being a teenager and young adult, but subsequently ended up *\

* by the time I was 15 and didn't arrive at University until age 20.5... and *then* started backfilling... *slowly.*

It's one of the reasons why I'm *chronologically* part of the Boomer generation, but *philosophically* feel far more like I belong to the leading edge of Gen-X, for example.

I identify with *\
* as being mostly the 1980s, even though it *\

* be the late 1960s and 1970s... but we never listened to music, so I have nothing but a void to relate to, there. As I listen to music nowadays, I don't even *like* the music of my *actual* childhood and youth.

![0800-Lake.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/denmarkguy/23r1gzANraYyrNhcnpvHKZPDexjTS26w6VbdEA6D3b4MQ7nGc5f3kmsoWWf5B1rtxuhXW.jpg)

Without a doubt, the rose-colored glasses of passing time are *\
* me about my experience of the mid-1980s... it was actually a really *difficult* time, and there was very little that was *\

* about it.

Besides, I was living in *Texas,* not *California,* the latter being a place I just *visited* many times and a place where it seemed like most of my friends were originally from. 

Maybe some of these memories — that aren't actual memories — are actually shades of *regret* about never having experienced what we *hoped* life would be. But does life *ever* live up to people's hopes and dreams?

Thanks for stopping by and have a great Memorial Day!

title.title: More Than Pieces on a Board
title.body: At first glance, this may look like a simple wooden chess board with a few pieces standing under warm sunlight. But chess has always been more than wood, squares, and pieces to me. Every game feels like a small journey. One move can create opportunities, while one mistake can completely change the story of the board. Sometimes you think you are winning, and suddenly your opponent finds a move you never expected.

/>  
Photo Credit: Daniel Stiel on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-wooden-chess-board-with-chess-pieces-on-it-hayc4n2dI-k)  
  

That is one of the reasons I enjoy chess. It teaches patience and reminds us that rushing often leads to mistakes. It also teaches us to think ahead because every action creates consequences.  
Looking at this position, I imagine two players sitting quietly, planning their next move while trying to read each other's minds. The board becomes a battlefield where strategy matters more than strength.  
In life, we also play similar games. We make choices, take risks, lose some battles, and learn from our mistakes. Just like chess, every move matters.

မိုးမရွာခင်က အိုက်လိုက် ပူလိုက်တာ လွန်ပါရော။ ဒါ‌ကြောင့် 
မိုးနဲ့ လေနဲ့များလာစေချင်ရဲ့။ ခြံဘေးက မြောင်း ရေလျှံ
စေချင်ရဲ့လို့ စိတ်မှာ အောင်းမေ့မိတာ။
ဦးမာဃနဲ့ ကိုယ်စိတ်ကူးကို တစ်ရာရာခိုင်နှုန်း
လိုက်လျောလိုက်ပုံများ သဘောကောင်းချက်။ 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma9YsD36EmYbN8DXwBujgrhfV1kzNmp3ZU9nijVKbUMDZ/image_7e518b0b_0fdc_4560_9202_ab6e55dc870c8024127420602861318.jpg)

ပူအိုက်သမို့ မိုးကိုမျှော်မိတာပေါ့။ မိုးရွာမယ်ဆိုလည်း
သဲသဲမဲမဲ ဝေါကနဲ့ ရွာချပြီး လေရော မိုးပါရွာစေချင်တာ။ 
လေကတော့ အအေးပေါ့ယုံပါလေ။
မုန်တိုင်းကဲ့သို့တော့ မတိုက်စေချင်ပါဘူး။
အပူတွေကို လွင့်စင်သွားယုံလေးပါပဲ။ မိုးက
ရွာတာ မိုးရေအတော်ပါသည်။ မိုးရေများပေသိ
မြေကြီးက ရေငတ်နေတာ အတော်ကြာသမို့
မြေကြီးပေါ်မှာ ရေအိုင်မရှိ‌သလောက်ပေ။
ထိုအပြင် ခြံဘေးရှိ ရေမြောင်းမှာပင် ရေများက
မရှိပေ။ 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUT8JDtWeqbMaw4LQBYjTDVF2jxyzu7qhJYiAKyAcimV4/image_275b1591_75fe_4b2f_b5f4_ff34785043d62348799011275906326.jpg)

မိုးရွာပြီး နောက်တနေ့မှာ အပူအနည်းငယ်သက်သာ
သွားသည်။ နောက်ရက်များမှာတော့ ပူအိုက်မြဲသာပင်။
ပူပူ အိုက်အိုက်၊ မိုးရွာချင်ရွာပါစေ ကိုယ်တွေကတော့
Hive မှာ ပိုစ့်တင်စာရေးရပေအုံးမည်။ Hive
ဈေး ဘယ်တော့များမှ တက်မည်မသိရသော်လည်း
တဖြည်းဖြည်းချင်း ဟိုက်ပါဝါများကိုတော့ စုနေရသည်။
ပုရွက်ဆိတ်များ အစာသယ်ယူစုသလို တရွေ့ရွေ့ပေါ့လေ။ 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQtfbfqZUZxvkpKaZo87Yqy5C7uHL4DpPM2yWWv7kmAj2/image_bf05b4f4_685c_43cc_a8e7_65054b31d7856609102063814772124.jpg)

ကွန်မန့်များကိုလည်း ပေးမရဖြစ်နေသည်။

title.body: Maybe it was psychological but I've been so depressed over the prospect I had to give up cheese, it's been a hard couple of months.  I like Mexican food and that usually entails a lot of cheese.  Though I discovered it doesn't taste half bad without it.  My son stops by tonight, he has a box with him.  I asked him what was in the box, he said chips and cheese.  I told him I can't have that.  He said it wasn't like normal chips and cheese, it was some cheese sauce, can't remember what he called it, think it started with a g.  I open the box and it had the sauce, meat, tomatoes and green peppers. I told him I'd try one.  Within minutes it's like I felt better than I had in months, lol.  I ate some more, still feelin' better than I have in months.  I'll have to look for that cheese you recommended.

title.title: Upcoming Seasonal Events and Festivals Happening in Fort Worth
title.body:
Fort Worth continues to grow as one of Texas’ most exciting destinations for entertainment, culture, and community celebrations. Throughout the year, the city hosts seasonal festivals, live performances, outdoor events, and cultural gatherings that bring residents and visitors together for memorable experiences.

Whether you enjoy food festivals, live music, local markets, or art-focused attractions, Fort Worth offers something exciting during every season.

At [What's Up Fort Worth](https://whatsupfortworth.com/), we’re passionate about helping locals stay informed about the latest happenings across the city. If you’re planning your next outing, here’s a look at some of the upcoming seasonal events and festival experiences that make Fort Worth such a vibrant place to explore.

## Spring Festivals and Outdoor Celebrations

Spring is one of the busiest seasons for outdoor entertainment in Fort Worth. Warmer temperatures and blooming parks create the perfect environment for festivals, concerts, and community gatherings.

Popular spring events often include:

*   Outdoor food festivals

*   Art fairs

*   Farmers markets

*   Live music performances

*   Family-friendly park events

Many spring festivals also showcase local artists and creative experiences connected to exhibits in Fort Worth and community art programs.

## Summer Concerts and Community Events

Summer brings an energetic atmosphere to Fort Worth with outdoor concerts, evening entertainment, and citywide celebrations taking place throughout the season.

Summer event highlights may include:

*   Outdoor movie nights

*   Rooftop music events

*   Cultural festivals

*   Family activity weekends

*   Food truck gatherings

Entertainment districts and public parks become popular destinations for residents looking to enjoy longer evenings and community activities.

## Seasonal Art Shows and Museum Experiences

Fort Worth’s arts and cultural scene continues to expand with rotating exhibitions, gallery events, and interactive experiences throughout the year.

Visitors interested in Fort Worth museum exhibits can often explore:

*   Contemporary art displays

*   Historical collections

*   Interactive family exhibits

*   Photography showcases

*   Traveling exhibitions

Many museums and galleries also participate in larger seasonal festivals and cultural celebrations happening around the city.

## Fall Festivals and Local Traditions

As temperatures begin to cool, Fort Worth transitions into a season filled with community fairs, cultural events, and outdoor celebrations that attract large crowds.

Fall festivals commonly feature:

*   Seasonal food vendors

*   Pumpkin patches

*   Harvest markets

*   Live entertainment

*   Arts and crafts fairs

This season is especially popular for families looking for weekend activities and festive community experiences.

## Winter Holiday Events and Celebrations

The holiday season transforms Fort Worth into a festive destination filled with lights, performances, and seasonal attractions.

Popular winter activities may include:

*   Holiday markets

*   Tree lighting ceremonies

*   Ice skating events

*   Seasonal theatre productions

*   Community parades

Many cultural venues also introduce special holiday-themed Fort Worth museum exhibits and interactive experiences during this time of year.

## Cultural Festivals and Community Gatherings

Fort Worth’s diverse community is reflected in the many cultural festivals held throughout the year. These celebrations allow visitors to experience music, dance, cuisine, and traditions from different backgrounds and communities.

Cultural events often include:

*   Traditional performances

*   Artisan vendors

*   Educational exhibits

*   Family activities

*   Live music and entertainment

body.title: I Lost Money Days Before My Birthday: How Scammers Use Your Desperation Against You.
body.body:
Scams are everywhere today, and if we are not very careful and watchful, we can fall for it. Especially online, where we kind of find it a little hard to tell what is true from what's false.



We now see various things online, ranging from fake investments platform, to ponzi sites, and a lot more. And it just seems this scammers are getting smarter by the day, cause most of us keeps falling for them, when we seem to have known their pattern, they come in another that's so real..and we fall again.



![1001067338.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23tv8ErKW1yxDGZPv5smMFUca43qcWznq9kQbTDV9RX5YSZrPrjaQ85p3nFohAbCeKisW.jpg)




The funniest part is, the economy is hard on everyone and we all are kind of finding a means to at least survive, that they knew as well, and they are making the best use of the desperations of people.



This year February, I also fell victim of one, here on hive. It was just a few days to my birthday. And even though the money involved is small, I felt it, because I was so so broke at that time. I blamed myself for it, I shouldn't have clicked on the link I didn't verify and ask others about, it promises some sort of rewards and I clicked. That particular experience has made me more careful about a lot of things, especially links. I no longer click on links anyhow, even if its coming from someone I knew.


And that's the thing about these online scammers, they don't just target people who are careless, they also know how to take advantage of trust, sites, emotions, and such... they just need to make it look like what you would have loved.



Sometimes last month, I heard people talking about a particular site, how they've invested in it and are cashing out of it. People patronized this site like, even secondary school students registered..and the rate at which people were cashing out and investing made more people believe in it.



Less than two weeks ago, it crashed, and w began hearing stories of those who invested in it, cashed out and invested more again, we heard of those who lost huge amounts and act as if they didn't even invest in it. I even heard about a man who usually helps people to get ram for festivals and he has collected millions on naira for this upcoming ileya festival(Eid celebration), he invested all of this money into the platform thinking it would triple in two weeks time, well before then the site stopped working.



![1001067344.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23tGXhYCtCevAbu6bqEZAGoLCrGW3ecJwaVb9pQNNsAu2KfNLiNpPGgbQuRkZNELizciN.jpg)




This issue isn't a small one, like it affects a lot of people, some victims of this things are in the hospital as I speak and some like the man who collected money for rams has fled the community already.


So, to avoid being scammed, we need to be wary of links. Verify a site very well before doing anything on it, don't trust all this get rid quick and quick money platforms. Also, don't share your sensitive information carelessly or litter it around, and make use of two factor authentication on all of your accounts, it goes a long way in helping.



Here's my advice, in as much as we all agree that we take risks and that life itself is a risk, I will like to add that its better to be careful and watchful as it is better to miss out on an opportunity than to lose your whole life savings and peace all together.




🌹

**First image is AI generated, 2nd image is a screenshot of how I was scammed.**

**Thanks a lot for taking your time to read through, kindly do well to stop by my blog @marsdave for more exclusive and amazing content.**

body.title: The Hard Lesson I Learned About Online Scammers
body.body:
‎
‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎It is another beautiful week and it's with great pleasure to welcome everyone to my blog today.
‎
‎When I first joined Hive, I was honestly too excited. Everything about the platform looked new and full of opportunities. I wanted to grow fast, meet people and understand how everything worked. Because of that excitement, I made some mistakes that almost cost me dearly during my first three months on the Hive.
‎

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPxKcP2eYvRYYhgcT39FoMAHP2LQMxg7ittZzVJ5Lw2j8/1779694688190.jpg)

‎[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/technology-devices-electronics-6801334/)
‎
‎Back then, I used to click on almost every link people dropped for me. Some would say it was a way to grow your account faster, while others promised rewards or special opportunities. Since I was still new to the online space, I didn’t actually know how dangerous some of those links could be.
‎
‎I can still remember one particular moment when I realized not everybody online means well. I clicked on a link that looked very genuine at first. Everything about it appeared normal, so I didn’t suspect anything. It was later I discovered it was most likely a scam attempt. And before I knew it, my account is taken over, and the scammer packed all the hive and hbd I have worked hard for. That experience really shook and weigh me down but I don't let it stopped me.
‎
‎And thanks to amazing people on hive, someone like @flaxz who introduced me to someone that later help me regain my account.
‎
‎Since that day, I changed the way I approach things online.
‎
‎Now, I no longer rush into clicking links just because someone shared them with me. I take my time to research properly before joining anything. I check if people are talking positively about it, ask questions from trusted users and sometimes even completely ignore it  if it feels suspicious. I have learned that being careful online is far better than regretting later.
‎
‎One thing scammers understand very well is human emotion. They know people like instant results, easy money and fast growth. That is why many scam messages usually sound tempting. But over time, I discovered that it is better to double-check it first if something sounds too perfect online.
‎
‎These days, I tread carefully on the internet because not everybody is really trying to help you. Some people are simply looking for who will make one careless mistake.
‎
‎The internet is a beautiful place with many opportunities, but it also requires wisdom. For me, one of the biggest lessons Hive taught me early was this: never stop doing your own research before trusting any link online.
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)
‎

body.title: How I Sew My Double Layer Abaya
body.body:
Happy new day to us all. I hope that we all had a wonderful night rest. It's another day, let arise and shine. And I want to share with the community this not so beautiful Abaya i was able to cut and sew yesterday. It is my first trial because i always fear of mistakes.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUJoadF2hw9eCpeFxQxaBNcww2vUq53sugLiu8kUmbGwY/1000219768.jpg 

I don't know the value of little knowledge about fashion designer I have until now. We were preparing for Eid-ul-Adha and  every was buying abaya. Ordering are flying around and me that I did not have money just in one place placing my faith in God.

But I was about to give up hope when I remembered that I can sew, and it will only cost me the material money to get my own abaya ready,  so I checked my account balance and truly, I have enough to buy the fabric and the material needed.

Chiffon fabric 
Lace applique with sequins
Tread 
Scissors 

They called the style double layer abaya. It's just a simple A line shape style but it is double layer.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSKUMrj7eFEzuD6qqDck6eFxq6kurDKxrpYqHTzdKcFbv/1779693103332.jpg)


I draft out my basic body measurements on A line shape with a V neck line.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXtTWTPC29d7xpEewDsGToFhnV4Qw3pP4q36cfAdasCP4/1779693131521.jpg)


I placed the one I already drafted on another fabric and draft out another one but this time around , it will be shorter than the previous one.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQqtFvMhnKDZQ9J9TZrQwC8Z69sT5PstMFqRZX5QrT4SW/1779693151714.jpg)


I removed ten inches from the length and add my Basque effect and I removed two inches from the front because I'm going to add flap to it. The back pattern will be done the same way only that it will not have opening.

body.title: 📜 El Arte de la Madurez: 10 Verdades Incómodas que Aprendí con los Años / The Art of Maturity: 10 Uncomfortable Truths I Learned with Age
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYVScM28iGmbGCkWmYHF57sgM9xUEi4f4b7VsJq5f2m7o/img_20260524_153617_592.jpg)
A lo largo de mi camino en esta colmena, suelo compartir con ustedes mis grandes pasiones: el análisis del béisbol, las dinámicas del ecosistema cripto y el día a día de mis proyectos. Sin embargo, hoy quiero hacer un alto en el camino. Quiero despojarme de las gráficas, las estadísticas y los negocios para abrirles una ventana a mi mente y a mi experiencia más íntima.

Hay lecciones que no se aprenden en los libros ni en los campos de entrenamiento; se aprenden en el silencio de la observación, en los golpes cotidianos de la vida y en ese proceso inevitable —y a veces doloroso— que llamamos madurar. Hoy comparto con ustedes diez verdades psicológicas que transformaron mi manera de ver el mundo y que, con total honestidad, desearía haber asimilado mucho antes.

*Throughout my journey in this hive, I usually share with you my great passions: baseball analysis, crypto ecosystem dynamics, and the day-to-day of my projects. However, today I want to pause. I want to strip away the charts, statistics, and business to open a window into my mind and my most intimate experience.*

*There are lessons that are not learned in books or on training grounds; they are learned in the silence of observation, in the daily blows of life, and in that inevitable —and sometimes painful— process we call maturing. Today I share with you ten psychological truths that transformed the way I see the world and that, in all honesty, I wish I had internalized much sooner.*

---

## 🏛️ 1. El Silencio y el Autocontrol: Nuestras Armas Más Poderosas / Silence and Self-Control: Our Most Powerful Weapons

> **La persona más calmada en la sala es quien suele dominar el entorno.**

Siempre nos han vendido la idea de que el líder es el que más grita o el que más rápido responde. Qué gran error. La verdadera fuerza no es reactiva; es magnética. Cuando dejas de reaccionar emocionalmente a las provocaciones, te conviertes en el eje central sobre el cual los demás tienen que pivotar.

A esto se suma el poder del silencio. Cuando dejas de hablar y solo miras con calma, el vacío genera una incomodidad tan profunda en el otro que, por pura desesperación, termina revelando sus verdaderas cartas. El silencio no es ausencia de comunicación; es control absoluto.

> ***The calmest person in the room is usually the one who dominates the environment.***

*We have always been sold the idea that the leader is the one who shouts the loudest or responds the fastest. What a huge mistake. True strength is not reactive; it is magnetic. When you stop reacting emotionally to provocations, you become the central axis around which others must pivot.*

*Added to this is the power of silence. When you stop talking and just look calmly, the vacuum generates such a deep discomfort in the other person that, out of pure desperation, they end up revealing their true cards. Silence is not an absence of communication; it is absolute control.*

---

## ⚡ 2. Primeras Impresiones y el Límite de las Explicaciones / First Impressions and the Limit of Explanations

La gente te pone a prueba inconscientemente en cuestión de minutos. Una broma sutil a tu costa, una interrupción o un retraso son exámenes silenciosos. Tu primera respuesta ante ese pequeño límite marcará la pauta de cómo te tratarán durante años.

Y en ese juego, **menos siempre es más**. Caer en la trampa de sobreexplicar o justificarte es la vía rápida para perder autoridad. Cada vez que te justificas de más, te empequeñeces. Las respuestas cortas y firmes transmiten una confianza ciega que hace que el otro se cuestione a sí mismo, no a ti.

*People unconsciously test you within minutes. A subtle joke at your expense, an interruption, or a delay are silent exams. Your first response to that small boundary will set the tone for how they treat you for years.*

*And in that game, **less is always more**. Falling into the trap of over-explaining or justifying yourself is the fast track to losing authority. Every time you over-justify, you diminish yourself. Short, firm answers convey a blind confidence that makes the other person question themselves, not you.*

---

## 🍃 3. Desapego y la Psicología de la Escasez / Detachment and the Psychology of Scarcity

Existe una regla de oro en la vida y en los negocios: **la persona que menos necesita la venta, es quien se la lleva**. Cuando demuestras necesidad, hueles a vulnerabilidad. En cambio, cuando estás dispuesto a dar un paso atrás y marcharte, el equilibrio de poder cambia de bando de forma automática.

Esto se conecta directamente con tu disponibilidad. En un mundo hiperconectado, el acceso constante reduce tu valor percibido. Cuando regulas tu presencia y proteges tu tiempo, obligas al entorno a tratar cada uno de tus minutos como el recurso valioso que realmente es.

*There is a golden rule in life and business: **the person who needs the sale the least is the one who gets it**. When you show need, you smell of vulnerability. On the other hand, when you are willing to take a step back and walk away, the balance of power automatically shifts to your side.*

*This connects directly with your availability. In a hyper-connected world, constant access reduces your perceived value. When you regulate your presence and protect your time, you force your environment to treat every single one of your minutes as the valuable resource it truly is.*

---

## 🛡️ 4. Proyecciones y el Escudo contra la Manipulación / Projections and the Shield Against Manipulation

He aprendido a observar patrones y no solo opiniones. Las críticas repetitivas de las personas rara vez hablan de ti; son radiografías de sus propias inseguridades y debilidades. Quien critica constantemente un defecto ajeno, suele estar librando una batalla perdida contra ese mismo fantasma en su interior.

Entender esto es el mejor escudo contra los manipuladores. Su moneda de cambio es tu culpa, tu enfado o tu necesidad de defenderte. Si logran alterarte, te controlan. Tu neutralidad emocional los deja completamente desarmados, tirando golpes al vacío.

*I have learned to observe patterns and not just opinions. People's repetitive criticisms are rarely about you; they are X-rays of their own insecurities and weaknesses. Someone who constantly criticizes another's flaw is usually fighting a losing battle against that very ghost inside themselves.*

*Understanding this is the best shield against manipulators. Their bargaining chip is your guilt, your anger, or your need to defend yourself. If they manage to upset you, they control you. Your emotional neutrality leaves them completely disarmed, throwing punches into empty space.*

---

## 🪞 5. El Respeto se Enseña y la Aprobación se Suelta / Respect is Taught and Approval is Released

> **La sociedad no te mide por lo que vales, sino por lo que toleras.**

La mayoría de las personas deciden cuánto respetarte observando cómo permites que otros te traten. Si toleras una falta de respeto en público por \

, tu valor cae inmediatamente ante los ojos de los testigos. El respeto no se mendiga, se modela con límites claros.

Y el paso definitivo hacia la verdadera madurez llega cuando dejas de buscar la aprobación ajena. Buscar que todos te aplaudan es crear tu propia prisión de dependencia. El desapego de la opinión pública genera una ventaja que la gente percibe al instante: te vuelve incorruptible, libre y, por encima de todo, dueño de tu propio destino.

> ***Society does not measure you by what you are worth, but by what you tolerate.***

*Most people decide how much to respect you by observing how you allow others to treat you. If you tolerate a lack of respect in public to \

your value drops immediately in the eyes of witnesses. Respect is not begged for; it is modeled with clear boundaries.*

*And the definitive step toward true maturity comes when you stop seeking approval from others. Wanting everyone to applaud you is creating your own prison of dependency. Detachment from public opinion generates an advantage that people perceive instantly: it makes you incorruptible, free, and, above all, the master of your own destiny.*

---

## 💭 Reflexión Final / Final Reflection

Escribir estas líneas es también un ejercicio de autorreflexión para mí. A veces nos enfocamos tanto en ganar batallas externas que olvidamos que la victoria más grande ocurre dentro de nosotros mismos, al aprender a gobernarnos.

A ti, que te detuviste a leerme hoy en Ecency: **¿Cuál de estas verdades te ha tocado vivir más de cerca? ¿Hay alguna lección de madurez que añadirías a esta lista basado en tu propia experiencia?** Me encantaría leerte en la sección de comentarios y debatir desde el respeto y la vivencia compartida.

¡Gracias por acompañarme en esta faceta más humana!

*Writing these lines is also an exercise in self-reflection for me. Sometimes we focus so much on winning external battles that we forget that the greatest victory happens within ourselves, by learning to govern who we are.*

*To you, who stopped to read me today on Ecency: **Which of these truths have you had to live closest to? Is there a lesson in maturity that you would add to this list based on your own experience?** I would love to read you in the comments section and debate from a place of respect and shared experience.*

*Thank you for joining me in this more human side of my journey!*

---
body.author: luisma79

body.title: The Fruit Bats of Colac
body.body:
![Grey Headed Flying Fox 2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/harveyword/23tvZzjCJvxHToBCsZUBQ7XgMYzx3fdVvffiwnrew5VvkFLbuLcMJx3oDboWZimDtPY2n.jpg)


There’s a particular kind of noise that comes from the Colac Botanical Gardens (about 2 hours west of Melbourne in Australia)  if you arrive at the right time of day. It's a layered, restless chatter that you might think in the first instance is birds. But if you Follow it to the end of the gardens  you’ll find them: hundreds of grey-headed flying foxes draped across the treetops making one hell of a noise.  


![Grey Headed Flying Fox.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/harveyword/AK2CNtd662LuujFs19ADm3L5gPayUb9JhEtL8sjyiZrtdEztX7G97vrWxWB3MPR.jpg)


A sidebar - You might think they are bats and you are right. A grey-headed flying fox is Australia’s largest native fruit eating bat, with grey fur and a rusty-orange collar around its neck. It eats fruit, nectar, and pollen, and unlike many other bats, it mainly uses its eyes and sense of smell rather than echolocation

They hang there with an odd sort of purpose, wrapped in themselves, occasionally jostling for space like commuters on a crowded tram. Every so often one drops, wings snapping open mid-fall, and glides across the gardens with a grace. Hard to catch with a camera but after enough tries I got there. the Sun shining through their wings. 


![Grey Headed Flying Fox in Flight.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/harveyword/AKKRXeEMgthaVMRUgJtEvdCPmuXs38PAxsdQvDhfEp7Hj3SK99DLD8hTgLc1EyH.jpg)


Locals seem divided about them. Some see mess, smell, and noise, so much noise, and so much stripping of the trees. Others see a living, shifting ecosystem right in the middle of town. Stand there long enough and you start to notice the details: the rustle of wings, the soft clicking sounds, the way sunlight filters through a canopy that’s very much alive.

The locals have tried to remove them, scare them of with noises and frequencies and unplesant sounds, but they are leaving, and there is a certain irony to trying to remove a native animal to protect the introduced European trees of the planned garden. 


![Grey Headed Flying Fox in Flight 2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/harveyword/AK568drGpYGqJeAhXkgMTG2JaDd1EEECyL7cjG6RqwppvaGzEeAHJfGmaaTUagu.jpg)


So here I am in the late afternoon as the the colony begins to stir in earnest. One by one, then in loose waves, they lift off toward the horizon, heading out over Colac in search of food. The trees grow quieter, but not empty—just waiting for their return.


![Grey Headed Flying Fox in Flight 3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/harveyword/243LthQknxh7UrQGKY9HHEPbSeXLDMzjWkNSre1vZ3TCwJ1VVJnx9g84wNQfrR9zrQMQM.jpg)

body.title: MISUNDERSTANDING ABOUT RETROGRADE SATURN IN VEDIC ASTROLOGY
body.body: Retrograde Saturn in Vedic astrology is one of the most commonly misunderstood placements, often surrounded by fear, exaggeration, and oversimplified interpretations. Many people assume that a retrograde Saturn is automatically negative, karmically punishing, or a sign of failure and delay in all areas of life. This misunderstanding largely comes from reading Saturn only through a lens of fear rather than understanding its deeper philosophical and karmic role in Vedic astrology. In reality, retrograde Saturn does not signify weakness or doom; instead, it represents an inward, intensified, and often more complex expression of Saturn’s principles. One major misunderstanding is the belief that retrograde Saturn always gives worse results than direct Saturn. In Vedic astrology, retrogression does not mean that a planet loses strength. In fact, a retrograde planet is often considered more powerful because its energy is concentrated and internalized. Saturn governs discipline, responsibility, karma, time, and life lessons. When retrograde, these themes tend to operate on a psychological and internal level before manifesting externally. Such natives may experience deep self-reflection, heightened awareness of duty, and a strong inner moral compass, even if external success appears delayed. Another common misconception is that retrograde Saturn inevitably causes delays, failures, and suffering throughout life. While Saturn does signify delays, these delays are purposeful rather than punitive. Retrograde Saturn often indicates unfinished karmic lessons from past lives that need resolution in this lifetime. This does not mean constant hardship, but rather repeated opportunities to learn patience, perseverance, and accountability. Many individuals with retrograde Saturn achieve long-lasting success, especially later in life, once they align with Saturn’s lessons instead of resisting them. People also misunderstand retrograde Saturn as a sign of bad karma alone. In truth, it can indicate both unresolved and advanced karmic patterns. Some natives with retrograde Saturn possess wisdom, maturity, and seriousness beyond their age. They may feel different from others early in life, carrying a strong sense of responsibility from a young age. This placement can make a person self-critical and introspective, but it also grants the ability to master Saturnian qualities such as endurance, fairness, and ethical living over time. A further misunderstanding lies in ignoring house placement, sign dignity, aspects, conjunctions, and dashas when interpreting retrograde Saturn. Saturn does not act alone. A well-placed retrograde Saturn in its own sign or exaltation can give remarkable results, including authority, stability, and respect. Conversely, a poorly placed direct Saturn can cause more challenges than a well-supported retrograde one. Vedic astrology emphasizes holistic chart analysis, and isolating retrogression without context leads to inaccurate conclusions. Many also believe that remedies for retrograde Saturn must be extreme or fear-driven. In reality, Saturn responds best to consistent effort, humility, service, and ethical conduct. Retrograde Saturn natives benefit from self-discipline, long-term planning, and inner work rather than quick fixes. Acts of responsibility, helping the underprivileged, honoring elders, and maintaining integrity naturally harmonize Saturn’s energy. In conclusion, retrograde Saturn in Vedic astrology is not a curse or a sign of inevitable suffering. It is a powerful indicator of deep karmic work, inner growth, and long-term transformation. The misunderstanding arises from fear-based interpretations and incomplete analysis. When understood correctly, retrograde Saturn becomes a teacher rather than a punisher, guiding the native toward maturity, wisdom, and lasting success through patience and conscious effort. #retrogradesaturn #astrology #horoscope #vedicastrology #indianastrology #vedicastrologer #astrologer #predictions #destiny #psychic #kundli #jyotish #remedy

body.title: Congratulations, You Got What You Wanted
body.body:
# Congratulations, You Got What You Wanted

**Markets & Macro — Issue No. 48 — Monday, May 25, 2026**

---

*Bitcoin is at $75,860. The CLARITY Act just passed committee. BlackRock's IBIT bled $448 million in a single session. Please, tell me more about how regulatory clarity is a bullish catalyst.*

---

| | |
|---|---|
| **BTC spot** | ~$75,860 — down ~7% from May high |
| **IBIT outflows (May 18)** | $448.4M — second-largest daily redemption of 2026 |
| **Total ETF outflows, 6-day streak** | ~$1.55B since May 15 |
| **CLARITY Act** | Advanced Senate Banking Committee 15-9, May 14 |
| **Tokenized RWA market** | ~$34.5B — up 100%+ year-on-year |

---

For two years, the dominant story in crypto was that the industry was being strangled by regulatory ambiguity. The SEC was hostile. The CFTC and SEC were fighting over turf. Nobody knew what was a security, what was a commodity, what was a prayer. Every earnings call from Coinbase contained some variation of the same lament: if Washington would just give us *rules*, the institutional money would flood in and everything would be wonderful.

Washington gave them rules.

Bitcoin dropped six thousand dollars.

This is, in the most technical sense, hilarious. The Senate Banking Committee advanced H.R. 3633 — the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — by a 15-9 vote on May 14. The bill would resolve the SEC-CFTC jurisdictional standoff that has defined crypto regulation since approximately forever. Coinbase, Circle, and Ripple backed it. The industry had been lobbying for something like this since 2022. Bitcoin briefly broke back above $81,000 on the news. Then, over the following week, US spot Bitcoin ETFs shed roughly $1.55 billion across six consecutive outflow days — the most sustained institutional exit since these products launched. IBIT alone dropped $448 million on May 18. That was its second-largest single-day redemption of 2026.

The market-structure bill that crypto spent three years begging for arrived, and the response from professional capital was: *hard pass, actually.*

---

## What \

Looks Like When the News Is Everything\n\nThe charitable interpretation is that this is simply mechanics. Traders who bought Bitcoin at $76,000 in anticipation of regulatory progress took their profit once the headline hit. Clean. Rational. Textbook. The uncharitable interpretation is that the \

thesis was always partly circular — a story the industry told itself to explain why prices would eventually go up, rather than a genuine analysis of what institutions actually need before allocating capital to an asset that spent February capitulating 30% while the Strait of Hormuz closed.

Both interpretations are probably right, in different proportions for different participants.

What's genuinely interesting is the divergence within crypto flows. XRP spot ETFs pulled in $60.5 million during the same week that Bitcoin was hemorrhaging. Ethereum spot ETFs recorded $255 million in redemptions. Capital is rotating, not fleeing. The story isn't that institutions have lost faith in digital assets — the tokenized RWA market hit $34.5 billion in May, up more than 100% year-on-year, with BlackRock's BUIDL fund and Ondo Finance pulling in institutional money at a pace that would have seemed science fiction eighteen months ago. The story is more specific and more uncomfortable: at current prices and under current macro conditions, Bitcoin the speculative asset is less interesting than the on-chain infrastructure building around it.

> *Six consecutive outflow days. $1.55 billion. This is what the most-anticipated regulatory development in crypto's recent history looks like when you zoom out from the headline.*

---

## The Macro Trap Nobody Wants to Talk About

Here is the thing about Bitcoin and inflation that the bulls never quite squared: Bitcoin was supposed to be a hedge against fiat debasement and monetary excess. When the Fed was printing, BTC was the answer. That was the brand. The problem is that the same conditions that produce inflation — energy shocks, supply disruptions, geopolitical instability — also produce a strong dollar, rising real yields, and risk-off positioning. All of which are headwinds for Bitcoin.

The 30-year Treasury at 5.19%. The 10-year near 4.7%. Moody's stripped the US of its Aaa rating in May — the third ratings agency to do so — citing a \

Bond yields moved higher on the news. The dollar strengthened. Both are, historically, brutal for BTC. A stronger dollar tightens global liquidity. Higher yields make non-yielding assets less appealing on a relative basis. The inflation hedge narrative runs directly into the rising-rate reality, and rising rates win almost every time.

Strategy purchased another 24,869 BTC during this period, absorbing some of the selling pressure. One company's conviction trade is doing meaningful work in a market that, without it, would probably look worse than it does. That is not a stable foundation.

---

## Meanwhile, in the Part of Crypto Nobody Is Panicking About

While everyone stares at the BTC price ticker, something quieter is happening that will matter more over a five-year horizon. The tokenized real-world asset market — Treasuries, money market instruments, private credit on-chain — tripled between early 2025 and Q1 2026. BlackRock filed two new tokenized fund applications with the SEC on May 8. Not one — two. Tokenized US Treasuries alone sit at $15.2 billion in market cap, with BlackRock and Circle leading inflows. Ondo Finance ran from $0.26 to nearly $0.47 during the May breakout before giving it back.

The GENIUS Act already created a regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, with a July 2026 deadline for follow-on rules. The CLARITY Act, if it passes the full Senate, resolves the SEC-CFTC turf war that has kept institutional product development in a holding pattern. Standard Chartered projects the tokenized asset market reaching $30 trillion by 2034. That number sounds insane until you run the math on what fraction of global fixed income it would represent and realize it's actually conservative.

None of this helps Bitcoin at $75,860. In the short term, BTC lives and dies on macro: oil, yields, the dollar, and whether Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting produces language that sounds more hawkish than the market expects. If Hormuz reopens in earnest and Brent retraces toward $80, the inflation story softens, real yields compress slightly, and risk assets including BTC catch a bid. That's the bull case, and it's genuinely plausible.

But the *Bitcoin as inflation hedge, regulatory clarity as unlock* narrative has taken a serious beating this month. The thing that was supposed to happen when Washington delivered clarity — didn't happen. The thing that was supposed to happen when inflation ran hot — also didn't happen, in the way promised.

At some point the story has to square with the data.

---

*Data references: BTC spot price, IBIT/FBTC/ARKB daily ETF flows (Farside Investors), CoinShares fund flow report May 18, CLARITY Act Senate Banking Committee vote May 14, tokenized RWA market cap (RWA.xyz), Moody's US credit downgrade, Strategy BTC purchase disclosures. All figures as of May 22–23, 2026.*

body.title: Entre visitas y café
body.body:
Un buen fin de semana entre visitas y café. Poco a poco voy visitando o me vienen a encontrar la familia. Y los venezolanos somos generosos y agradecidos de todo lo que logramos, pero los españoles llenan la mesa full de comidas. La verdad es que tienen abundancia en sus mesas y mucha variedad. Una mezcla que resulta maravillosa entre lo que dejamos allá y lo que se está formando aquí. 

Estoy agradecida en verdad no sabía que tanta gente quiere verme y que les cuente cómo vamos en casa. 



![1000875418.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbeb5ft3LLnhLe3AnZKvDQqrhfTpTvqxSj1pZXwbjyozk/1000875418.jpg)


![1000875374.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPxLyMQoBp1sdb7SxGxT99t76wcbvYsq1aLGduofZmuWp/1000875374.jpg)


![1000875419.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWEudUofFMU4gyuYVs9HhHLVGZhkEDJnYoLTj2qTwf5tf/1000875419.jpg)


![1000875332.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW4zH3kGPtcjEDVHGz9Ru9eTKoh7y3foDNnxMh51CV1pw/1000875332.jpg)

Mi hija de desayuno panquecas es como estar en casa. 


![1000875120.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWRbEetw3vTpU3MhD1eoiMT7prez8GdRuhtt9no1Yo8bk/1000875120.jpg)

Creó que lo que hago es comer, caminar y volver a comer. Me resulta difícil almorzar a las 3 pm mi cuerpo a las doce del mediodía como es en Venezuela pide la comida. Mi hija dice cuando tengas hambre tu comes y punto. Cuál es la diferencia para que los españoles aguanten y es que tienen entre comidas o como yo las llamo meriendas. 


![1000874124.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU5o3thzu2w2Yp7jkgtrTRvdMz8VnyxvKsQfp7Anqu7y8/1000874124.jpg)

![1000873805.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdAJHNwijzQKLG3nQe5nwcUYhos3CyEoisaoc6RnUw6Rs/1000873805.jpg)

Aquí no he cocinado ni un huevo frito, mi hija y mi yerno preparan todo, como trabajan mucho, son comidas para dos días. Me compraron los ingredientes para hacer quesillo, leche condensada, huevos, vainilla y azúcar. Pronto la estaré haciendo. 


![1000875887.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNMLCiKdWXoJECjGCZT2AU4o1UYEpDHkTdfmHGeyXYKmg/1000875887.jpg)

![1000875870.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdvpxqYcvXWxDEhaobPeNkBvfJRuMFkxaLpVdqVmQ2HiV/1000875870.jpg)


![1000875872.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc6egWbBBDHKdL5QCxN8AJDshkCy878vg5QiQrUGKH1Cj/1000875872.jpg)

![1000875871.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUnCDmw1QQP1r5LzfT3g8gvBMx8FomafgCJja11216NL9/1000875871.jpg)

Me falta otro sobrino por visitar pero estaba en la graduación de su hijo. Con José Miguel no lo había visto desde el anterior viaje afrontó graves problemas de salud por la diabetes, le hicieron un transplante después de esperar y ver la gravedad de su caso. Asusté a mi hija cuando le dije que se había fracturado los dedos de un pie y que sino sanaba se lo cortaban, ella estaba de viaje mando a su esposo que lo llevará al hospital donde le habían hecho el transplante. 

Resulta que los medicamentos para que no rechazará el órgano le habían causado osteoporosis y se había fracturado sin ningún golpe. Ahora está bien, con su control no ha vuelto a presentar problemas. 


![1000875867.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUvC6hFVU1eNXGCreNwYdCdm33eYWnyAvVjwQ4hJKrCTG/1000875867.jpg)

La medicina te puede matar aquí o allá sino hay personas pendientes. 


![1000875868.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmayXznnwy2fh4emtRLHwthte8JYjNdSZ7PU8byFNADqQM/1000875868.jpg)

![1000875833.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPz2UowmwVqp46gn6hDfR7YzhMCYBm3pHiAx2EagqAv71/1000875833.jpg)

Me paseo por los automercados disfrutando de la variedad de marcas de café y de otros productos. En Venezuela hay de todo ahorita pero costoso. 


![1000876143.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQhxEZ2zPJyDJzXwJ2DEUnreWpa5oZ6MsRmbzRbhZFjBH/1000876143.jpg)

![1000876886.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfP8eZK6opebogDQeBPjnQdNUM2L5w82AjWj3r36ooXsX/1000876886.jpg)

Disfruto de las caminatas libremente y con poco peligro. El calor comenzó y tengo prohibido salir de 1 pm (13 h) hasta las 5 pm (17 h) aproximadamente. Palabras de mi hija: los viejitos no salen a esas horas. Y buscan las sombritas por las aceras. 

Tiene planeado un viaje a Málaga, allí estaremos en casa de una de las trillizas, amiga desde Venezuela. Allí hay playas y una habitación en su casa. Todavía no hemos podido cuadrar con la familia de Archena Murcia. 


![1000875338.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRZbZmZKThoCozXGdPseENJogu6V7yLdXAZrKMsiKtbkT/1000875338.jpg)

![1000875838.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdGdiaKJLnjtENFxtMdwvXXGarZdT6rbEuNYcbSt6y3eS/1000875838.jpg)

Ya veremos, no quiero cansarme mucho, disfruto a mis hijos y mientras tanto veo los apagones en Venezuela.

# Learn AI Series (#77) - Image Processing Fundamentals

Welcome to **Arc 5: Computer Vision**. We've spent the last twenty episodes deep in LLM territory -- language models, transformers, RAG, agents, evaluation, the whole works. And in episode #76 we capped that arc off by building a complete AI assistant that ties it all together. Now we're shifting focus. From text to pixels.

Here's the thing though -- we haven't been *completely* ignoring images. Back in episodes #45-47 we built **CNNs** and used them for classification, detection, and style transfer. In episode #54 we covered **Vision Transformers**. And in #75 we looked at **multimodal models** that bridge text and vision. But in all of those episodes we sort of... assumed the images were already preprocessed and ready to go. We loaded them, resized them, maybe normalized them, and moved on.

That's backwards. In actual computer vision work, image preprocessing is where quit some of the battle is won or lost. A model trained on well-preprocessed images consistently outperforms the same architecture trained on raw, noisy, inconsistently-sized data. So before we go deeper into detection, segmentation, and generative vision models in the coming episodes, we need to build a proper foundation. Starting from the literal pixels.

## Digital images: just arrays of numbers

Way back in episode #3 we established that all data is numbers. Images are no exception. A **grayscale image** of size 480x640 is a 2D NumPy array with shape `(480, 640)`. Each element is a pixel intensity value: 0 means black, 255 means white, everything in between is a shade of gray.

A **color image** adds a third dimension: channels. An RGB image of size 480x640 has shape `(480, 640, 3)` -- one channel each for **red**, **green**, and **blue**. Each pixel is a triplet like `(142, 87, 213)`, meaning \

```python
import numpy as np
import cv2

# Load an image from disk
img = cv2.imread(\

)  # [B, G, R] array

# Create a grayscale gradient from scratch
gradient = np.zeros((256, 256), dtype=np.uint8)
for i in range(256):
    gradient[i, :] = i  # each row is a different brightness

# Create a color image from scratch
color_img = np.zeros((200, 300, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
color_img[:, :100] = [255, 0, 0]    # left third: blue (BGR!)
color_img[:, 100:200] = [0, 255, 0]  # middle third: green
color_img[:, 200:] = [0, 0, 255]    # right third: red
```

Now, here is an **important OpenCV quirk** that trips up literally everyone at some point: **OpenCV loads images in BGR order**, not RGB. This is a historical artifact from when BGR was common in camera hardware. It means that if you load an image with `cv2.imread` and display it with **matplotlib** (which expects RGB), the colors will be swapped -- reds become blues and vice versa. When passing images to **PyTorch** or any other framework that expects RGB, you need to convert:

```python
# OpenCV BGR to standard RGB
rgb_img = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

# Or skip the problem entirely: use PIL for loading
from PIL import Image
pil_img = Image.open(\

)   # loads as RGB directly
img_array = np.array(pil_img)       # (H, W, 3) in RGB order
```

I've wasted hours debugging color issues before realizing the BGR/RGB mismatch was the culprit. Consider this your warning ;-)

## Color spaces: beyond RGB

RGB is intuitive (we can reason about \

) but it's not always the best representation for computer vision tasks. Different **color spaces** separate different kinds of information, and choosing the right one for your task can simplify everything.

### HSV -- Hue, Saturation, Value

**HSV** separates *what color it is* (hue) from *how vivid* (saturation) and *how bright* (value). The hue channel runs from 0 to 180 in OpenCV (not 360 -- another quirk), saturation and value from 0 to 255.

Why HSV matters: suppose you want to find all the red objects in a scene. In RGB, \

means high R, low G, low B -- but a dark red, a bright red, and a slightly orange red have very different RGB values. In HSV, all reds cluster around the same hue value regardless of lighting. You just filter on hue:

```python
hsv = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)

# Red wraps around hue 0/180 in OpenCV, so we need two ranges
lower_red1 = np.array([0, 100, 80])
upper_red1 = np.array([10, 255, 255])
lower_red2 = np.array([170, 100, 80])
upper_red2 = np.array([180, 255, 255])

mask1 = cv2.inRange(hsv, lower_red1, upper_red1)
mask2 = cv2.inRange(hsv, lower_red2, upper_red2)
red_mask = mask1 | mask2
# red_mask: 255 where red, 0 elsewhere

# Count red pixels
red_pixels = np.count_nonzero(red_mask)
total_pixels = red_mask.shape[0] * red_mask.shape[1]
print(f\

)
```

### LAB -- Perceptually uniform

**LAB** (also called CIELAB) splits an image into **L** (lightness), **A** (green-to-red axis), and **B** (blue-to-yellow axis). The key property is that it's *perceptually uniform*: a numerical distance of 10 in LAB space looks like the same amount of visual difference no matter where in the color space you are. That's NOT true for RGB (a change of 10 in the blue channel looks very different at low brightness vs high brightness).

LAB is useful for any operation where you need to reason about \

-- things like color-based clustering, image quality metrics, and contrast enhancement.

### Grayscale -- When color doesn't matter

For many tasks -- **edge detection**, **text recognition**, **feature matching** -- color is irrelevant. Converting to grayscale reduces your data from 3 channels to 1, making everything 3x faster:

```python
gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
lab = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB)

# Grayscale conversion uses a weighted average, not a simple mean:
# gray = 0.299*R + 0.587*G + 0.114*B
# These weights match human perception (we're most sensitive to green)
```

Choosing the right color space for the job is one of those things that separates a thoughtful pipeline from a naive one. For color-based detection: HSV. For perceptual operations (contrast, color distance): LAB. For speed and when color doesn't matter: grayscale. For everything else: RGB (or BGR if you're stuck in OpenCV land).

## Convolution as image filtering

We covered convolution mathematically in episode #45 when we built CNNs. The same operation -- sliding a small matrix (the **kernel**) across the image and computing weighted sums -- has been used in image processing for decades before neural networks existed. CNNs just learn which kernels to use automatically. Today we're designing them by hand.

```python
def convolve2d(image, kernel):
    \

h, w = image.shape[:2]
    kh, kw = kernel.shape
    pad_h, pad_w = kh // 2, kw // 2

    # Pad edges using reflection (mirror the boundary pixels)
    padded = np.pad(image, ((pad_h, pad_h), (pad_w, pad_w)),
                    mode='reflect')
    output = np.zeros_like(image, dtype=np.float64)

    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            region = padded[i:i + kh, j:j + kw]
            output[i, j] = np.sum(region * kernel)

    return output
```

This is deliberately slow (pure Python loops over every pixel) but it shows exactly what happens: at each position, extract a region the size of the kernel, multiply element-wise, sum. The kernel values determine the effect.

Different kernels produce fundamentally different results:

```python
# Box blur: average neighboring pixels (smoothing)
blur_kernel = np.ones((5, 5)) / 25.0

# Sharpen: enhance edges and fine details
sharpen_kernel = np.array([
    [ 0, -1,  0],
    [-1,  5, -1],
    [ 0, -1,  0]
], dtype=np.float64)

# Sobel: detect horizontal edges
sobel_x = np.array([
    [-1, 0, 1],
    [-2, 0, 2],
    [-1, 0, 1]
], dtype=np.float64)

# Sobel: detect vertical edges
sobel_y = np.array([
    [-1, -2, -1],
    [ 0,  0,  0],
    [ 1,  2,  1]
], dtype=np.float64)

# Apply using OpenCV (orders of magnitude faster than our loop)
blurred = cv2.filter2D(gray, -1, blur_kernel)
sharpened = cv2.filter2D(gray, -1, sharpen_kernel)
edges_x = cv2.filter2D(gray, cv2.CV_64F, sobel_x)
edges_y = cv2.filter2D(gray, cv2.CV_64F, sobel_y)

# Combine edge directions for overall edge magnitude
edge_magnitude = np.sqrt(edges_x**2 + edges_y**2)
edge_magnitude = np.clip(edge_magnitude, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
```

_Why does this matter for deep learning?_ Because the first layers of a trained CNN learn edge-detection kernels that look remarkably similar to Sobel filters. The network independently discovers through backpropagation what image processing engineers designed by hand in the 1960s. That's not a coincidence -- edges are the most informative low-level features in an image.

### Gaussian blur

The box blur above applies equal weight to all neighbors. **Gaussian blur** weights center pixels more than edge pixels, following a bell curve distribution. This produces a more natural smoothing effect:

```python
# Gaussian blur: kernel size must be odd, sigma controls spread
blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (5, 5), sigmaX=1.0)
very_blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (15, 15), sigmaX=5.0)

# Bilateral filter: blurs while preserving edges
# (slow but powerful for noise reduction)
denoised = cv2.bilateralFilter(img, d=9,
                                sigmaColor=75,
                                sigmaSpace=75)
```

The **bilateral filter** is worth highlighting. Regular Gaussian blur smooths everything -- edges included. The bilateral filter adds a second condition: only average pixels that are also *similar in color*. This preserves sharp edges while smoothing flat regions. It's computationally expensive but produces dramatically better results for noise reduction.

### Canny edge detection

**Canny** is the go-to edge detection algorithm. It combines Gaussian blur (noise reduction), gradient computation (finding edges), non-maximum suppression (thinning edges to single-pixel width), and hysteresis thresholding (connecting strong edges to weak ones) into a single pipeline:

```python
# Canny edge detection
edges = cv2.Canny(gray, threshold1=50, threshold2=150)
# Result: binary image, 255 at edges, 0 elsewhere

# The two thresholds control sensitivity:
# - Below threshold1: definitely NOT an edge
# - Above threshold2: definitely an edge
# - Between: only an edge if connected to a strong edge
# This hysteresis approach produces cleaner results than a single threshold
```

Having said that, tuning those two thresholds is something of an art. Too low and you get noise edges everywhere. Too high and you miss real structure. A common strategy is to compute the median pixel intensity and set thresholds relative to it:

```python
median_val = np.median(gray)
lower = int(max(0, 0.7 * median_val))
upper = int(min(255, 1.3 * median_val))
edges = cv2.Canny(gray, lower, upper)
```

## Histogram equalization and contrast

An image **histogram** shows the distribution of pixel intensities. A dark underexposed photo has most of its pixels clustered near 0. A washed-out overexposed photo has pixels bunched around 200-255. **Histogram equalization** remaps the distribution so it spans the full 0-255 range, improving contrast automatically.

```python
# Basic histogram equalization on grayscale
equalized = cv2.equalizeHist(gray)

# Compute histograms to see the difference
hist_before = cv2.calcHist([gray], [0], None, [256], [0, 256])
hist_after = cv2.calcHist([equalized], [0], None, [256], [0, 256])
```

For **color images**, you can't just equalize each RGB channel independently -- that creates weird color shifts because the channels are correlated. Instead, convert to **LAB** and equalize only the **L** (lightness) channel:

```python
lab = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB)
lab[:, :, 0] = cv2.equalizeHist(lab[:, :, 0])
equalized_color = cv2.cvtColor(lab, cv2.COLOR_LAB2BGR)
```

### CLAHE: adaptive histogram equalization

Global equalization has a problem: it applies the same transformation everywhere. A photo with a bright window and a dark corner needs different adjustments in different regions. **CLAHE** (Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization) solves this by dividing the image into tiles and equalizing each tile independently:

```python
clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=2.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))

# Apply to grayscale
enhanced_gray = clahe.apply(gray)

# Apply to color via LAB
lab = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB)
lab[:, :, 0] = clahe.apply(lab[:, :, 0])
enhanced_color = cv2.cvtColor(lab, cv2.COLOR_LAB2BGR)
```

The `clipLimit` parameter controls how much contrast enhancement is allowed per tile. Higher values mean more contrast but also more noise amplification. The `tileGridSize` controls how many tiles the image is divided into -- `(8, 8)` means 64 tiles, each equalized independently (with interpolation at tile borders so you don't see seams).

CLAHE is used extensively in medical imaging where lighting conditions are variable and subtle details in dark regions matter. It's also standard in autonomous driving pipelines where the camera might see bright sky and dark shadows in the same frame.

## Image transformations

Resizing, cropping, rotating, and warping are the workhorses of every image pipeline. Every model expects a fixed input size. Every dataset has images of different dimensions. Transformations bridge that gap.

```python
# Resize to exact dimensions
resized = cv2.resize(img, (224, 224))

# Resize by scale factor
half = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=0.5, fy=0.5)
double = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=2.0, fy=2.0)

# Resize with high-quality interpolation
resized_hq = cv2.resize(img, (224, 224),
                          interpolation=cv2.INTER_LANCZOS4)

# Crop is just NumPy slicing
cropped = img[50:300, 100:400]  # rows 50-300, cols 100-400

# Rotate around center
h, w = img.shape[:2]
center = (w // 2, h // 2)
matrix = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(center, angle=30, scale=1.0)
rotated = cv2.warpAffine(img, matrix, (w, h))

# Flip
flipped_h = cv2.flip(img, 1)   # horizontal mirror
flipped_v = cv2.flip(img, 0)   # vertical mirror
flipped_both = cv2.flip(img, -1)  # both axes
```

**Interpolation** matters more than most people realize when resizing. Here's a quick reference:

- `INTER_NEAREST`: fastest, but pixelated. Only use for label masks (where you don't want to blend values)
- `INTER_LINEAR`: good default for upscaling, fast
- `INTER_AREA`: best for downscaling (preserves information by averaging)
- `INTER_LANCZOS4`: highest quality for upscaling, slower

A common mistake is using `INTER_LINEAR` (the default) for downscaling. When shrinking an image significantly, `INTER_AREA` produces noticeably better results because it averages all the source pixels that map to each destination pixel rather than just sampling a few.

### Perspective transforms

Sometimes you need to correct perspective distortion -- like straightening a photo of a document taken at an angle. This requires a 4-point perspective transform:

```python
# Source points (corners of the tilted document in the photo)
src_pts = np.float32([
    [56, 65], [368, 52], [28, 387], [389, 390]
])
# Destination points (where we want those corners to end up)
dst_pts = np.float32([
    [0, 0], [300, 0], [0, 400], [300, 400]
])

M = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(src_pts, dst_pts)
straightened = cv2.warpPerspective(img, M, (300, 400))
```

This is the same math behind every \

app. Detect the document corners, compute the perspective transform, warp to a flat rectangle. Simple in principle, and the OpenCV implementaton is very efficient.

## Building a complete preprocessing pipeline

Real computer vision projects chain multiple operations into a consistent pipeline. Here's a class that takes raw images and produces model-ready tensors:

        self.std = np.array([0.229, 0.224, 0.225])

        # Step 7: HWC to CHW for PyTorch

        return img

        new_w = int(w * scale)

            interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA
            if scale < 1.0 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR

        pad_top = (th - new_h) // 2
        pad_left = (tw - new_w) // 2
        padded = np.zeros((th, tw, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        padded[pad_top:pad_top + new_h,

        return padded

Several design decisions here are worth noting:

**Aspect ratio preservation** with padding instead of stretching. Stretching distorts features -- a circle becomes an oval, a square becomes a rectangle. For models pretrained on ImageNet (where images are square), this distortion can hurt accuracy. Padding maintains the original proportions.

**Automatic interpolation selection**: `INTER_AREA` when downscaling, `INTER_LINEAR` when upscaling. This gives the best quality for each direction without the user having to think about it.

**Conditional CLAHE**: only applied to low-contrast images (standard deviation below 40). Applying histogram equalization to an image that already has good contrast wastes computation and can actually degrade quality by amplifying noise in already-visible regions.

**ImageNet normalization values** (`mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406]`, `std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]`). These numbers are worth memorizing if you work with vision models. Nearly every pretrained model (ResNet, VGG, EfficientNet, ViT -- all of them) was trained with these statistics. If you normalize differently, the first layer receives input it wasn't calibrated for and performance drops. It's a small thing that makes a big difference.

The **HWC to CHW** transpose at the end is because PyTorch expects channel-first format `(C, H, W)` while OpenCV and NumPy use channel-last `(H, W, C)`. This is another constant source of shape-mismatch bugs. Get it right in the preprocessing pipeline and you never have to think about it downstream.

Generate 10 augmented versions and verify that pixel statistics (mean, std) remain reasonable after augmentation.

body.body:
>Cara Menyingkirkan Orang Toxic Tanpa Perlu Banyak Berbicara:

\n\n1.

>Berhenti menjelaskan diri sendiri: Seseoang yang toxic memberi penjelasan dari yang kamu beri. Mereka akan memutar bali omongan dan mencari celah logika kamu ,dan memamcing agar terus menerus membela diri. Diam adalah jawaban yang terbaik;

\n2.

>Balas dengan jarak: Tidak perlu pengumuman ketika kamu pergi, cukup berhenti muncul di tempat di mana kamu tidak dihargai. Batasi akses, kurangi komunikasi, dan jaga ruang pribadi. Jarak adalah filter alami; seseorang yang tidak tepat akann tersisih dengan sendirinya;

\n3.

>Responlah seperlunya: Balas seadanya, kasih jeda waktu yang lama, dan gunakan nada bicara yang netral. Kamu bukan menjadi orang yang dingin, namun hanya sedang bersikap tegas. Jangan kasih mereka reaksi emosionla, dengan begitu mereka akan kehilangan kendali atas diri kamu. Kehadiran kamu itu istimewa, tidak semua orang layak mendapatkannya.

\n4.

>Upgrade kualitas diri: Saat meng-upgrade pola pikir, target, dan kebiasaany, energi palsu tidak akan tahan lama di dekat kamu. Semakin tinggi kualitas kamu, semakin sulit kamu dijangkau oleh hal-hal yang membawa pengaruh negatif.

. . . How to Get Rid of Toxic People Without Having to Say Much: 1.

>Stop explaining yourself: A toxic person gives you an explanation instead of what you give. They will twist things around and look for loopholes in your logic, and provoke you to constantly defend yourself. Silence is the best answer;

\n2.

>Reply with distance: No need for announcements when you leave, just stop showing up in places where you are not appreciated. Limit access, reduce communication, and maintain personal space. Distance is a natural filter; someone who is not right will automatically be excluded;

\n3.

>Respond as necessary: ​​Reply simply, give a long pause, and use a neutral tone. You are not a cold person, but just being firm. Don't give them emotional reactions, that way they will lose control of you. Your presence is special, not everyone deserves it.

\n4.

>Upgrade your self-quality: When you upgrade your mindset, targets and habits, false energy will not last long with you. The higher your quality, the more difficult it is for you to be reached by things that bring negative influence.

#

![Are There Any Reasons Not to Build an Elevator in Your Home (1).jpg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/711e0d2510d3b1ae50138f9080ae1c3d65212a7907f0df534914a0c163b41b0b)

Building a home elevator can improve comfort, accessibility, and luxury, but there are some important reasons homeowners may think twice before installing one. The biggest concern is the overall cost. Home elevators require investment for installation, construction changes, electricity, and regular maintenance. For small families or low-rise homes, this expense may not always feel necessary.

Another reason is limited space. Some houses do not have enough room for an elevator shaft or machine area, which may require major structural modifications. This can increase renovation time and affect the interior layout of the home. In some cases, installation work may create temporary noise and dust, causing inconvenience during construction.

Maintenance is another important factor. Home elevators need routine servicing and safety inspections to ensure smooth and safe operation. If maintenance is ignored, performance issues may occur over time. Power backup systems may also be required during electricity failures.

However, despite these challenges, many homeowners in urban areas still prefer elevators because they add convenience, property value, and modern living benefits.
